title: [HIP] Enable CK fmha LLC head grouping on RDNA (batch mode)
body:
Wire CK's LLC-aware head grouping into `fmha_fwd_ck`, batch mode only.

## Why

aiter launched every q head in one `fmha_fwd` call, so the whole KV working set (821 MB for a 28-head fp8bf16 shape) had to stream from memory every launch. CK's example runner already splits heads into LLC-resident groups — `fmha_fwd_args` even carries `num_head_q_total` / `head_start`, hard-coded to 0 on the aiter side.

## Result

gfx1201 (RDNA3.5), fp8bf16, averaged over 101 iterations (`aiter.test_common.run_perftest`). **Requires #5786 first** — without its `--targets` wiring, gfx12 has no fp8 CK factory to dispatch to and these calls do not build/run at all.

Real workload shapes, packed/varlen (THD) layout. These are group mode (`is_group_mode=true`), which this PR does not touch — head grouping only engages in batch mode, so the numbers below are baseline fp8bf16 throughput for reference, not a grouped-vs-ungrouped comparison:

| shape (T, H, D) | causal | latency | throughput |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[8064, 16, 72]` | false | 5.33 ms | 56.3 TFLOPS |
| `[3582, 64, 128]` | true | 1.56 ms | 135.0 TFLOPS |
| `[3582, 56, 128]` | false | 2.66 ms | 138.6 TFLOPS |

The batch-mode shape this PR targets — grouping engages here, compared against `CK_TILE_FMHA_DISABLE_HEAD_GROUPING=1`:

| shape (B, S, H, D) | causal | grouped | disabled | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `[1, 114660, 28, 128]` | false | 1372.7 ms (137.3 TFLOPS) | 2373.9 ms (79.4 TFLOPS) | 1.73x |

## What changed

Reuse `fmha_fwd_head_grouping.hpp` from the pinned CK (`af9e1d1f`, no CK change, no submodule bump, no new kernel instance): `get_head_group_size()` owns the arch table, LLC probe, threshold, and launch cap; `run_fwd_head_grouped()` owns the per-group pointer math. aiter adds only the runtime-string → type-tag dispatch (`fp16` / `bf16` / `fp8bf16`), since `BiasDataType` and `ODataType` do not follow the input dtype.

- Batch mode only. The two group-mode callers of `aiter::mha_fwd` (`mha_varlen_fwd_kernels.cu`, `asm_mha_varlen_fwd.cu`) are out of scope — this is exactly why the THD shapes above do not speed up.
- gfx9 is unaffected — `get_head_group_size` returns `nullopt` for non-RDNA archs.
- `CK_TILE_FMHA_DISABLE_HEAD_GROUPING=1` restores the old single-launch behavior.

## Verified

Grouped vs `CK_TILE_FMHA_DISABLE_HEAD_GROUPING=1` output is bitwise identical, run as a subprocess pair (CK caches `CK_TILE_FMHA_*` in a function-local static, so toggling the env var mid-process is a no-op). Grouping is **forced** via CK's own `CK_TILE_FMHA_LLC_CACHE_MB` override rather than relying on the host's real LLC size, so the comparison cannot go vacuous on a large-LLC part — confirmed on gfx1201 with CK's `CK_TILE_FMHA_HEAD_GROUP_LOG=1` showing 4 groups engage before asserting bitwise equality.

- gfx1201: 7 bitwise-identical cases passed (fp8bf16 ± causal, fp8bf16 GQA 8:2, fp8bf16 batch=2, bf16, fp16, bf16+LSE).
- The 4 shapes in the Result table above were also spot-checked for NaN/shape/dtype sanity (not a numerical-accuracy comparison against a reference implementation).

## Compatibility

No CK change, no submodule bump, no new kernel instance. `CK_TILE_FMHA_DISABLE_HEAD_GROUPING=1` is an immediate rollback if a regression surfaces on hardware not covered above.

title: [HIP] opt inverse rope group quant gfx1250
body:
## Motivation

Follows #4806. The payload now goes through the gfx1250 tensor engine, the
tier orders apply to row-major, and the op carries one stated policy for
non-finite input. Also fixes an out-of-bounds LDS write, a SIGABRT that
#4806's layout gate introduced, and a dispatch band that was removed by
mistake

## Technical Details

1. Tier sort extended to row-major narrow slices. The orders were restricted
to n32k4, but row-major admits the same sort and it is worth 13-18% once
the slice is narrow. The gain is the narrow quantize path -- a pass whose
groups all miss the rotary tail needs no widening, no cos/sin and no f32 --
which only a uniform segment per wave can select statically. Gated on
TDS == 16: below that a wave spans too few groups to amortize the sort.
2. Payload staged through the tensor engine. Every access order this kernel
uses is a regular 2D tile, tiering included, so the window is
dim0 = run*GROUP_SIZE by dim1 = slots/run and the tier only moves the
origin. Most of the effect is the staged wait: s_wait_tensorcnt<0>
serialises every tile behind the first consumer.
3. WAR stalls removed. s_wait_xcnt was 45% of all stall cycles in the s=16384
ATT trace -- three exec-mask writes landing on a store still in flight:
store_scale's saveexec around a one-byte store whose lanes already agree on
address and value, the cos/sin load's lane-term guard, and a wave-uniform
tdm_wave that divergence analysis could not see through.
4. Four-group heads tier at the exact cut. At GS=128 rope lives only in group
3, so cutting at GROUPS_PER_HEAD/2 filed the pure-nope group 2 under rope
and it paid f32 widening for a rotation it never performs. Held to four
groups per head; the same correction at eight costs 11.7%.

Each scale layout is built only where it can run. mfma_tile feeds CDNA's
V_MFMA_SCALE and n32k4 feeds RDNA's WMMA scaleB, so a third of the module
was kernels the target could never launch.
  gfx1250   372 -> 264 instantiations, 5.31 -> 3.88 MiB device code
  gfx950    372 -> 264 instantiations, 5.31 -> 3.27 MiB device code
  build     26.6 -> 22.3 s
The gate lives entirely in the translation unit; both macros keep an
#ifndef escape hatch for a target that genuinely needs both.


## Test Plan

384 checks pass on gfx1250, HIP graph capture/replay included. gfx942 is
added to SUPPORTED_GFX: its exclusion cited permlane16_swap, which the amax
reduction stopped using, and the op builds and runs there with mfma_tile
included.
Two gaps the sweep could not reach are now covered. Rows whose Ks leaves a
part-wave block, at 9 and 3 heads -- every default shape is a whole number
of waves. And the invalid-group policy, since none of the DATA_DISTS can
produce a non-finite input, which is why that behaviour had moved twice
under optimisation with nothing watching it.

## Test Result

gfx1250, h,g = 128,16, against main. Four interleaved rounds -- both builds
measured inside each round, since absolute timings drift between batches and
only a ratio taken within a round holds up. Median of the per-round ratios:
                          main      branch
  row   GS=128  s=2048   36.18 us   24.89 us   -31.2%
  row   GS=128  s=16384 295.59 us  211.08 us   -28.6%
  row   GS=32   s=2048   35.93 us   27.04 us   -24.7%
  row   GS=128  s=512     7.99 us    6.27 us   -21.3%
  row   GS=32   s=16384 293.00 us  237.78 us   -18.8%
  n32k4 GS=32   s=2048   33.12 us   29.86 us    -9.8%
  n32k4 GS=32   s=16384 261.91 us  238.36 us    -8.9%
The two remaining s=512 points, row/GS=32 and n32k4/GS=32, land around -5%
but spread several points round to round, so they are quoted that way rather
than to a figure.
A wider sweep -- 2 head configs x 3 layout/group-size combinations x 6
values of S -- is uniformly in the same direction with no regression, but it
was collected one build after the other and so carries that batch drift;
treat it as direction rather than magnitude.

## Submission Checklist

- [ ] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests.

title: [FlyDSL] Fused all-reduce + RMSNorm
body:
## Motivation

Current Aiter all-reduce + RMSNorm kernels are not optimal for PCIe interconnects. For tensors of shape [m, 7168], we get on average the following speedup

| Regime | world size 2 | world size 4 | world size 8 |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| Decode | 1.47× (M ≤ 12) | 1.45× (M ≤ 4)  | 1.35× (M ≤ 4) |
| Prefill (M ≥ 1024), FlyDSL uses quantization | 2.38× | 15.1×  | 31.0×  |

## Technical Details

This PR extends the plain `all-reduce` kernel from #5461 with an RMSNorm eplogue. There is per family (1-stage, 2-stage-mesh, and 2-stage-ring) heuristics to select the best instance per family, as well as a policy to select the best FlyDSL family for the message sizes where they are better than then current Aiter kernels. The policy is integrated to the Aiter's communication dispatcher such that when the FlyDSL kernels are enabled via `AITER_FLY_AR=1`, they are tried first. If they are applicable, they'll be used, otherwise the current Aiter fused all-reduce kernel are used.

title: [HIP] [FlyDSL] [JIT] Support Conv3d for Qwen-Image / Wan2.1 VAE on MI35X
body:
## Motivation

aiter has no conv3d (only Triton conv2d). Two diffusion VAEs need one:

- **Wan2.1** encodes in 4-frame chunks and prepends 2 cached feature frames
  after the first chunk. Those frames are real, not causal-pad zeros, so the
  `T=1` `conv3d -> conv2d` identity fails. That is **67.7% of one encode's 650
  convolution calls**.
- **Qwen-Image** is the same VAE fine-tuned at `T=1`, where the identity holds,
  so it needs this kernel's 2-D path.

A GEMM library cannot absorb these shapes: N is the 96/192/384 channel ladder,
and 7 of 18 Qwen-Image shapes have `K` not a multiple of 64 or `N=3`, which
A16W16 cannot express.

## Technical Details

### 1. Vendored implicit-GEMM convolution (`flydsl_conv_implicit`)

Same vendoring as `gemm_a16w16_gfx950`. Dispatches 1D/2D/3D off filter rank;
gathers from the source instead of im2col (~9× less activation traffic).
Keyword surface unchanged (`groups`, `padding_mode`, `splitk`, `stream`,
`tile`, `wgm`, `autotune`, `input_layout`, `output_layout`).

Three mechanical edits vs upstream: local `buffer_atomic_add` (flydsl wheel
has no `kernels/common/`); `kt` -> `k_tile` (filter temporal extent); one
`if` collapsed to `and`. 54/56 top-level definitions byte-identical.

Named `flydsl_conv_implicit` because the entry point dispatches on rank.

### 2. Offline tile tuner

The heuristic N tiles are powers of two. Against 96/192/384, two rungs sit at
**75% N occupancy**; masked B columns still issue MFMA. `TILE_N` 96/192 is
legal but was unreachable: `TILE_{M,N} % (16 * WAVE_M * WAVE_N) == 0` excludes
the eight-wave shape every shipped candidate uses.

- `conv3d_policy.py` enumerates that closed form (reject = arithmetic, not a
  compile), then prunes on N fill, waves, LDS, accumulators.
- `csrc/flydsl_conv3d/conv3d_tune.py` writes per-model CSVs under
  `aiter/configs/model_configs/` (`qwenimage_vae_*`, `wan21_vae_*`).
- `_lookup_tuned_tile` reads them. Miss / missing file / malformed row falls
  back to the unmodified heuristic.

Launch config is five integers, not a `solidx` (reordering candidates must not
silently invalidate the table).

**Tune with `--compare --update_improved`.** `mp_tuner` times across eight GPU
processes; production runs one. A bare sweep regressed three shapes by up to
4.8%. The compare gate re-times on the production path and rejects gains below
`--min_improvement_pct` (default 3%).

Also fixes `autotune=True` / `FLYDSL_CONV3D_AUTOTUNE=1`, which imported a
FlyDSL-repo path and raised `ImportError`.

### 3. A16W16 pruner fix

`GemmConfigPruner` `keep_ratio` climbs with M: at M=27556 it kept only tiles
wasting <0.44% on padding. HTI needs `block_n=256`, so N=384 (pad to 512)
dropped the whole HTI catalog (~30% loss). Cap lets a tile pad up to 30%.

### 4. Tests

`op_tests/test_flydsl_conv_implicit.py`: keyword surface plus Wan / Qwen
shapes from an input resolution (`--wan-res`, `--wan-frames`, `--qwen-res`),
traced on meta-device encodes. Benches:
`op_tests/op_benchmarks/flydsl/qwenimage_vae_conv/bench_three_way.py` (conv vs
A16W16 vs hipBLASLt) and `bench_conv_tuned_ab.py` (tile table on vs off).

## Test Plan

```bash
PYTHONPATH=$PWD python3 op_tests/test_flydsl_conv_implicit.py
python3 -m unittest op_tests.tuning_tests.test_config_shape_collision -v

PYTHONPATH=$PWD python3 csrc/flydsl_conv3d/conv3d_tune.py \
  -i aiter/configs/model_configs/qwenimage_vae_bf16_untuned_conv3d.csv \
  -o aiter/configs/model_configs/qwenimage_vae_bf16_tuned_conv3d.csv \
  --max_configs 32 --mp 8 --compare --update_improved

PYTHONPATH=$PWD python3 op_tests/op_benchmarks/flydsl/qwenimage_vae_conv/bench_three_way.py
PYTHONPATH=$PWD python3 op_tests/op_benchmarks/flydsl/qwenimage_vae_conv/bench_conv_tuned_ab.py
```

All results below: gfx950 / 256 CU, bf16.

## Test Result

### Correctness

`test_flydsl_conv_implicit.py`: **75/75 `checkAllclose`**, `rtol=atol=2e-2`.
`flydsl err` **0 on all 33 model shapes** (the one non-zero cell is torch's
own bf16 rounding at K=27, `err_ratio` 4e-05).

`test_config_shape_collision.py`: 18/18, including `conv3d_bf16_tuned`.

Every tuned row has `err_ratio = 0.0`. Instrumenting `_lookup_tuned_tile`
over the op_test: **1236 hits / 12 distinct shapes**, all non-default tiles
(e.g. `(96, 96, 2, 3)`, `(192, 128, 2, 2)`, `(128, 192, 1, 4) wgm=8`).

### Performance (gfx950 / 256 CU, bf16)

One table for the published buckets. **vs X** is `X_ms / current CSV` (or
`torch / orig flydsl` only where current is missing). Torch and original
flydsl † are the PR-open three-way (NCHW, includes pre-transpose). hip is
`three_way.json` library-best `torch.mm` on materialised `M×K` (no im2col).
Current CSV is NDHWC (`ed7b5a5a8`). ‡ NCDHW-tuned CSV (`05f919868`). Mixed
sessions; hip/a16 traffic is not the conv gather.

| bucket | torch | orig flydsl | hip | current CSV | vs orig flydsl | vs hip | vs torch |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Wan2.1 `T>1`/cached, 480×832, 81f (8 shapes, 440 calls) | 505.32 ms | 310.37 ms † | — | **200.91 ms** | **1.55x** | — | **2.52x** |
| Wan2.1 same 8, 368×544, 81f | — | 128.70 ms ‡ | — | **110.43 ms** | **1.17x** | — | — |
| Qwen-Image, 1024² (10 shapes, 52 calls) | 20.37 ms | 12.00 ms † | 8.70 ms | **7.76 ms** | **1.55x** | **1.12x** | **2.63x** |
| Qwen-Image, 1024² (16 layers, 58 calls) | — | — | 10.02 ms | **8.92 ms** | — | **1.12x** | — |
| Qwen-Image, 1328² (10 shapes, 52 calls) | — | 16.13 ms ‡ | — | **12.68 ms** | **1.27x** | — | — |

title: [ASM] [HIP] [JIT] [Kernel] [gfx1250] Add F8GEMM 256x256 split-K and 128x128 AP0/AP1 kernels
body:
## Motivation

Support the six gfx1250 MXFP8 x MXFP8 (a8w8) cases with both row-major A (AP0) and preshuffled A (AP1). The 256x256 Split-K kernels expose more parallel work for small-M cases; the 128x128 K128/PF8 kernels serve the `(M,N,K)=(512,8192,1536)` indexer case. Split-K support added by this PR is limited to MXFP8 × MXFP8 (a8w8). MXFP8 × MXFP4 (a8w4) remains unchanged and continues to use a single split.

## Technical Details

- Update five existing files: `aiter/ops/gemm_op_a8w8.py`,`aiter/jit/core.py`, `csrc/py_itfs_cu/asm_mxfp8fp4gemm.cu`, the existing kernel CSV, and `op_tests/test_mxfp8fp4gemm.py`. Add the tuned config `aiter/configs/asm_mfxp8fp4gemm.csv` and four code objects: 256x256 cluster 4x2 and 128x128 cluster 4x4, each for AP0/AP1.
- Keep the a8w8 interface in `gemm_op_a8w8.py`. When `splitk` is omitted (`None`), the operator looks up the tuned CSV by gfx, M/N/K, `b_intype`, A layout, and output dtype. The six shapes have separate AP0/AP1 entries (12 rows) supplying `kernelName` and `splitK`. The `b_intype` column uses the HSA registry's `mxfp8`/`mxfp4` values; all 12 shipped rows currently use `mxfp8`. Override the config file through `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_MXFP8FP4`.
- A config miss passes an empty kernel name and defaults to `splitk=1`, using the original native dispatch. An explicit positive `splitk` overrides the configured count. An explicit `kernelName` bypasses the CSV and defaults to one split unless `splitk` is also specified. Split counts are literal counts, not log2 values; `splitk=0` is not an automatic-selection mode.
- Split-K (`splitk > 1`) is supported only by the new 256x256 a8w8 kernels, for both AP0 and AP1. The 128x128 a8w8 kernels support `splitk=1` only. The a8w4 API, dispatch, and single-split behavior remain unchanged. Keep the eight original code objects unchanged.
- Supported split counts allocate BF16 partials; the public API sums them and returns `[M,N]`. A local fake implementation preserves the public output shape for `torch.compile`.
- Preserve the 76-byte launch arguments for original kernels and use 80-byte arguments for the four additions. Validate Split-K counts, partition sizes, output capacity, and 128x128 shape restrictions.
- The existing test entry point reuses the operator's config resolution, with no hardcoded six-shape table in either the test or native dispatch. `--splitk` overrides the configured count; `--no-reduce` measures GEMM only and compares BF16 partials to separate partition references. Shared data initialization and timing files are unchanged. Functional mode covers both AP layouts.

## Test Plan

Both the public API and test driver use the following tuned CSV entries when `splitk` is omitted. A config miss uses native dispatch with `splitk=1`.

| Case | M | N | K | Configured Split-K | Tile |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| wqkv_a | 512 | 2048 | 7168 | 8 | 256x256 |
| wo_b | 512 | 7168 | 16384 | 4 | 256x256 |
| gate_up_proj | 512 | 6144 | 7168 | 4 | 256x256 |
| w2 | 512 | 7168 | 3072 | 4 | 256x256 |
| wq_b | 512 | 65536 | 1536 | 1 | 256x256 |
| indexer_wq_b | 512 | 8192 | 1536 | 1 | 128x128 |

Run on gfx1250 with a fresh JIT directory after the native-code change. Use a fresh TorchInductor cache when validating the updated optional-argument schema with `torch.compile`:

```bash
python -m op_tests.test_mxfp8fp4gemm --mode func --intype a8w8 --apre 0 1 --shape 512,2048,7168 512,7168,16384 512,6144,7168 512,7168,3072 512,65536,1536 512,8192,1536 --no-reduce --data-init constant uniform --scale-init constant auto --seed 0 --warmup 0 --iters 5 --rotate 1

python -m op_tests.test_mxfp8fp4gemm --mode func --intype a8w8 a8w4 --apre 0 1 --shape 32,2048,2048 128,1280,8192 --data-init constant --scale-init constant --seed 0 --warmup 0 --iters 5 --rotate 1
```

## Test Result

Validation of commit `16857b1b2` used gfx1250 and an isolated TorchInductor cache for compile checks.

- 38/38 constant-input, constant-scale GPU cases passed: 12 six-shape partial-output cases, 12 six-shape reduced-output cases, 8 legacy a8w8/a8w4 regression cases, 4 empty-config fallback cases, and 2 explicit `splitk=1` override cases. All groups cover AP0/AP1.
- An empty CSV supplied through `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_MXFP8FP4` sent both `(512,2048,7168)` and `(512,8192,1536)` back to the original 256x256, 4x4 native dispatch with `splitk=1`.
- Verified all 12 config rows against registered kernels, config hits/misses, explicit split-count overrides, and explicit-kernel bypass behavior.
- Verified that `mxfp8` and `mxfp4` entries for the same shape coexist in one CSV and resolve independently. The shipped table has no `mxfp4` tuning rows; an `mxfp4` lookup returns no config.
- FakeTensor passed. Six actual GPU `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` checks passed with `splitk` omitted: AP0/AP1 for `(512,2048,7168)`, `(512,8192,1536)`, and the config-miss shape `(128,1280,8192)`. Default eager outputs matched the constant-input reference; compiled outputs matched eager outputs exactly. Launch capture confirmed selected kernels, resolved split counts, and partial-buffer shapes.
- Black, Ruff 0.16.0, and whitespace checks passed.

Numerical warnings remain unresolved and tolerances are unchanged. Prior uniform/auto testing at commit `775435acd` reported warnings on all 12 six-shape AP0/AP1 partial-output cases; those inputs were not re-evaluated for this CSV revision. Earlier same-input diagnostics showed that BF16 partition rounding accounts for most of the increased error after reduction, with residual differences. Constant-input and partial-output checks do not establish reduced-output accuracy on uniform inputs.

title: [MHA] Add tuned-config dispatch and delta-race tuner for packed varlen
body:
## Motivation

PR #5592 adds a gfx942 split-KV ASM kernel and picks its split count from a rule of thumb compiled into C++.
But it cannot discover that CK, Triton, Gluon, FlyDSL or OPUS would be faster for a given attention shape. 
This PR lets dispatch look up a choice that was actually measured on that GPU, and adds the tuner that produces those measurements.

## What this PR adds

- A tuned-config lookup in `flash_attn_varlen_func` for packed-varlen MHA forward.
- A tuner, `op_tests/tuners/tune_mha_fwd.py`, with `exhaustive`, `race` and `smoke` strategies.
- Two shipped rows: gfx942 / mi325x, hd192, `asm_v3` split 3, for `return_lse` 0 and 1, measured by @amd-yashagar.

## Technical Details

**Lookup**

- Exact key of `(gfx, gpu_model, cu_num)` plus the problem's 30 shape and dtype fields into `aiter/configs/tuned_mha_fwd.csv`, pinning `(backend, num_splits, backend_config)`.
- Anything else falls through to today's C++ auto-select, so untuned shapes behave as on `main`, at about 2.5 us per call.
- A row is a hint, not a correctness contract: if no kernel gate can honor it, dispatch warns and falls back.

**Backends.** All six are arch-gated in `aiter/ops/mha_fwd_policy.py`, and each was driven through the tuner one at a time on gfx950 / MI355X against the shipped shape, with the correctness and arch gates live:

| backend | on gfx950 |
| --- | --- |
| opus, ck, triton, gluon | ran, passed the correctness gate |
| asm_v3 | ran and passed at split 1; splits 2-8 refused by the split-KV policy, which is gfx942 hd192 only |
| flydsl | gfx1250 only, and no gfx1250 hardware was available here |

Five of six run, flydsl is the one we have no hardware to reach, and a rejected or failing candidate never reaches the published table. `ck` is CK at its own default tiling, for the reason under Related PRs. One number is the reason to tune at all: across the gluon tile configs sampled here, latency spans a factor of 28.

**Tuner**

- `MhaFwdTuner` subclasses `TunerCommon`, the same base as the CK and OPUS GEMM tuners, so the untuned-CSV-in / tuned-CSV-out contract and the CLI are the familiar ones.
- Every candidate is correctness-gated before timing, then measured through `mp_tuner`, one fresh process each.
- `exhaustive` (default) times the whole catalogue to full depth. `race` draws from that same catalogue but measures in randomized short blocks, dropping a candidate once it is proven more than delta worse than the leader: 104 s against 315 s on the 200-candidate field, a **3x wall-clock saving**. `smoke` samples each tile grid and says so in its evidence.
- The race core in `aiter/utility/block_race.py` is family-agnostic.

**Incumbency**

- We want to avoid changing the tuning table if not strictly necessary, hence we always want to compare to the currently selected kernel, i.e. the "incumbent".
- A challenger must beat it by a margin: delta (2% by default) under `race`, twice the combined standard error (about 95%) under `exhaustive`, otherwise no (new) row is published.

**Evidence and resuming**

- A race records every finished measurement block in a journal, so `--resume` picks an interrupted run up where it stopped. Resuming is only sound for the same race, so the journal's filename hashes the shape, the candidate list, the race thresholds, etc to distinguish one tuning run from the other.
- A candidate that faults or returns a latency that is not positive and finite leaves the field with a `crash` verdict; it neither takes the run down nor wins on a broken number.
- Measurements stay out of the dispatch table (measurements are noisy and needlessly grow file size of the lookup table). They go to their own CSV, journal and manifest, and the runtime reader rejects any file carrying measurement columns.

**Shared infrastructure**

Three files outside the MHA path changed because this tuner needed them, and they are worth a separate look from their owners:

- `aiter/utility/mp_tuner.py` (@yzhou103): the worker pool now restarts after a fault and collects per-candidate progress for every caller, so a candidate that crashes the worker costs only itself instead of every measurement already finished for that shape.
- `aiter/utility/base_tuner.py` (@yzhou103): shared tuner CLI and CSV plumbing.
- `aiter/jit/file_baton.py` (@Lingpeng-Jin): detects a lock left behind by a zombie process, which a multi-hour tune hits and a short build does not.


## Test Plan

- `python3 -m unittest` over the eight GPU-free modules registered in `.github/workflows/tuning-tests.yaml` at levels 0 and 1: key derivation and lookup, policy and arch gating, race elimination, incumbency and promotion, journal binding and replay.
- `op_tests/tuning_tests/test_mha_store_agreement.py` on gfx950: ASM and Triton resolve the same table to the same launch, and a tuned row genuinely displaces the C++ auto-select rather than coinciding with it.
- `op_tests/test_fmha_gfx942_asm_splitkv.py` on gfx942, including the CSV-override case and the no-CSV fallback.

## Test Result

- 186 tests in 7.3 s, all passing; store agreement passes on a locked MI355X; `ruff check .` and `black` are clean.

## Related PRs

- **#5592**: this PR is stacked on it and targets its branch, and will be retargeted to `main` once #5592 merges. It ships the ASM kernel and the compiled-in split rule that this PR replaces with a measured choice for the keyed shapes.
- **#5024**: complementary. Both tune kernel parameters; what differs is where each backend exposes them.
  - This PR tunes, per exact shape, the backend and that backend's per-call parameters: Triton and Gluon `BLOCK_M`, `BLOCK_N`, warps, waves and stages, each config JIT-compiling its own kernel, plus the asm_v3 split count. The result is a dispatch-table row.
  - CK's tile recipe is fixed when the module is built, so no per-call row can set it. #5024 rebuilds CK per candidate tile and emits a JSON that CK reads at codegen time through `CK_TILE_FMHA_FWD_CUSTOM_TUNE_CONFIG_FILE`, the hook from ROCm/rocm-libraries#11298.
  - They compose: with such a JSON deployed, the `ck` this tuner measures is the tuned CK, competing against the tuned Triton, Gluon and ASM configs.

## Credit

The foundation, namely the problem and plan contracts, the first exhaustive tuner, the dispatch plumbing and the Triton tile path, is @amd-yashagar's: of the 6188 lines added on this branch, 3821 are his.

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#pull-requests.

title: feat(tune): record untuned shapes for every GEMM family, not just bf16
body:
Fixes #5267.

## Why

`AITER_TUNE_GEMM=1` makes `tuned_gemm.py` append every missed bf16 shape to `bf16_untuned_gemm.csv`. That single feature is why tuning a real bf16 deployment is self-service: run the server, collect the CSV, hand it straight back to the tuner.

The fp8 per-token, block-scale and mxfp4 families have no equivalent — they log misses at INFO and write nothing — so their shape lists have to be scraped out of server logs by hand. That is also how shape-key mistakes creep in: we shipped a tuned table that never matched anything because the engine fuses two projections and dispatches `N=2688`, while the tuned rows targeted the unfused `N=2624`. A recorded shape list makes that impossible to miss.

## What

`aiter/utility/untuned_shapes.py` — `record(tuned_file, row)` appends one de-duplicated row **in the schema that family's tuner consumes**. The destination name is derived from the tuned table's own name (`*_tuned_*` → `*_untuned_*`), so a family never has to name its untuned file twice, and a merged `/tmp/aiter_configs` copy still resolves to the right destination.

Wired into the miss paths of:
- `gemm_op_a8w8.get_CKGEMM_config` (block-scale, ± preshuffle) → `M,N,K`
- `gemm_op_a8w8.get_GEMM_config_with_quant_type` (a8w8, a8w8_bpreshuffle) → `M,N,K,q_dtype_w`
- `gemm_op_a4w4.get_GEMM_config` → `M,N,K`

## Behaviour

- Same switch as before (`AITER_TUNE_GEMM=1`) — nothing new to learn; **off by default**.
- `AITER_TUNE_GEMM_DIR` overrides the destination, for read-only package directories and containers (we had to copy the file out of a container image more than once).
- Hot path cost after a shape has been seen is one set lookup; a serving run repeats its shapes, so the append happens a handful of times.
- Never raises. A read-only configs dir or a full disk must not take down inference — it logs a warning and moves on.

## Checked

Name derivation (including the merged-copy path), per-family schemas, de-duplication across repeats, disabled-by-default, and graceful degradation on an unwritable destination.

Same campaign as #5262 / #5263–#5266.

title: [JIT] Make CK fmha kernel generation follow GPU_ARCHS
body:
Make every `01_fmha/generate.py` call site pass `--targets` derived from `GPU_ARCHS`, instead of either omitting `--targets` (CK's silent default `gfx9,gfx950`) or passing a raw device name that CK's factory does not recognize.

## Why

`mha_recipes._ck_targets_flag()` passed the runtime device name (e.g. `gfx1100`) straight through as `--targets`. CK's fmha factory keys are coarser than device names (`gfx11` covers `gfx1100`-`gfx1103`), so any non-gfx9 host got an empty kernel set and `mha_fwd` failed at dispatch with "invalid argument for fmha_fwd". Every other `01_fmha/generate.py` site omitted `--targets` entirely, which defaults to CK's `gfx9,gfx950` regardless of what `GPU_ARCHS` actually asked for.

## What changed

- `map_gpu_archs_to_ck_fmha_targets` / `ck_fmha_targets` / `ck_fmha_factory_key` / `ck_fmha_batch_prefill_gen_targets` (`aiter/jit/utils/build_targets.py`): a small prefix table mirroring CK's `fmha_fwd.get_factory()`, more-specific prefixes first (`gfx950` before `gfx9`, `gfx115` before `gfx11`, `gfx125` before `gfx12`). Unmapped archs (`cpu`, `gfx1030`, ...) keep CK's default `gfx9,gfx950` so a GPU-less `PREBUILD` still emits FMHA modules instead of silently dropping them.
- Wired into every `01_fmha/generate.py` call site: JIT `cmdGenFunc_*`, `optCompilerConfig.json`, `mha_recipes.py`, and the standalone `op_tests/cpp/mha/compile.py`. `batch_prefill` uses a dedicated helper because CK drops *every* batch_prefill kernel if any `--targets` token is not `gfx9*`.
- fp8 has no CK factory on gfx11/gfx115; `mha_batch_prefill` is gfx9-only (its PREBUILD stub is API-only). Both are now rejected with a clear `NotImplementedError` instead of failing deep inside CK dispatch.
- The gate needs the *live* device (`get_gfx_runtime()`) at the public API and at `compile_ops`'s per-call module-name lookup, but the *build-time* `GPU_ARCHS` value (`get_gfx()`) inside `cmdGenFunc` for PREBUILD. Missing this distinction means `GPU_ARCHS=gfx942;gfx1100` (last token wins) would reject a real gfx942 card at runtime. `compile_ops` calls `gen_func` on *every* invocation for its module-name lookup, not only on cache miss, so the lookup path needed the same runtime-vs-build split as the public API, not just `cmdGenFunc` itself.

## Behavior change

`GPU_ARCHS="gfx942"` wheels no longer also contain gfx950 FA kernels (CK's default was always `gfx9,gfx950` regardless of `GPU_ARCHS`). Set `GPU_ARCHS` to every arch the wheel must run on. `docs/installation.rst` is updated accordingly.

## Verified

1. No-GPU unit tests for the mapping table and every gate (`op_tests/test_ck_fmha_targets.py`, `op_tests/test_ck_fmha_targets_wiring.py`): 43 passed.
2. gfx1201 (RDNA3.5): appended FA cases to `op_tests/test_mha.py` (hdim-80 pad-up fp16/bf16, fp8bf16 hdim64, fp8bf16 GQA) — 4 passed, GQA `max_diff=0.05878` against a `< 0.07` bound (per-tensor quant noise on the GQA broadcast, not a gfx12/GQA kernel defect).
3. `ruff check .` (CI-pinned `0.16.0`) and `black --check` clean on every changed file.
4. No CK change, no submodule bump.

gfx942/gfx950 regression is expected to be covered by CI on this PR; the gate logic itself only changes behavior on non-gfx9 archs and unmapped/no-GPU builds.

title: [Triton/Gluon] Merge MoE MXFP8 GEMM into existing _moe_gemm_a8w8 kernel
body:
## Summary

  Follow-up to #5310. Per reviewer request, removes the standalone `_moe_gemm_mxfp8_kernel` and reuses the existing `_moe_gemm_a8w8` kernel for MXFP8 MoE GEMM.

The only difference is the FP8 format: `_moe_gemm_a8w8` uses OCP `float8e4nv` (gfx950) while `moe_gemm_mxfp8` needs AMD fnuz `float8_e4m3fnuz` (gfx942). A new `USE_FNUZ: tl.constexpr` flag handles this: when `True`, it replaces `tl.dot_scaled` (OCP-only) with manual E8M0→fp32 dequant + `tl.dot`.

  ## Changes

  - `_moe_gemm_a8w8`: add `USE_FNUZ=False` constexpr (default preserves current behavior). Relax FP8 dtype assert to accept fnuz when `USE_FNUZ=True`. Fix bias dtype mismatch in SPLIT_K>1 else-branch.
  - `moe_gemm_mxfp8` wrapper: route through `_moe_gemm_a8w8(USE_FNUZ=True)`. Tile params moved out of Python into `configs/gfx942/triton/moe/mxfp8_fnuz/DEFAULT.json`.
  - `moe_utils.py`: add `group_sizes_to_expt_tensors()` to convert the `group_sizes` routing interface to the `ExptHist/ExptOffs/ExptData` format expected by `_moe_gemm_a8w8`.
  - Delete `_triton_kernels/moe/moe_gemm_mxfp8.py` (the duplicate kernel).

title: [HIP] [OPUS] [JIT] Unify gfx950+gfx1250 MXFP4 MQA-logits
body:
## Motivation

gfx950 (#5332) and gfx1250 (#5656) shipped the same operator as two parallel
implementations: two JIT modules, two schedule builders, two Python surfaces and
two op tests. Every fix had to be landed twice, and two of them already diverged
in exactly the same shape of hole (a compile-time stride behind a rank-only
check). This folds them into one module / schedule / API / test, leaving both
device bodies untouched.

## Technical Details

**One JIT module.** `module_pa_mqa_logits_mxfp4_opus` carries both device bodies;
a version macro selects which compiles (`__gfx950__` MFMA 32x32x64 wave64 vs
`__gfx1250__` WMMA 32x16x128 wave32/TDM), and the fat binary is built with
`--offload-arch` per arch, the idiom `opus_gemm` already uses. The two
`_gfx1250_` C++ files are deleted, their contents moved verbatim.

**One schedule.** gfx1250's two-phase `build_tiles` + `build_sched` is now the
only builder; gfx950's per-row builder is retired. gfx950 runs at
`q_per_block == 1`, where a tile is one row and the tile-union window is that
row's, so the shared builder emits exactly the per-row record its MFMA kernel
already reads.

**The tile cut is skipped at `q_per_block == 1`.** There the cut is the identity
-- tile `t` is row `t` -- so the boundary array is the arange the host already
knows. `build_tiles` exists to serve `q_per_block > 1` and is no longer launched
at 1: **one fewer kernel per forward** on every gfx950 call and on gfx1250's
MTP=1 decode instance, and `plan_buffers` stops allocating a buffer nothing
reads. `build_sched` takes `q_per_block` and reads the mapping through
`tile_row()` with a NULL `cu_tiles`.

**One runtime-arch dispatch.** `pa_mqa_logits_mxfp4_fwd_sched` reads
`get_gpu_arch()` and calls the MFMA or WMMA launcher, then dispatches within it
by `(q_per_block, block_k)`. aiter JITs per target GPU, so the arm that launches
always matches the compiled body.

**One Python surface** `aiter/ops/opus/pa_mqa_logits_mxfp4.py`, arch-parameterized
by `MqaLogitsVariant(name, q_per_block, block_k, cta_resident)`. **One op test**
on both arches (`SUPPORTED_GFX = ["gfx1250", "gfx950"]`), building natural
layouts on gfx1250 and MFMA-permuted ones on gfx950.

**`-mllvm -enable-post-misched=1` is load-bearing for gfx950 and must not be
dropped.** aiter's base JIT flags set it to 0; this module turns it back on,
which is the state the tuned standalone uses. The merged module now applies it
to the gfx1250 body as well (its own module did not) -- measured below.

## Test Plan

- Unified op test on both arches: corner cases on every compiled instance, NaN
  E8M0 scale propagation, and the four perf tables.
- Schedule table compared **byte for byte** against the pre-change builder, since
  the kernel consumes only that table.
- Kernel ISA compared against the standalone reference (`tools/fp4_aiter_isa.sh`
  + `tools/cmp_isa_aiter_vs_standalone.py`), to show the device bodies did not
  move.
- `-mllvm -enable-post-misched=1` A/B on gfx1250, since the merged module applies
  it to a body that never had it.

## Test Result

### gfx1250 (ROCm 10.1, clang 23)

| check | result |
|---|---|
| op test, both instances | 28/28 corner cases, NaN E8M0 6/6, `err = 0` on all 50 perf rows |
| schedule table vs built cut | **byte-identical** over 4 reps x 11 shapes (decode 1-2048 seqs, prefill 16384/25000 rows, with `local_starts` and `row_to_batch`) |
| kernel resources | 269 VGPR / occupancy 3 / no spill / LDS 9728 on both instances, unchanged |
| plan-stage launches | `qlen1_kv64` 2 -> 1 (small) and 3 -> 2 (split); `qlen4_kv64` unchanged |
| plan-stage cost | 8.7-9.1 us saved per forward on MTP=1 decode, 12-20 us on prefill |
| kernel time | 6 runs vs 16 pre-change, geomean 0.9982, inside the measured noise |

**post-misched on gfx1250.** The flag is active (`=1` is appended after the base
`=0`, last-wins) and it does change the ISA -- but it is a pure post-RA
reschedule: resources are identical to the digit, and the reordered code has
*fewer* instructions (VOPD packing, fewer `s_delay_alu`/`v_nop`). 16 paired
alternating runs, binary verified per run: **no shape regresses beyond noise, and
7 prefill shapes are 1.0-2.9% faster with the flag on** (13-16/16 sign
consistency, 0.4-3.6% within-arm spread). Decode shows no direction.

### gfx950

gfx950 (#5332) now runs through the unified module / schedule / API. Every call is at
`q_per_block == 1`, where the tile cut is the identity, so the MFMA body is recompiled, not
rewritten. gfx950 runs the `qlen1_kv64` (`block_k = 64`) instance in production; `qlen1_kv256`
is compiled and correctness-checked but not on the production path. Validated on a gfx950 box
(ROCm 7.2.4), module rebuilt fresh.

**Correctness** — op test, both instances (`qlen1_kv64`, `qlen1_kv256`):

| table | rows | err |
|---|---|---|
| corner (13 cases × 2 instances) | 26 | 0 |
| NaN E8M0 propagation | 6 | 0 |

**Kernel and schedule vs. standalone #5332:**

| check | result |
|---|---|
| kernel ISA, both Table kernels (`block_k` 64 / 256) | byte-identical (full text, 223 VGPR / 0 spill, counts, `s_waitcnt`) — `cta_resident`-independent |
| schedule table, identity cut vs. general built cut at equal `cta_resident` | byte-identical, all fields |
| `build_tiles` at `q_per_block == 1` | skipped (identity); `cu_tiles` no longer allocated |
| host row bound `total_q > q.shape[0]` | raises on gfx950 |

The production `qlen1_kv64` keeps #5332's `SCHED_CTA_TARGET = 1024`, so its schedule table is
byte-identical to #5332 across **every** #5332 scenario, verified on hardware:

| scenario | schedule vs. #5332 |
|---|---|
| prefill fresh / causal / chunked | identical (16384 tiles ⇒ one CTA per tile; grid is `cta_resident`-independent) |
| decode (seqs 1 / 8 / 32 / 128) | identical (`cta_resident` 1024 = #5332's, same CTA split) |

(`cta_resident` is a `build_sched` input — it shapes the schedule, not the kernel ISA. `qlen1_kv256`
carries an untuned `512`, but it is off the gfx950 production path, so it does not affect any
number here.)

**Performance** — same-card A/B on `qlen1_kv64` at #5332's chunked shapes (25000 cols, bs 1/2/4),
`run_perftest` 50/10, min-of-25: unified matches standalone #5332 within noise (≤1%, never slower).
This is the expected result and it generalizes to every scenario above: the ISA is byte-identical
and the schedule table is byte-identical, so the timed kernel is the same machine code on the same
table — the unification only drops one `build_tiles` launch per forward.


<!-- Briefly summarize test outcomes. -->

title: [CI] review-pr: fix agent-timeout envelope so large-diff reviews do not spuriously time out
body:
Follow-up to #5666. A real review (#5778, +1544/-339, 14 files) timed out: the GLM worker hit the 1000s agent timeout on every attempt, so no card.

**Two fixes:**
1. **1000s is too short for a large diff** (GLM generation has high thinking-chain variance) -> raise `AITER_AGENT_TIMEOUT` to **2400s (40min)**.
2. **`run_agent` retried a timeout**, which just burns another full window. Now a **timeout (exit 124) is not retried**; only a transient failure (dropped connection / 5xx) is, up to `AITER_REVIEW_RETRIES` attempts.

**Envelope:** timeout path = one 40min attempt per agent (worker + refuter = 80min worst), under the job cap, raised `90 -> 120min`. 40min is a reasoned start; override per-run via the env vars.

title: [ASM] [HIP] feat(fmha_bwd): add bf16 hd=256 fused dKdV+dQ ASM kernels for gfx950
body:
## Summary

Add hand-written ASM backward attention kernels for **bf16 hd=256** on **gfx950 (MI355X)**:

- **Fused dKdV+dQ kernel**: Two-phase single-launch kernel. Phase 1 computes dK/dV (Q-walk with K/V resident in registers). Phase 2 computes dQ (K-walk with Q/dO resident). Writes dQ directly as bf16 — no atomic accumulation, no post-processing needed.
- **ODO preprocessing kernel**: Computes D = dO · O per token using coalesced loads and LDS tree reduction. Layout-agnostic (reads head stride from args).

## Supported contract

- **Layout**: group/varlen THD (mode=1), non-causal (mask=0)
- **Precision**: BF16, hd_qk=256, hd_v=256
- **Workgroup**: 512 threads (8 waves) for dQdKdV, 256 threads for ODO
- **Atomic**: a16 (atomic32=0) — no post-processing needed
- **Causal / a32 / dense BSHD**: not supported; fall through to CK

### Gaps vs sibling ASM kernels

Callers relying on a sibling kernel's coverage will silently fall back to CK for these cases:

- **mode=0 (batch/dense)**: not supported. Siblings have it.
- **mask=1/mask=2 (causal)**: not supported. The fp8bf16 hd256 backward already supports causal; this kernel does not yet.
- **atomic32=1 (a32)**: not supported. Only a16 mode.
- **fp16**: not supported. Only bf16.
- **GQA/MQA**: rejected by gate (`nhead_q == nhead_k`). Caller falls back to CK — no wrong-answer risk.

## Changes

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `hsa/gfx950/fmha_v3_bwd/bwd_hd256_bf16_a16_pssk_group.co` | Fused dQdKdV kernel (512 threads, 8 waves) |
| `hsa/gfx950/fmha_v3_bwd/bwd_hd256_odo_bf16_group.co` | ODO preprocessing kernel (256 threads) |
| `hsa/gfx950/fmha_v3_bwd/fmha_bwd_dqdkdv.csv` | +1 entry: bf16, hd256, noncausal, group, pssk=1 |
| `hsa/gfx950/fmha_v3_bwd/fmha_bwd_odo.csv` | +1 entry: bf16, hd256, group mode |
| `csrc/cpp_itfs/mha_bwd.cu` | bdx=512 for hd>=256 |
| `aiter/ops/mha.py` | Enable gfx950 bwd dispatch for hd256: hdim gate, atomic32=0, causal guard |

## Performance

Tested on MI355X (gfx950) using `bwd.exe` with `AITER_ASM_DIR=<repo>/hsa`:

```
./bwd.exe -prec=bf16 -b=16 -h=18 -d=256 -s=2560 -mask=0 -v3_atomic_fp32=0 -mode=1 -kname=1 -v=0
```

Note: stock `generate_seqlens()` randomizes segment lengths in group mode (total tokens preserved). Numbers below are with randomized segments.

| Configuration | CK (baseline) | ASM (this PR) | Speedup |
|--------------|---------------|---------------|---------|
| b=8, h=18, d=256, s=2560, group | 12.1 ms (200 TFLOPS) | **3.65 ms (662 TFLOPS)** | **3.3x** |
| b=16, h=18, d=256, s=2560, group | 23.6 ms (205 TFLOPS) | **7.15 ms (676 TFLOPS)** | **3.3x** |

## Accuracy

PyTorch path (test_mha_varlen.py): dQ/dK/dV max diff ~0.004 at b=2 s=256. NRMSE ~2e-4 through PyTorch (Section 7 of independent repro confirms).

C++ bwd.exe reports higher NRMSE (~9e-2) for dQ/dK due to BF16 ODO D values in the C++ reference — this is a reference precision issue, not kernel accuracy. BF16 D is intentional (avoids extra F32 workspace).

## Test plan

Python (`test_mha_varlen.py`) on MI355X:

| Config | Result |
|--------|--------|
| b=2 h=8 s=256 (main benchmark) | dQ/dK/dV max diff 0.004, 58 TFLOPS bwd |
| b=2 h=8 s=256 (seq_padding: mixed, q_only, k_only, no_padding) | All pass (causal falls through to CK) |
| b=8 h=18 s=2560 | 597 TFLOPS bwd, correct |
| b=8 h=18 s=5121 (~41K tokens) | dQ/dK/dV max diff < 0.005, no ODO fault |

C++ (`bwd.exe`) on MI355X:

- [x] Simulator: 9/9 varlen tests pass (EqualSegments, UnequalSegments, ManySmallSegments, PaddedSegments, PaddedEqualSegments, DiffQKLengths)
- [x] GPU (MI355X): dQ/dK/dV max diff 0.004 at b=2 s=256
- [x] GPU (MI355X): bwd.exe 676 TFLOPS at b=16 s=2560, no ODO fault
- [x] Independent repro: PyTorch NRMSE ~2e-4, C++ ~632 TFLOPS at b=8 s=2560
- [x] C++ API (`bwd.exe`): b*h*s*d layout with sq != sk now passes (`valid:y`) — fixed dQ head stride in varlen SRD rebase

title: [ASM] [HIP] feat(fmha_fwd): add bf16 hd=256 forward ASM kernel for gfx950
body:
## Summary

- Add group-mode (varlen) BF16 forward attention ASM kernels for head dimension 256 on gfx950 (MI355X/MI350X)
- **Non-causal**: 14% faster than CK — 497 TFLOPS vs 436 TFLOPS (b=8, s=5121, 18 heads)
- **Causal**: 17% faster than CK — 509 TFLOPS vs 436 TFLOPS (same config)
- Supports variable-length sequences with physical/logical padding (ptr_qseq_padding/ptr_kseq_padding)
- Handles seqlen_q != seqlen_k per segment (cross-attention / ragged batches)
- Adds NRMS and mean diff reporting to test_mha_varlen.py for more meaningful accuracy metrics

## Supported contract

- **Layout**: group/varlen THD (mode=1), causal (mask=2) and non-causal (mask=0)
- **Precision**: BF16, hd_qk=256, hd_v=256
- **Workgroup**: 256 threads (4 waves), bdx=256
- **Heads**: MHA only (nhead_q == nhead_k); GQA/MQA falls back to CK
- **Input**: contiguous packed THD tensors (non-contiguous falls back to CK)
- **Not supported** (fall back to CK): GQA/MQA, dense BSHD, a32, dropout, alibi, bias, sink, logits_soft_cap, non-contiguous Q

### Gaps vs sibling ASM kernels

Callers relying on a sibling kernel's coverage will silently fall back to CK for these cases:

- **mode=0 (batch/dense)**: not supported. Every sibling (including fp8bf16 hd256) has it. Planned for a follow-up.
- **GQA/MQA**: rejected by gate (`nhead_q == nhead_k`). Caller falls back to CK — no wrong-answer risk.

## Accuracy note

BF16 hd256 uses BM=128 (Q-tile size), resulting in more online softmax rescaling steps than hd128/FP8 kernels (BM=256). At long sequences (s>1024), max element-wise diff can reach ~0.016 vs CK reference, but NRMS remains excellent (~4e-5). The stock test_mha_varlen.py tolerance (max(4x pytorch_noise, 0.01)) passes at all tested configs.

For causal with sq > sk (bottom-right alignment), Q rows that see no K columns output O=0 and LSE=-inf, matching the expected convention for fully-masked rows.

## Changes

- **hsa/gfx950/fmha_v3_fwd/fwd_hd256_bf16_group.co** — non-causal kernel binary (4 waves, bdx=256)
- **hsa/gfx950/fmha_v3_fwd/fwd_hd256_bf16_causal_group.co** — causal kernel binary with K-loop trim and NaN-safe epilogue
- **hsa/gfx950/fmha_v3_fwd/fmha_fwd.csv** — add bf16 hd256 entries for non-causal and causal
- **csrc/cpp_itfs/mha_fwd.cu** — bdx=256 for gfx950 bf16 hd256 group mode; tg_div=1 (no tile merging)
- **aiter/ops/mha.py** — enable bf16 hd256 varlen dispatch on gfx950, gated on nhead_q==nhead_k, q.is_contiguous(), no sink
- **op_tests/test_mha_varlen.py** — report NRMS and mean diff alongside max diff

## Performance (MI350X, b=8, nh=18, s=5121, hd=256, bf16)

| | ASM fwd (TFLOPS) | CK fwd (TFLOPS) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| Non-causal | 497 | 436 | 1.14x |
| Causal | 509 | 436 | 1.17x |

## Test plan

- [x] Simulator: 36/36 bf16 hd256 varlen tests pass (EqualSegments, UnequalSegments, RaggedTail, ManySmallSegments, SingleLargeSegment, DiffQKLengths — x3 configs x2 kernels)
- [x] GPU (MI350X): test_mha_varlen.py causal b=8 nh=18 s=5121 — forward max diff 0.015625, NRMS 3.9e-05
- [x] GPU (MI350X): test_mha_varlen.py non-causal b=8 nh=18 s=5121 — forward max diff 0.001, NRMS 3.0e-04
- [x] GPU: All 4 padding scenarios pass (mixed, q_only, k_only, no_padding) for both causal and non-causal
- [x] GPU: Backward pass (CK) produces finite gradients with ASM forward output (dQ/dK/dV within 0.03125)
- [x] GPU: repro_5403.py sections A-F pass (sq==sk, sq!=sk, causal, ragged, GQA->CK fallback)
- [x] GQA/MQA correctly falls back to CK via nhead_q==nhead_k gate
- [x] Non-contiguous Q correctly falls back to CK via q.is_contiguous() gate
- [x] Declared-unsupported paths (dropout, alibi, bias, swa, sink, logits_soft_cap, fp16, dense BSHD) fall back correctly
- [x] No regressions on hd64/96/128/192, fp8, or existing gfx942/gfx950 paths
- [x] C++ API (`fwd.exe`): b*h*s*d layout with sq != sk now passes (`valid:y`) — fixed K/V head stride in varlen SRD rebase

title: Fuse fp8 mqa logits clean
body:
## Summary

Fuse `clean_logits=True` output clearing into the existing gfx950 Gluon FP8 MQA logits kernel. Each workgroup fills its query rows' invalid windows with `-inf`, removing the separate full-output initialization. For the measured `clean_logits=True` prefill cases, latency is reduced by 5.42%–11.98% against the same launch configurations without fusion.

This PR is stacked on [PR #5621](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5621). The [incremental diff](https://github.com/qilihuan/aiter/compare/tune-fp8-mqa-logits-sweep...fuse-fp8-mqa-logits-clean) contains only the clearing fusion and its tests; the gfx950 dispatch buckets from PR #5621 are unchanged.

## Motivation

With `clean_logits=True`, the wrapper initializes the entire output to `-inf` before the compute kernel overwrites valid scores. Filling only the invalid windows inside the compute kernel removes that extra launch and the initial writes to valid positions.

## Changes

- Allocate an uninitialized output for all `clean_logits=True` calls on the gfx950 Gluon path, and pass a compile-time `FUSE_CLEAN_LOGITS` flag to the existing kernel. Fusion is not restricted to the shapes in the performance table.
- Fill the prefix and suffix outside each row's valid window in the same workgroup that computes its scores. Preserve the compute pipeline, grid, and launch settings; include the fusion flag in the kernel's trace representation.
- Keep `clean_logits=False` on the original compute path, with fusion disabled. Other architectures and the non-Gluon fallback retain their existing output initialization.
- Extend `op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_fp8_mqa_logits.py` to check all invalid positions are `-inf` and all valid scores match the reference, including full, empty, unaligned, and different adjacent-row windows.

## Performance

These are **local measurements on Triton 3.7 / gfx950, not CI results**. Clocks were not locked. The measurement inputs and `aiter.test_common.run_perftest` follow ROCm/aiter PR [#5434](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5434), `op_tests/test_mqa_logits.py`. That script and the local comparison driver are not part of this PR; no sweep scripts or CSV files are submitted.

Fusion applies to all gfx950 Gluon calls with `clean_logits=True`; the table covers only the measured shapes below.

Fixed `M=4096, H=32, D=128`, with FP8 E4M3FN Q/KV, FP32 KV scales and weights, and row i's valid window `[0,N-M+i+1)`. Both public wrappers use the same inputs and the `(BM,BKV,W,C)` settings selected in PR #5621, where the tuple denotes `BLOCK_M/BLOCK_KV/waves_per_eu/NUM_CHAINS`. Launch parameters were compared directly; fusion is the only additional kernel option.

Each measurement uses 2 warmups and 101 calls, summing GPU profiler kernel durations per invocation and discarding the first iteration and IQR outliers. Results are medians from four independent processes, alternating baseline/fusion call order. Input generation, quantization, and reference computation are excluded. Both True timings include the work needed to provide `-inf` outside the valid windows; False excludes downstream masking.

| N | clean_logits | Shared (BM,BKV,W,C) | #5621 without fusion (μs) | This PR (μs) | Latency reduction | This PR TFLOPS | This PR TB/s |
| ---: | :---: | :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4096 | True | (2,64,2,1) | 65.413 | 61.867 | 5.42% | 1111.033 | 1.373124 |
| 16384 | True | (2,64,2,1) | 328.498 | 294.142 | 10.46% | 1635.443 | 0.978776 |
| 65664 | True | (2,128,2,2) | 1439.938 | 1267.444 | 11.98% | 1684.189 | 0.870970 |
| 131072 | True | (2,128,2,2) | 2882.285 | 2551.011 | 11.49% | 1697.109 | 0.855381 |
| 4096 | False | (2,64,3,2) | 55.086 | 55.756 | -1.22% | 1232.802 | 0.921958 |
| 16384 | False | (2,64,2,2) | 303.271 | 302.156 | 0.37% | 1592.070 | 0.841796 |
| 65664 | False | (2,128,2,4) | 1220.794 | 1223.063 | -0.19% | 1745.303 | 0.873432 |
| 131072 | False | (2,128,2,4) | 2458.445 | 2459.531 | -0.04% | 1760.231 | 0.873557 |

False rows are controls with fusion disabled in both versions. The changes in those timings do not represent a fusion benefit. True and False use different configurations selected in PR #5621, so their timing difference alone does not isolate clearing cost. Performance outside these shapes and causal windows has not been characterized.

For valid pair count V and latency t in μs, TFLOPS is `2×H×D×V/(t×10^6)`. TB/s estimates Q/KV/scales/weights bytes plus output bytes, divided by `t×10^6`; output bytes are `4×M×N_padded` for True and `4×V` for False. This is an effective byte estimate, not a hardware bandwidth counter or measured peak-bandwidth utilization.

## Testing

- [x] Extended the existing unit test module with full-output checks for varied windows, the four measured KV lengths, an unaligned short shape, and an odd query-row count. Tests call the public wrapper without tuning overrides.
- [x] Ran the existing and added tests on gfx950. Valid scores are compared against an FP32 reference from the quantized inputs with TF32 disabled and `rtol=atol=0.01`; every invalid element is checked for `-inf`.
- [x] Performance comparison: see above (local gfx950 measurements).
- [ ] Tested on MI250X — not tested.
- [ ] Tested on MI300X — not tested.

From the patched repository root in the ROCm environment:

```bash
export AITER_TRITON_ONLY=1
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD"
python -m pytest -q op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_fp8_mqa_logits.py
```

## Documentation

- [x] Clarified the returned logits' window semantics in the wrapper docstring.
- [ ] User guide updated — not needed; the public API is unchanged.
- [ ] Performance guide updated — measurement method and results are documented here.

## Dependencies

- [x] No new third-party dependencies added.

Depends on [PR #5621](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5621) for the selected dispatch configurations used in the comparison. Merge PR #5621 first, then rebase this branch so the upstream diff contains only the fusion commit. The #5434 test script is a measurement source, not a runtime dependency.

## Breaking Changes

None. Valid-score arithmetic and the public API are unchanged. With `clean_logits=True`, positions outside each row's window remain `-inf`; with False, those positions remain unspecified.

On gfx950 Gluon, True changes output allocation from `full(-inf)` to `empty`; the kernel fills the invalid regions with `-inf` to preserve these semantics.

title: [ASM] [HIP] [JIT] [gfx942] Optimize long-context FMHA with split-KV
body:
## Motivation

Kimi-K3 packed-varlen prefill (BF16, D_QK=192, D_V=128, H=12, Sq=4096, Sk~8K–128K) is long-K bound on the current gfx942 ASM kernel. vLLM already calls `aiter.flash_attn_varlen_func`. This PR should speed that path up without changing the public API.

## Technical Details

- New ASM kernel `fmha_fwd_hd192x128_bf16_rtna_group_splitkv` (splits 2–8) plus a HIP LSE combine.
- Public `fmha_v3_varlen_fwd` now auto-selects split-KV. `num_splits=0` means auto, `1` keeps the unsplit kernel, `2–8` force that split.
- Auto uses split-3 when the kernel contract matches, KV tiles ≥ 256 (Sk ≥ 8192), and `Q_tiles * heads ≤ 2 * CU`. Other cases stay unsplit.
- `_fmha_v3_varlen_splitkv_fwd` is an internal op for tests and later tuning. `mha.py` only registers it. No extra env vars and no public signature change.

## Test Plan

- `op_tests/test_fmha_gfx942_asm_splitkv.py` on MI325X
- `op_tests/op_benchmarks/bench_fmha_gfx942_asm_splitkv.py --sq 4096 --sk 42700 --heads 12 --splits 3`

## Test Result

26/26 tests passed (splits 2–8, tails, LSE, public auto-select, `out=`, CUDA graph, `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)`).

Relevant target shape Sq=4096 Sk=42700 H=12 on MI325X:
- unsplit ASM 3.065 ms
- split-3 2.269 ms (26% faster)
- cosine difference 5.087e-6
- combine is ~0.020 ms

title: [Config] Revert 13 regressed Kimi-K3 A8W8 rows
body:
## Summary

- restore 13 Kimi-K3 A8W8 rows from #5690 to their previous CK/CKTile kernels
- keep the other 5 initially-questionable FlyDSL rows after higher-iteration ABBA repeats confirmed >=2% production speedup
- change config only; no kernel implementation is reverted

## Why

The first post-tune verification loaded CK/CKTile production modules built before the model config, so missing lookup entries fell back to heuristic kernels. After forcing `AITER_REBUILD=1`, the extreme reported gains disappeared (for example, `M=2176,N=576,K=7168` returned from ~213 us to ~24 us baseline latency).

## Verification method

- one fixed MI355X/gfx950 GPU (`HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`)
- rebuilt CK and CKTile production lookup from the main config
- baseline and candidate run sequentially on the same GPU
- initial run plus reverse-order repeat: 10/20 warmups, 101/201 timed iterations
- six unstable rows received two additional ABBA passes with 30 warmups and 301 timed iterations
- acceptance rule: `baseline_us / candidate_us >= 1.02`

## Result

- 12 rows consistently regressed
- `M=1216,N=576,K=7168` improved only 0.19%, below the 2% threshold
- 5 rows were retained after four-run ABBA medians confirmed 3.6%–18.1% speedup
- worst reverted rows:
  - `M=1472,N=1536,K=7168`: candidate `0.612x` baseline
  - `M=2112,N=576,K=7168`: candidate `0.875x` baseline

## Validation

- final config was rebuilt into the production CK/CKTile modules
- all 18 disputed shapes passed production numerical checks (`atol=0.01`, `rtol=0.01`)
- config contains 1039 unique positive-timing rows
- `git diff --check` passes

Related: #5690

title: [FlyDSL] Add gfx950 FHMoE producer on gemm_moe_tune.py
body:
## Summary

gfx950 fused heterogeneous MoE (FHMoE, DSV4 I384) already serves through `fused_moe` + `aiter/configs/tuned_fhmoe.csv`. What was missing is a **producer**: a tuner that sweeps FlyDSL stage1×stage2 pairs, rejects fast-wrong kernels against torch, and writes a native tuned CSV (`block_m`, `kernelName1`, `kernelName2`, `us`).

This PR adds that producer as `FhmoeTuner` on the existing FMoE script (`gemm_moe_tune.py --fhmoe`), wires it into `op_tune.sh` and Tuning Tests like the other families, and **does not** replace the shipped 12-row `tuned_fhmoe.csv`.

FHMoE is its own family, not a flag on FMoE tests: different CLI (`--fhmoe`), different CSVs (`untuned_fhmoe.csv` / `tuned_fhmoe.csv` / `AITER_CONFIG_FHMOE`), gfx950-only, shared-expert + routed FP4 + shared FP8. Serving `fused_moe` / `aiter/fhmoe.py` are not in the diff.

## Tuner (`FhmoeTuner`)

Subclass of `FmoeTuner`, selected with `--fhmoe` (mutually exclusive with `--grouped-gemm` and `--mxfp4-flydsl` on the same `__main__`).

**Catalogue.** `aiter/configs/untuned_fhmoe.csv`: 12 DSV4 I384 rows, tokens 1,2,4,…,2048. Same shape keys as shipped `tuned_fhmoe.csv` (that file has no `us` column; the producer adds `us`).

**Arch gate.** `aiter/fhmoe.py` is `NotImplementedError` off gfx950. `gemm_moe_tune.py` multiplexes four tuners in one file, so the gate is in `__main__`: `--fhmoe` on a non-gfx950 process `SystemExit`s (`--fhmoe is only supported on gfx950`). Grouped GEMM already does the same for gfx1250. This is **not** A6W6’s `RuntimeError` inside `tune()`: A6W6 is its own script, so a unittest subprocess can still import and skip; here the process dies before `FhmoeTuner` runs. Changing FHMoE to `RuntimeError` would not remove the need to skip `--fhmoe` subprocesses in Tuning Tests, and it would be inconsistent with `--grouped-gemm`. The skip belongs in the tests (and in `op_tune.sh`), not by weakening `__main__`.

**How a candidate is timed.** Public `fused_moe()` cannot inject a one-row candidate. `supports_dsv4_i384_fhmoe` requires every padded-M tier in the config file (e.g. `fused_moe(M=16)` needs tuned rows for 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16). The worker therefore times `_fused_moe_impl` with a temporary one-row CSV (`kernelName1` / `kernelName2` / `block_m`). That is kernel-pair search, not the serving lookup.

**Published token is the serving lookup key.** Serving `get_2stage_cfgs` looks up `get_padded_M(token_num)`, not the raw catalogue token (`fused_moe.py`; for M < 32768 that is `nextPow2`, so 3072 → 4096). Candidate timing already wrote that padded key in `_write_candidate_csv`. `post_process` used to emit the catalogue token, so a non-power-of-two untuned row would be timed at the padded tier and published under a key serving never reads: the gap-fill job can exit 0, the CSV grows a dead row, and the shape stays uncovered. The producer now publishes `get_padded_M(X)` through `_lookup_token`, the same helper timing uses. Save the padded token only — not `X`, not both — because serving has a single `token` column.

The 12 shipped catalogue rows are already 1,2,4,…,2048; `pad(X) = X` for them and this does not change `tuned_fhmoe.csv`.

Local check on gfx950, two-pair smoke regex (not the cartesian), `--mp 1`, ~66s: catalogue token=3 → `/tmp/tuned_fhmoe_token3.csv` has `token=4`, `us=47.3686`, cosine OK (0 failed). `BaseTuner.tune_summary` still row-matches the `-i` frame (token=3) against success (token=4), so it prints leftover “untuned” and `[Tuning not Finished]` / exit 1. That is a key mismatch in the shared summary, not a failed kernel. We do **not** pad the catalogue on read and we do **not** rewrite `BaseTuner`’s message (every family uses it). Serving lookup is the contract this producer has to match; the 12-row gap-fill job never hits the mismatch.

**Search.** For each catalogue row, `_kernel_pairs` builds the legal FlyDSL cartesian (`block_m` ∈ {16,32,64,128} × stage1 names × stage2 names, after tile/LDS/`inter_dim` filters). DSV4 I384 INTERLEAVE is on the order of **5632 pairs per token**. Winner = min `us` among pairs with cosine vs torch ≤ `errRatio`. `post_process` drops the whole shape if every pair fails. Fast-wrong pairs must not win on latency.

**Data.** `generate_fhmoe_data` builds routed MXFP4 + shared FP8 tensors on the **host** (FMoE’s `generate_data` stays on CUDA). Dummy expert pad, `gate_mode` preshuffle. Weights are ~6 GiB per shape and **token-independent**. `run_config` regenerates per row sequentially and `empty_cache`s; this is not a 12×6 GiB peak. Left as-is; not a `test_run_config` bug.

**mp_tuner.** Same worker pool as FMoE. `shape_grouped=True` puts every pair of one shape in **one** task group. Default `--timeout` is 1800s **per group**. A full cartesian for one token is hours, so a real producer run needs `--timeout` on the order of a day (see Perf). Pipeline smoke is two pairs and stays under 1800s.

**`--run_config`.** Overrides the parent FMoE path. Iterates the tuned CSV, calls public `fused_moe` with shared-expert args, cosine vs torch, reports `e2e_us`. `--run_config <csv>` sets `AITER_CONFIG_FHMOE` to that file (same env serving uses) and clears FHMoE caches. Tuner `us` and `e2e_us` are different clocks (search vs production); do not compare them.

**`op_tests/test_fhmoe.py`.** `__main__` now runs `pytest.main`. `python3 op_tests/test_fhmoe.py` used to exit 0 without collecting tests. That file is the op oracle, not the tuner.

## op_tune.sh / Operators Tuning

Job, same gap-fill shape as FMoE:
```python3 csrc/ck_gemm_moe_2stages_codegen/gemm_moe_tune.py --fhmoe
-i aiter/configs/untuned_fhmoe.csv -o aiter/configs/tuned_fhmoe.csv
```

**No `--all`.** Without `--all`, `FmoeTuner.pre_process` drops keys already present in `-o` (“only kernels that are not in the tuned CSV”). The 12 catalogue rows **already match** shipped `tuned_fhmoe.csv`, so on gfx950 this job is a **no-op** until someone adds a new untuned shape. `--all` would retune those keys in CI and could overwrite production defaults. This PR is the producer, not a retune of shipped rows.

Operators Tuning’s runner is `linux-aiter-oci-mi300x-1` (**gfx942**). The script walks the **full** `tune_jobs` list, so `--fhmoe` would `SystemExit` and fail the workflow. The fhmoe job **skips** unless `get_gfx() == gfx950`. `get_gfx()` follows `GPU_ARCHS` (same helper as the rest of this script and aiter tests). Live `rocminfo` / `get_gfx_runtime()` is the other clock; we did not switch `op_tune.sh` to it.

## Tuning Tests (family tables, not a one-off yaml)

`tuning-tests.yaml` is unchanged: `test_csv_validation`, `test_tune_pipeline`, `test_run_config`. `GPU_ARCHS=gfx950`, runner `linux-aiter-mi35x-1`. Triggers are **schedule + `workflow_dispatch` only** — not `pull_request`. Opening this PR does not launch that workflow.

Grouped GEMM is **not** a Tuning Tests family (gfx1250; this workflow is gfx950). FHMoE **is** a family, with an explicit gfx950 skip so `--fhmoe` `SystemExit` is not a FAIL if `GPU_ARCHS` is wrong.

### `test_csv_validation.py`

- `TUNED_CSVS` includes `tuned_fhmoe.csv`.
- `test_fhmoe_no_duplicates` uses FHMoE extra keys (`act_type`, dtypes, `shared_expert_id`, pads, `gate_mode`, …), not GEMM `M,N,K`.
- Untuned catalogue file must exist.

### `test_tune_pipeline.py`

- Smoke only: `TUNE_MOE_KERNEL_REGEX` pins **two** kn1×kn2 pairs, not the cartesian (`timeout_mp1` 1200s). Measured ~72s on gfx950.
- **`test_fhmoe_mp1` only** — no `mp_default`. One GPU is enough to prove the tuner writes a CSV; all-GPU cartesian smoke is not the family pattern we need.
- Skip is an `if not _is_gfx950(): skipTest` inside `test_fhmoe_mp1`, not a `required_gfx` dict key. Pipeline methods are one-per-family; there is no loop over `TUNER_FAMILIES` that would miss a dict field. `_is_gfx950()` uses `get_gfx()` (honors `GPU_ARCHS`), same as CI.

### `test_run_config.py`

- Family `fhmoe`: `extra_args=["--fhmoe"]`, `config_property=AITER_CONFIG_FHMOE_FILE`, `required_gfx=gfx950`, `timeout=1800`.
- **Why `required_gfx` lives on the dict:** `TestRunConfig` loops every family, and `TestRunConfigCustom` (`TUNE_TEST_FAMILY=fhmoe`) must skip too. A skip only inside `test_fhmoe` would still blow up Custom on gfx942. Helper `_skip_unless_required_gfx` is called from both. Other families do not `SystemExit` in `__main__` on a Tuning Tests gfx950 box, so they do not need this key.
- **Why 1800s:** 600s died after token=512 cosine OK. 12 shipped rows finished in **690.9s**, all OK. Weights ~6 GiB/row sequential, plus a distinct FlyDSL pair JIT per token.
- `run_config` here is correctness + e2e of the **shipped** CSV, not a producer search.

### `test_fhmoe_replay.py` (in tree, **not** on the yaml)

Producer → serving in a **fresh** interpreter: tuner times `_fused_moe_impl`; this checks that public `fused_moe(...)` with shared-expert args reads only `AITER_CONFIG_FHMOE`. Empty DSV4 CSV must raise; a CSV `FhmoeTuner` actually wrote must be the kn1/kn2 that launch. A planted row is not the contract. M=16 needs the padded-M ladder in the file; the test tunes 1,2,4,8,16 and replays 1 and 16.

Other families do not put a sibling replay on `tuning-tests.yaml`. Listing it there was considered and dropped so FHMoE matches fmoe/a8w8 CI surface. Run it locally if you want the serving lookup proof.


## What this PR does not do (on purpose)

- Does not change serving `fused_moe` / `fhmoe.py`.
- Does not commit a new `tuned_fhmoe.csv`. A producer that beats **one** shipped token is evidence, not a default swap.
- Does not pass `--all` on Operators Tuning (would overwrite shipped keys).
- Does not run the FlyDSL cartesian in CI (token=1 alone is 5632 pairs; default 1800s watchdog would kill the grouped task).
- Does not add replay / extra tests to `tuning-tests.yaml`.
- Does not switch `op_tune.sh` from `get_gfx()` to `rocminfo`.
- Does not unify pipeline’s `_is_gfx950()` with run_config’s `required_gfx` helper. Different dispatch (named method vs family loop + Custom). Both honor `get_gfx()` / `GPU_ARCHS`.
- Does not pad catalogue tokens on read, and does not change `BaseTuner.tune_summary`. A non-power-of-two `-i` row still trips `[Tuning not Finished]` after a successful padded write (token=3 check above). The shipped 1…2048 catalogue does not.

## Perf evidence (token=1 only — not a CSV update)

Quiet gfx950, `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` on an idle GPU (device 4; device 1 was 98% and unused). `TUNE_MOE_KERNEL_REGEX` **unset**. `--timeout 86400` because 5632 pairs are one `mp_tuner` group. Tune ~1.5 h, then `--run_config` shipped vs tuner CSV, **same** public `fused_moe`, warmup=2, iters=5.

Producer wrote `/tmp/tuned_from_producer.csv` (1 row, `us>0`, 0 failed). Cosine OK on both clocks.

| | CSV | kn1 | kn2 | e2e_us | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before | shipped `tuned_fhmoe.csv` token=1 | `…_t32x64x256_w4_gui_kw4_fp8` | `…_t32x256x128_atomic` | 39.58 | OK |
| After | tuner-written CSV | same kn1 | `…_t32x128x128_atomic_persist` | 37.83 | OK |

Same kn1, **different kn2**: real cartesian, not the two-pair smoke regex. After is not slower (~4%). One token, 2/5 iters; not a reason to replace the 12-row shipped file in this PR. Tuner `us=38.86` on after is a different clock (101 iters in `run_perftest`); compare e2e to e2e only.

## Files

- `csrc/ck_gemm_moe_2stages_codegen/gemm_moe_tune.py` — `FhmoeTuner`, `--fhmoe`, cosine, `run_config`, `_lookup_token` (publish `get_padded_M`)
- `aiter/configs/untuned_fhmoe.csv` — DSV4 I384 catalogue
- `.github/scripts/op_tune.sh` — fhmoe job + gfx950 skip
- `op_tests/tuning_tests/test_{csv_validation,tune_pipeline,run_config}.py` + README
- `op_tests/tuning_tests/test_fhmoe_replay.py` — local producer replay
- `op_tests/test_fhmoe.py` — pytest `__main__`

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m unittest op_tests.tuning_tests.test_csv_validation -v`
- [x] `python3 -m unittest op_tests.tuning_tests.test_tune_pipeline.TestTunePipeline.test_fhmoe_mp1 -v` (gfx950, ~72s, 2 pairs)
- [x] `python3 -m unittest op_tests.tuning_tests.test_run_config.TestRunConfig.test_fhmoe -v` (gfx950, 12 shipped rows, 690.9s, all OK)
- [x] Producer token=1 cartesian (`candidates=5632`) + `--run_config` shipped vs tuner CSV (table above)
- [x] Catalogue token=3 → tuned CSV `token=4` (`pad` publish), two-pair smoke, gfx950, 66s, `us=47.3686`. Summary leftover 3 vs 4 / exit 1 is the unpadded `-i` key, not a cosine fail.
- [ ] `tuning-tests.yaml` GitHub workflow: not a PR check. Equivalent fhmoe tests already ran on gfx950. Full-suite dispatch (`test_tune_pipeline` / `test_run_config` for every family) is optional and not required to land the producer.

title: [HIP] [OPUS] [FlyDSL] FlyDSL gemm_decode: small-M dense GEMM kernels (BF16)
body:
## Motivation

LLM autoregressive decode runs linear projections at M=1..5 tokens per step. A standard 16×16 MFMA tile wastes ≥75% of compute slots at these sizes. This PR adds a FlyDSL BF16 decode GEMM optimised for small M, plus the tuned config rows for the shapes where it wins.

Target hardware: gfx942 and gfx950. Measured on MI325X (gfx942, 304 CU) and MI355X (gfx950, 256 CU).
Target shapes: Kimi-K3 TP8 decode GEMMs, N=896…40960, K=128…8448. Generic — no model-specific names in kernel or dispatch code.

## Technical Details

Two complementary FlyDSL policies, selected by a runtime tuner:

**Wave** (`gemm_decode_wave.py`) — warp-per-scalar output-centric GEMM. One wavefront owns one tile of (M×N) output scalars; K split across 64 lanes, reduced by butterfly XOR. `v_dot2_f32_bf16` on gfx950, scalar/packed FP32 on gfx942. Wins at M=1,2.

**BlockMFMA** (`gemm_decode_block_mfma.py`) — MFMA block policy with LDS A-staging and software prefetch. Wins at M≥3.

**Entry point** (`gemm_kernels.py`): `gemm_decode_bf16(A, B, C, config)`, dispatching to either policy via a tuned config from `iter_gemm_decode_configs`. The kernel exists only for M≤5; the dispatcher honours a `flydsl_decode` row on exact M match only, never through M padding.

**Tuned configs** — `flydsl_decode` rows in `kimik3_bf16_tuned_gemm.csv` for gfx950 and gfx942, M=1..5, covering the Kimi-K3 TP8 decode shapes. Most land where the dispatcher previously fell through to `torch`. On gfx950 the rest replace an existing `flydsl` or `triton` row, and each of those only where graph replay showed decode beats the incumbent for that exact shape and M. On gfx942 nothing is replaced — see below.

**Duplicate shapes across model configs.** A few keys at `(2112,7168)` also existed in `dsv3_` and `kimik2_bf16_tuned_gemm.csv`, and `(3584,7168)` arrived in main via #5702 while this PR was open. Since the runtime merges every `*bf16_tuned_gemm*` file into one keyspace, duplicates raise at merge time. All were resolved by the repository's own guard — `test_config_shape_collision.py --fix`, lowest-`us` wins — not by hand. That accounts for the deletions in the two other model files.

**Two fixes needed along the way.** The AOT path applied the bias placeholder substitution twice, failing every bias-free row. The tuner's candidate selection discarded valid decode configs before benchmarking them.

## Performance

Measured against the kernel the config named for the same shape before this PR — the existing row, or `torch` where none existed. Both kernels invoked by name, dispatcher out of the loop.

Packed HIP graph, wall clock over launches, four rotating weights, alternating A/B/B/A pairs scored per pair, incumbent timed against itself as a null control (2% threshold). Both sides checked against an FP32 reference before each timing.

gfx950 (MI355X, 256 CU), every row in this PR, **3 independent passes**:

| M | cells | better | tied | worse | ours, µs | previous, µs | gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 20 | 19 | 1 | 0 | 306.0 | 404.6 | +24.4% |
| 2 | 17 | 17 | 0 | 0 | 299.3 | 379.8 | +21.2% |
| 3 | 18 | 18 | 0 | 0 | 307.7 | 406.5 | +24.3% |
| 4 | 14 | 14 | 0 | 0 | 276.9 | 340.2 | +18.6% |
| 5 | 13 | 13 | 0 | 0 | 270.4 | 329.5 | +17.9% |
| **all** | **82** | **81** | **1** | **0** | **1460.4** | **1860.6** | **+21.5%** |

**Every row confirmed in every pass, zero regressions.** The one tie is `(7168,1536)` at M=1, where the kernels sit 0.3% apart; it never lost a pass.

An earlier revision of this description quoted −9%…−25% against `wvSplitK`. Those were taken against a September-2025 build of that kernel and are withdrawn.

**Downstream:** the same rows measured end to end through vLLM's `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl` give +4.7% on M=1..4 against `wvSplitK` — a kernel aiter cannot select, as it lives in vLLM's own extension. Wiring and caveats in [vllm-project/vllm#55860](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55860).

gfx942 (MI325X, 304 CU), every row in this PR, **3 independent passes**:

| M | cells | better | tied | worse | ours, µs | previous, µs | gain |
|---|-------|--------|------|-------|----------|--------------|------|
| 1 | 21 | 21 | 0 | 0 | 419.1 | 560.9 | +25.3% |
| 2 | 21 | 21 | 0 | 0 | 436.6 | 562.8 | +22.4% |
| 3 | 19 | 19 | 0 | 0 | 444.9 | 550.6 | +19.2% |
| 4 | 19 | 19 | 0 | 0 | 421.3 | 516.5 | +18.4% |
| 5 | 11 | 11 | 0 | 0 | 376.3 | 423.0 | +11.0% |
| **all** | **91** | **91** | **0** | **0** | **2098.1** | **2613.8** | **+19.7%** |

**Every row confirmed in every pass, zero regressions, no batch discarded by the null control.** Here `previous` is always the heuristic fallback, which resolved to `torch`: at the branch point no bf16 config carried a `gfx942` row with `cu_num=304`, so all 91 rows are additions and none replaces an existing row. The rows are keyed `(gfx942, cu_num=304)`, which also matches MI300X; that part was not re-measured.

**Shapes deliberately left without a row.** 11 cells at M=3,4,5 where `opus` is faster — `router` at M=5 by 22%, `(7168,8448)` at M=5 by 9%, six other long-K shapes at M=5 by 0.5…6%, `router` and `shared down` at M=3, `latent down` at M=4 — confirmed on two cards with 0–2 wins out of 90 pairs. Plus 3 cells where the tuner and graph replay disagree reproducibly (`(7168,8448)` at M=4, `attention O` and `(4608,1536)` at M=5): five tuner runs rank `opus` first, graph replay ranks the decode kernel first by up to 1520/1520 pairs.

**Full evidence** — protocol, benches, raw records, and the measurement errors made and corrected along the way — is attached as `pr4114_evidence.tar.gz`.

## Architecture support

- **gfx950**: Wave uses `v_dot2_f32_bf16`; BlockMFMA uses MFMA with two-stage prefetch
- **gfx942**: Wave uses scalar_f32 contraction; BlockMFMA uses single-stage prefetch; both paths correctness-tested

## Test Plan

- `op_tests/test_flydsl_decode_gemm.py` — a standard op_test: `python3 <file>` runs the five correctness cases (Wave no-bias, Wave with bias and odd N/K tails, BlockMFMA global, BlockMFMA full LDS with K padding, BlockMFMA persistent-N multi-turn) and then the perf sweep with `checkAllclose` against an FP32 reference. `pytest <file>` runs the same five cases. No CI script changes are needed — the file sits where the runner already scans.
- `python3 -m unittest op_tests.tuning_tests.test_config_shape_collision` — `Ran 17 tests ... OK`. The config keyspace stays collision-free across every model file; includes a positive control (a planted duplicate must be caught).
- Row-level verification: every row confirmed over 3 independent passes, zero regressions (raw records in the attached archive).
- Black and Ruff 0.16.0 (the CI pin) clean on all changed files.
- CI on MI300X (gfx942) and MI355X (gfx950).

body:
## Summary

- **torch.symm_mem transport**: Add `torch.distributed._symmetric_memory` (backed by `mori.allocator`) as a new transport for custom all-reduce on gfx1250. Opt-in via `AITER_CUSTOM_AR_USE_SYMM_MEM=1`. Replaces manual IPC handle exchange (TCPStore / Unix socket VMM fd) with `symm_mem.rendezvous()` which handles fabric handles or POSIX fds internally. Reuses existing gfx1250 VMM-style C++ ops (pointer-list interface) — no C++ kernel changes for this part.
- **Collective P2P probe**: Before init, allocates a small buffer + rendezvous across all peers. mori's rendezvous validates P2P via `hipMemSetAccess(RW)` for each peer — all ranks agree on pass/fail, safe fallback to VMM/IPC with no hang risk.
- **world_size 6/8**: Extend gfx1250 template instantiations from {2,4} to {2,4,6,8} across all dispatch points (allreduce, allgather, reduce_scatter). Introduce `DISPATCH_NGPUS_1250` macro to unify the dispatch pattern. No algorithmic changes — kernels are simple `for(i<ngpus)` loops and `Signal`/`RankData` structs already have 8 slots.
