title: [Triton/Gluon] Add rotating-buffer GEMM A16W16 benchmark
body:
## Motivation

Add bench_gemm_a16w16_rotating.py — a GEMM benchmark that uses rotating buffers captured in a HIP graph to measure realistic L2-cold kernel latency while eliminating host launch overhead.

## Technical Details

- Allocates a buffer pool sized to exceed L2 capacity so each kernel dispatch within a graph replay is an L2 miss.
- Captures N kernel dispatches (round-robin through the pool) into a single graph, replays it multiple times for stable statistics.
- --bias flag (default off) to control ADD_BIAS kernel variant.
- --kernels-per-graph, --num-replays, --warmup-replays, --pool-size, --target-pool-mb for fine-grained control.

## Test Plan

As this is a benchmark test I have been running it to test certain gemms.

## Test Result

Output from this fix is more consistent with expectations (rotating buffer results in benchmark times that do not get faster after first run)

## Submission Checklist

- [ ] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#pull-requests.

title: [Triton/Gluon] Drop `GRID_MN` from the batched MXFP4 GEMM specialisation keys
body:
### Motivation

Both batched MXFP4 GEMM kernels take `GRID_MN` as a `tl.constexpr`, fed by a
`@triton.heuristics` lambda over the raw `M` and `N`:

```python
"GRID_MN": lambda args: triton.cdiv(args["M"], args["BLOCK_SIZE_M"])
* triton.cdiv(args["N"], args["BLOCK_SIZE_N"]),
```

That puts `M` into the JIT cache key without passing through
`STANDARD_M_BOUNDS`. Under serving, `M` is the scheduler-formed batch size, so
the key is effectively indexed by batch shape: the kernel mints a new binary
every time a new batch shape appears, and never converges. On
`GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` (MI355X, TP2, vLLM), `_batched_gemm_a16wfp4_kernel`
built 168 binaries for 10 distinct configs and was still compiling new variants
at repetition 5 of a benchmark.

### Change

Four edits per file:

- Call site: `remap_xcd(pid, GRID_MN)` → `remap_xcd(pid, num_pid_m * num_pid_n)`
- Drop the `GRID_MN` lambda from `@triton.heuristics`
- Drop `GRID_MN: tl.constexpr` from the kernel signature
- Drop `"GRID_MN"` from the `make_kernel_repr` list

`num_pid_m` and `num_pid_n` are already computed in-body from the same `M`,
`N`, `BLOCK_SIZE_M`, `BLOCK_SIZE_N`, so the value is identical; `remap_xcd` is
pure index arithmetic and both call sites discard its return. Same binaries,
far fewer of them. No tuning configs are touched.

### Precedent

- **#2427** made exactly this change — same four edits — to `gemm_a16w16` and
  to `batched_gemm_a8w8_a_per_token_group_prequant_w_per_batched_tensor_quant`,
  under the title "for no recompile".
- **#4199** did it for `gemm_a8w8_blockscale`, but bundled a re-tune of 12
  config JSONs. This PR changes no configs.
- `gemm/basic/gemm_afp4wfp4.py:88` already computes the same value in-body
  rather than as a constexpr, so the in-body form is already in the tree.

### Evidence

Six vLLM servers, three GPU pairs, started together on an idle host. Each
server runs one config (512×512 tokens, concurrency 16) for 6 repetitions.
Throughput is output tokens/s; "steady" is the mean of reps 3–6.

| build | GPUs | rep 1 tok/s | steady tok/s | rep‑1 vs steady | rep‑1 wall | compiles per rep | after rep 1 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| `main` | 0,2 | 217.1 | 372.7 | **−41.8%** | 25.56 s | 60, 8, 8, 8, 4, 0 | 28 |
| `main` | 1,3 | 227.4 | 386.8 | **−41.2%** | 24.40 s | 54, 4, 4, 4, 0, 0 | 12 |
| `main` | 4,6 | 239.9 | 375.6 | **−36.1%** | 23.13 s | 50, 0, 0, 8, 8, 0 | 16 |
| this PR | 0,2 | **405.1** | 400.2 | **+1.2%** | **13.70 s** | **14, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0** | **0** |
| this PR | 1,3 | **402.2** | 407.6 | **−1.3%** | **13.79 s** | **14, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0** | **0** |
| this PR | 4,6 | **385.2** | 399.9 | **−3.7%** | **14.40 s** | **14, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0** | **0** |

Totals: **220 → 42** compilations during the run, **56 → 0** after repetition 1.
Compiles per rep are counted by snapshotting the compile-cache directories at
each repetition boundary and diffing the new entries.

- The first-repetition cost is removed, not reduced — on all three pairs. The
  residual 14 are unrelated kernels compiled once at startup; this PR's arms
  build no `_batched_gemm_a16wfp4_kernel` variants at all.
- `main` never converges: it is still compiling at repetition 5. This PR
  compiles once, then never again.
- The cost is not confined to repetition 1: `main`'s steady figures (372–387)
  are themselves depressed by continued compilation. Averaging only the
  repetitions that provably compiled nothing puts `main` at 398–404 against
  this PR's 399–409 — steady-state performance is unchanged.

Across a wider six-config sweep on a single server, total compilations fell
285 → 35 (−88%).

### Testing

`op_tests/triton_tests/gemm/batched/test_batched_gemm_a16wfp4.py` and
`test_batched_gemm_afp4wfp4.py`, same container and GPUs, kernels swapped
between runs: **4977 passed, 0 failed** on both `origin/main` and this branch.

### Not included

- **`do_not_specialize=["M", "N"]`**, which #2427 also added. It removes zero
  compilations here (29 vs 33) — what remains after `GRID_MN` is Triton's
  bounded divisibility specialisation, paid once at startup — and costs
  0.9–2.5% throughput, the regression #2482 had to repair with `EVEN_MN`.
- **The other 15 files declaring `GRID_MN: tl.constexpr`.** Seven discard
  `remap_xcd`'s return identically and three never read the parameter at all;
  the rest need more care. This PR covers only the two batched MXFP4 files.

### Notes

The measured workload exercises `batched_gemm_a16wfp4` only —
`batched_gemm_afp4wfp4` never compiled during these runs. It is changed here
because it carries the identical heuristic, signature and discarded-return call
site, so the same cost applies wherever it is exercised; it is covered by the
tests above.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; the author has reviewed and validated the
change.

title: [HIP] [JIT] Remove unintended CK dependency from plain top-k
body:
## Summary

- replace CK numeric aliases in the plain top-k kernel with AITER's canonical
  Opus FP16/BF16 scalar and vector types
- define the raw-buffer cache-policy value locally instead of depending on
  `ck_tile::amd_buffer_coherence_enum`
- preserve the existing cache-policy encoding for legacy, CDNA3/4, and gfx12
  targets
- remove `module_topk_plain` from the CK-free exclusion list
- make the correctness test deterministic and configurable
- ensure correctness mismatches cause the test to fail

## Motivation

`module_topk_plain` is implemented as a native HIP/Opus module and does not
otherwise use Composable Kernel. However, its implementation referenced
`ck_tile` numeric aliases and a CK cache-policy enum through a transitive
include.

That accidental dependency prevented the module from building without the full
CK headers, requiring it to be excluded from CK-free builds.

The kernel only needs compiler-compatible FP16/BF16 types and the integer
cache-policy encoding passed to `llvm.amdgcn.raw.buffer.load`. AITER already
provides the appropriate scalar and vector types through Opus, so the CK
dependency is unnecessary.

## Behavior

No algorithmic behavior change is intended.

The local raw-buffer policy values match
`ck_tile::amd_buffer_coherence_enum::slc`:

- legacy targets, including gfx908: `2`
- gfx942 and gfx950: `19`
- gfx12: `25`

## Testing

Validated on AMD Instinct MI100 (`gfx908:sramecc+:xnack-`) atop the gfx908
target-enablement changes in #5720.

A clean rebuild of `module_topk_plain` succeeded.

The correctness matrix covered:

- FP16, BF16, and FP32

title: [HIP] [Activation] Add standalone relu2 (Squared ReLU) elementwise kernel for non-gated MoE MLPs
body:
## Motivation

NemotronH's non-gated MoE MLP layers use Squared ReLU (`relu(x)^2`) as their activation function. aiter currently only implements *gated* activations (`silu_and_mul`, `gelu_and_mul`, `gelu_tanh_and_mul`) and a plain (non-gated) `gelu_fast`, but has no plain Squared ReLU op. 

Improving performance for the ``NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-BF16`` model requires enabling relu2, fused MoE GEMM support, and vLLM AITER backend integration. This PR's scope is limited to enabling relu2.

This PR adds a standalone `relu2` elementwise kernel so non-gated MoE architectures like NemotronH can use aiter's fused activation path instead of falling back to eager PyTorch.

This is Tier 1 of a 3-PR series adding end-to-end relu2 support:
1. **This PR** standalone aiter elementwise kernel (no dependencies)
2. aiter CK-Tile fused MoE GEMM support for relu2 (depends on this PR). The draft [PR](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5708) is ready.
3. vLLM AITER backend integration (depends on the Tier 2 PR above)

**Note**: For end-to-end results and performance, refer to the related Tier 2 and Tier 3 PRs.

## Technical Details

Mirrors the existing `gelu_fast` pattern end-to-end:

- Declared the `relu2(out, input)` op signature alongside the other elementwise activations
- Implemented `relu2_kernel<T>` (`r = max(x, 0); return r * r`, computed in fp32) and its launcher, using the same vectorized launch macro as the other elementwise activations
- Added explicit tensor validation (GPU, contiguous, matching numel/dtype/device) before dispatch
- Added the pybind11 binding so the op is exposed to Python
- Added the Python-side `@compile_ops(...)` stub (JIT-compiled on first call, same as all other activation ops)
- Added `test_relu2` plus a driver loop matching the existing `test_gelu_fast` benchmark pattern

No changes to gated/MoE-fused activation paths, this is a plain elementwise op only.

## Test Plan

Validated on MI350 (gfx950):

- **Correctness**: compared `aiter.relu2(out, x)` against a  `torch.nn.functional.relu(x.float())**2` reference across 4 shapes:
  (1024,4096), (1024,8192), (4096,4096), (4096,8192), bf16 dtype.
- **Performance**: benchmarked `aiter.relu2` vs. the same eager PyTorch reference across the same 4 shapes.

## Test Result

|------|------|----------|----------|---------|--------------|--------|
| 1024 | 4096 | 8.038    | 22.051   | 2.74x   | 0.000000     | PASS   |
| 1024 | 8192 | 7.858    | 31.297   | 3.98x   | 0.000000     | PASS   |
| 4096 | 4096 | 13.158   | 55.536   | 4.22x   | 0.000000     | PASS   |
| 4096 | 8192 | 21.431   | 107.907  | 5.04x   | 0.000000     | PASS   |

Exact-match correctness (`max_abs_diff: 0.0`) and 2.74x–5.04x speedup
vs. eager PyTorch across all tested shapes.

title: [ASM] [HIP] MLA PS mode asm and opus kernel support nhead12,8
body:
## Motivation

On gfx950, fp8/fp8 MLA persistent decode only accepted head counts that are 16 or a multiple
of 16 (16 / 32 / 64 / 96 / 128). Anything else was either folded down to 16 heads — which is
only possible when `num_heads % 16 == 0` — or rejected outright by
`get_mla_metadata_v1_2_device`. A model with 12 query heads per KV head therefore had no path
at all, on either the asm or the opus kernel.

This PR makes both kernels accept head counts that are not a multiple of 16.

## Technical Details

### Why a non-multiple-of-16 head count broke the causal mask

Both kernels give each wave a fixed tile of packed Q rows — `W_M = 16` for the opus 16mx8
kernel, `SUB_Q = 32` for the asm qh32 kernel — and packed row `p` belongs to query token
`p / nhead`. While `nhead` is a multiple of that tile, every row of a wave lands on the same
token, so the causal bound is wave-uniform and lives in an SGPR:

```cpp
diag_kv_bound = (warp_id * T::W_M) / nhead + causal_diagonal;
```

With `nhead = 12` a token boundary falls *inside* a wave: rows 0–11 of warp 0 are token 0,
rows 12–15 are token 1. All 16 rows still got token 0's bound, so 4 of every 16 query rows
were masked one KV column too early. The bound has to be per lane:

```cpp
row = warp_id * T::W_M + lane_id % T::W_M;   // lane_id % W_M is the MFMA M index,
diag_kv_bound = row / nhead + causal_diagonal;   // same one make_layout_o and the LSE store use
```

Measured on the unmodified opus kernel, `-n 12,8` over the default grid: **16 of 64 cells
failed**, max |delta| 2.58 with 33% of elements off. The asm kernel had the same defect.

- **asm (SP3 `MLA_A8W8_QH32_1TG_4W_32mx4_64nx1_PS`)**: a third branch in `causal_mask` computes
  the token per lane with a `v_rcp_f32` divide plus a 1/256 bias before the truncating convert
  (`p < 128` and `gqa_ratio <= 128`, so `p/gqa_ratio` is either integral or at least 1/128 from
  the next integer, which absorbs the ≤1ulp reciprocal error in both directions). The existing
  fast paths — `gqa_ratio` a multiple of `SUB_Q`, and `gqa_ratio == 16` — are kept and take the
  same instructions as before. Only the four rebuilt `.co` files are in this PR; the SP3 source
  lives in a separate repo.
- **opus (`mla_decode_fp8_16mx8_32nx1.hpp`)**: `causal_kv_bound` takes `lane_id` and is gated on
  a new compile-time trait `WAVE_SPANS_TOKENS`, which the host sets from `H % W_M != 0`. Head
  counts that are a multiple of `W_M` keep the wave-uniform SGPR form, so their codegen is
  untouched; only the new head counts pay the extra live VGPR in a kernel that already sits at
  256.

### The causal diagonal is not confined to the last KV tile

A work item's bounds span its `q_len` columns ending at `valid_kv_len - 1`, so they sit inside
the last KV tile only when `valid_kv_len % KV_TILE_SIZE >= q_len`. Otherwise they reach back
into the previous tile, which `tile_idx == tile_end - 1` left unmasked, and the rows bounded
there attended past their diagonal. With only the per-lane fix applied, `-n 12,8 -c 33` still
**failed** at max |delta| 1.41 over 58% of elements.

`mask_oob_scores` now masks the last two tiles. Two is always enough: a work item holds at most
128 packed rows over at least 4 heads, so `q_len <= 32 == KV_TILE_SIZE`. Deriving the exact tile
set from `causal_diagonal` instead was tried and is slower — it keeps `causal_diagonal` live for
every tile's test, which measured −0.7% across the existing shapes versus −0.3% for the fixed
two-tile window.

This defect predates the PR and applies to every causal shape; the default test grid never hit
it because all of its ctx values are ≡ 0 or ≥ q_len mod 32.

### Dispatch and metadata

The same predicate is added in the five places that have to agree, alongside the existing
`natively_supported` clauses:

```
arch == gfx950 && q_fp8 && kv_fp8 && (nhead % 16 != 0) && (nhead * max_seqlen_qo <= 128)
```

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `csrc/kernels/mla/metadata/v1_2_device.cuh` | metadata `natively_supported` (no head folding) |
| `csrc/py_itfs_cu/asm_mla.cu` | routes to the qh32 kernel: `config_gqa_ratio = 32`, `config_max_seqlen_q = 4`, real gqa in `args.s_MQA` |
| `aiter/ops/attention.py` | metadata buffer sizing + `decode_update_mla_metadata_v1` |
| `aiter/mla.py` | `mla_decode_fwd` native-support check |
| `op_tests/test_mla_persistent.py` | the reference path's matching check |

Two smaller pieces:

- `csrc/kernels/mla/reduce.cu` gains the `(12 heads, 512 dim)` instantiation; the dispatch table
  is a whitelist and 12 was not in it.
- `get_mla_metadata_info_v1`'s `assert num_head_qo % 8 == 0` is relaxed to `% 4`. Nothing in that
  function divides by the head count — it only sizes buffers.

`opus_mla_decode_fwd.cu` needs no head-count gate of its own; the metadata check upstream of it
is the gate, and `WAVE_SPANS_TOKENS` is picked from the runtime `H`.

### Supported range

128 is what one work item holds: 8 waves × `W_M` 16 for opus, 4 waves × `SUB_Q` 32 for asm. The
gate is deliberately `nhead * max_seqlen_qo <= 128` — i.e. one qo tile per batch — rather than a
per-tile test, because the metadata splits qo tiles in *tokens*: `ceil(packed / 128)` tiles of
`ceil(seqlen_qo / tiles)` tokens. Two ceilings in a row can hand back a tile over the limit
(12 heads × 21 tokens → 2 tiles of 11 tokens = 132 rows), which the kernels would silently
truncate. Keeping the batch inside a single tile avoids that case entirely.

Combinations outside the range are rejected at metadata with the existing "only supports #heads
…" error rather than producing wrong results.

## Test Plan

```bash
# new head counts + the established shapes, both kernels, full default grid
for n in 12,8 12,6 16,8 32,4 64,2 128,2; do
  for opus in 0 1; do
    AITER_MLA_USE_OPUS=$opus python3 op_tests/test_mla_persistent.py -d fp8 -kvd fp8 -n $n
  done
done

# against origin/main, same grid, 3 reps, both kernels
AITER_MLA_USE_OPUS={0,1} python3 op_tests/test_mla_persistent.py -d fp8 -kvd fp8 \
    -n {12,8|12,6|24,8|16,8|32,4|64,2|128,2} -b 16 32 64 -c 5200 8192 16384 65535
```

Verdicts below are against the `golden fp8` reference — the one that quantises the same way the
kernel does. gfx950 / MI355X, ROCm 7.1.

## Test Result

### Accuracy, full default grid

`-b 1 3 5 16 32 64 128 256` × `-c 21 64 256 512 1200 3200 5200 8192`, 64 cells per shape.

`12,4` and `24,4` were also run over the full grid: 0 failed on both kernels. `24,8` is rejected

Before the fix, for reference: `12,8` opus **16 / 64 cells failed**, max |delta| 2.58;

title: [HIP] fix(custom_all_reduce): uniform trip count for the block barriers
body:
## What is wrong

Three kernels in `csrc/include/custom_all_reduce.cuh` stage their operands through shared memory
and bracket that with two block-wide `__syncthreads()` — inside a grid-stride loop whose trip
count is **not uniform across the block**:

| kernel | loop |
|---|---|
| `cross_device_reduce_2stage` | stage 1, reduce-scatter |
| `cross_device_reduce_2stage_write_mode` | stage 2 |
| `reduce_scatter_cross_device_store` | fused allreduce+rmsnorm, first step |

Taking the first as the example:

```cpp
for(int idx = start + tid; idx < end; idx += stride)
{
    *(reinterpret_cast<P*>(&tmp_smem[0]) + threadIdx.x) = ptrs[warp_id][idx];
    __syncthreads();
    if(warp_id == 0) { /* sum the ngpus operands out of smem */ }
    __syncthreads();
}
```

`end - start` is this rank's partition, `size / ngpus`, which is not generally a multiple of
`stride = gridDim.x * (THREAD_NUM / ngpus)`. The lanes that cover the tail therefore run one
iteration more than the rest, so the barriers pair up across different iterations — and against
the ones in `end_sync`. Two consequences:

* the `warp_id == 0` reduction can read `tmp_smem` before the other wavefronts have written
  their operands into it;
* a wavefront can reach `end_sync` and publish "stage 1 done" while another is still producing
  `tmp_out`, so the stage-2 all-gather can read a partition that is not finished.

Either way the output is wrong at a fixed relative position inside each rank's partition.

## How it shows up

`size` is flat, so each rank owns a contiguous `size / ngpus` slice — one quarter of the rows of
a `[bs, hidden]` tensor at `ngpus == 4`. The damage lands at the same offset in every quarter:

```
bs = 120  ->  bad rows {1, 31, 61, 91}      (stride 30 = 120/4)
bs = 160  ->  bad rows {11, 51, 91, 131}    (stride 40 = 160/4)
```

Found in an RL workload; reproduced standalone below.

## Standalone reproduction

Four ranks on MI355X, bf16 `[bs, 2880]`, 32 shapes × 600 reductions each. Every reduction is run
twice and compared bitwise (no tolerance needed), and also compared against RCCL's `all_reduce`
(bf16 rounding on a 4-way sum is ~0.05, so anything above that is a wrong answer rather than a
different summation order):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| wrong vs RCCL, and non-deterministic | **64 of 19200** | **0 of 19200** |
| shapes affected | bs = 120, 121, 127, 157, 160, 161 | none |
| worst \|diff\| | **12.4** | 0.0625 (pure bf16 rounding) |
| 48 reductions back to back, bs=160 | **300 of 11520** wrong, worst 13.1 | 0 of 11520 |
| world_size=2 (1-stage path) | 0 of 5120 | 0 of 5120 — no regression |

It is a race, so the counts move between runs; an earlier sweep over a slightly different set of
shapes gave 43/19200 and 173/11520. Most shapes pass either way — the race needs the partition
remainder to land mid-block, which is why this has survived.

The numbers above were measured on a build based on `d9e5ef7ce` that also carried a second
commit, since dropped, which widened two sync scopes. @TennyWang1223 re-measured `6110f00f`
on its own and reproduced the fix, which attributes it to the barrier change alone. The
three patched hunks are unchanged on `main`, and the rebased diff is byte-identical to the
one that was tested.

## The fix

Round the loop bound up to a multiple of the stride, which makes the trip count exactly uniform
(`tid < stride` by construction), and predicate the work. No added synchronisation and no change
to the reduction order.

`reduce_scatter_cross_device_store` is fixed by inspection — same defect, same file — but the
reproducer above does not exercise the fused-allreduce path.

Timing, 7 reps × 500 calls, median us/call taken as the max over ranks, whole measurement
repeated twice: within run-to-run noise at bs=120..161, and **3-6% slower** at bs=256
(19.2 → 20.3) and bs=512 (32.2 → 33.1).

title: [FlyDSL] [CI] gfx950 FP8 paged-prefill attention with asymmetric head dim and varlen support
body:
## Motivation

This PR aims to integrate the native gfx950 FP8 paged-prefill attention with asymmetric Q/K and V head dimensions and packed variable-length sequence support from [ROCm/FlyDSL#1066](https://github.com/ROCm/FlyDSL/pull/1066) into AITER.

AITER already supports FlyDSL dense FP8 attention through [ROCm/aiter#5326](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5326), but paged prefill still needs a native path that consumes the serving both kv cache layout used by sglang [SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT](https://docs.sglang.io/docs/references/environment_variables#amd-&-rocm) directly:
- `SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=nhd`: Linear KV-cache layout with page size 1 
- `SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d`: Vectorized 5D KV-cache layout with page size 16/64/1024

## Technical Details

- Add native causal packed-varlen FP8 paged attention for gfx950 based on FlyDSL `0.3.4.1` runtime.
- Support `D128/V128`, `D192/V128`, and `D192/V192` with BF16 output.
- Support page-1 linear/linear3d caches and page-16/64/1024 vectorized caches.
- Accept both block-table metadata and native CSR metadata (`kv_indptr`, `kv_page_indices`, and `kv_last_page_lens`).
- Add public API aiter.ops.flydsl.flydsl_flash_attn_paged_prefill_func for downstream farmwork integration.
- Preserve preallocated output, custom stream, graph replay, runtime softmax scale, ragged requests, odd page counts, and large cache addressing contracts, LSE.
- Share common dense/paged FP8 pipeline helpers and split paged GEMM, LDS, softmax, and epilogue helpers into focused modules.
- Add correctness, API, dispatch, metadata, stream, graph, and regression coverage to the standard AITER test shard.


## Performance

MI355X (`gfx950`) with ROCm/HIP `7.2.26015`, Torch `2.9.1+rocm7.2.0`, `B=1`, `Hq=16`, `Hkv=1`, causal `Q:KV=1:2`, page size 64, vectorized FP8 K/V, and preallocated BF16 output.

The FlyDSL source column uses PR #1066 commit `8a662b0` with its locally built FlyDSL `0.3.3` runtime. The AITER migrated columns use commit `c933927e` with FlyDSL `0.3.2`.

title: [CK] [Bugfix][Perf] fused_moe: tune the non-temporal load hint per tuned row
body:
## What's wrong

`get_2stage_cfgs()` initialises the non-temporal load hint to `False` and assigns it only
inside the heuristic branch:

```python
use_non_temporal_load = False
if cfg is None or bypass_tuned_config:
    use_non_temporal_load = use_nt(token, topk, expert)   # heuristic branch only
else:
    ...                                                   # tuned branch: never assigned
```

A shape loses non-temporal weight loads the moment it gains a tuned CSV row, and
`AITER_USE_NT` is dead there as well, because the override lives inside `use_nt()`.

An earlier revision of this PR simply derived the flag on the tuned path too. Review pointed
out why that is not sound, and measurements agree: the tuner never passes `non_temporal_load`
(`gemm_moe_tune.py` -> `ck_moe_stage{1,2}_fwd_out`), so **every** candidate in every shipped
row was ranked with the hint off. Turning it on at runtime runs the selected kernel outside
the conditions it was selected in, and the recorded `us1`/`us2` stop describing runtime. On
gfx942 that shows up directly: the shipped `ds_v3` row for `7168x2048 e33 topk9` at token 128
(`block_m=32`) is **6.6 % slower** with the hint on, while the same shape at tokens 16 and 64
is 5.0 % / 3.5 % faster. One shape family, no constant right answer.

## Fix

Make the hint part of what gets tuned instead of something derived next to the tuned row. The
tuner sweeps both values for the quant types whose kernels read it, ranks
`(kernel, block_m, nt)` jointly by `us1 + us2`, and records the winner in a new `nt` column;
the runtime reads that column.

```diff
     else:
         block_m = cfg["block_m"]
+        # rows tuned before the nt column keep the hint off
+        nt_override = int(os.environ.get("AITER_USE_NT", "-1"))
+        if nt_override != -1:
+            use_non_temporal_load = bool(nt_override)
+        elif "nt" in cfg:
+            use_non_temporal_load = bool(int(cfg["nt"]))
```

`use_nt()` and the heuristic branch are untouched, so nothing changes for shapes without a
tuned row. Rows without the column keep `nt=False`, which is today's behaviour, so no shipped
config changes until it is retuned. `AITER_USE_NT` now overrides both paths, as it was
documented to. On the tuner side `nt` is threaded exactly like the existing `flat` / `xbf16`
columns: it rides in the candidate tag, becomes a column in the candidate table, joins the
dedup key and the stage1 x stage2 merge key (so both stages of a row agree on it), and is
written out. The sweep is gated to `per_1x128`, so every other quant type keeps its candidate
count.

## Results, MI325X (gfx942, 304 CU)

DSv3 EP shape `7168x2048 e33 topk9`, per_1x128 fp8 blockscale, preshuffled weights.

**Tuner level** — same box, same harness, the extra dimension is the only difference:

| token | without the nt sweep    | with the nt sweep               | gain   |
| ----- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------ |
| 16    | `block_m=16`, 360.34 us | `block_m=16`, `nt=1`, 329.59 us | +8.5 % |
| 64    | `block_m=32`, 375.48 us | `block_m=32`, `nt=1`, 358.88 us | +4.4 % |
| 128   | `block_m=64`, 404.58 us | `block_m=64`, `nt=1`, 395.84 us | +2.2 % |

**Runtime level** — whole `fused_moe` op, CUDA-graph replay, 200 iters after 40 warmup, 8
rotated weight sets, 3 interleaved rounds per config, median:

| token | shipped rows | retuned, no nt sweep | retuned, nt swept | vs shipped |
| ----- | ------------ | -------------------- | ----------------- | ---------- |
| 16    | 383.2 us     | 374.5 us             | 329.6 us          | +14.0 %    |
| 64    | 398.0 us     | 411.5 us             | 365.0 us          | +8.3 %     |
| 128   | 455.4 us     | 431.2 us             | 417.2 us          | +8.4 %     |

Retuning with the hint in the search is worth +3.3 % to +12.0 % over retuning without it on
the same box.

**Why this cannot be a heuristic.** The `block_m` the tuner picks and the best value of the
hint are coupled: what the hint discards is weight reuse between M-tiles of the same expert,
so it wins while an expert stays inside one tile and loses once it spans two. At token 128 on
this shape, stage2 measured alone with `rocprofv3` is 161.0 -> 191.8 us with the hint at
`block_m=32`, but 153.1 -> 135.7 us at `block_m=64`; `rocprofv3 --pmc TCC_HIT_sum TCC_MISS_sum`
attributes the whole difference to cache hit rate (42.8 % -> 28.5 %, 722 MB -> 920 MB below L2
against 2 x 484 MB of logical B reads, both arms sustaining ~4 TB/s). A predicate over token
count cannot see `block_m`, and under imbalanced routing it cannot see the tail experts that
cross into a second tile before the mean does either. Tuning it removes the guesswork.

## Results, MI355X (gfx950, 256 CU)

Second architecture, independent box. 26 shapes from three families (`4096x384 e128 topk8`,
`7168x512 e257 topk9`, `3072x1536 e256 topk8`), same machine, same harness, same
single-process settings, one card, tuned **three times per arm** at the PR's parent `c3caa55`
and at the head `c26f391`. 23 of the 26 resolve a winner on every run of both arms (the other
three are under *Caveats*). Times are the tuner's own per-candidate measurement for the
winning row; gain is median-of-three, spread is max-min within an arm.

The result separates by winning path. The 16 asm 1-stage shapes do not read the flag and do
not move: all keep `nt=0`, median gain +0.07 % over a range of -0.7 % .. +0.8 % against
per-arm spreads up to 1.4 %. The 7 CK 2-stage shapes are one family, `4096x384 e128 topk8`,
`doweight_stage1=1`, all at `block_m=16`:

| token | parent    | PR        | gain   | per-arm spread | `nt`                |
| ----- | --------- | --------- | ------ | -------------- | ------------------- |
| 1     | 38.62 us  | 38.19 us  | +1.1 % | 7.1 % / 4.6 %  | `0`/`1`, unstable   |
| 2     | 42.65 us  | 41.38 us  | +3.0 % | 6.2 % / 1.5 %  | `1`                 |
| 4     | 50.69 us  | 47.30 us  | +6.7 % | 6.2 % / 3.6 %  | `1`                 |
| 8     | 61.86 us  | 57.14 us  | +7.6 % | 1.3 % / 2.7 %  | `1`                 |
| 16    | 83.12 us  | 76.54 us  | +7.9 % | 1.4 % / 1.7 %  | `1`                 |
| 32    | 113.93 us | 105.10 us | +7.8 % | 0.3 % / 0.4 %  | `1`                 |
| 64    | 122.32 us | 113.05 us | +7.6 % | 0.2 % / 0.4 %  | `1`                 |

From token 8 up, the gain is several times either arm's spread and holds within half a point
across four shapes. At tokens 1-4 the shape runs in tens of microseconds, the arms overlap,
and token 1 does not even settle on a value across repeats — the flag genuinely does not
matter there, so nothing is claimed. Both arms pick the same kernel pair at tokens 1-16; at
tokens 32 and 64 the PR arm's winner is the `128x16x128x128` variant rather than
`256x16x128x256`, which is the ranking doing its job once `nt` is in the search space. An
isolated single-shape rerun where both arms converged on the identical kernel and `block_m`
isolates the flag on its own: 121.76 us -> 114.31 us, +6.1 % (stage1 +7.0 %, stage2 +4.5 %).


## Cost and compatibility

* CK candidates double for `per_1x128` only: 10 -> 20 per shape here, one shape 19 s -> 38 s,
  roughly 10 min for a full model file. Verified that a `per_Token` tune is unchanged.
* Rows without the column behave exactly as today. The 46 shipped blockscale 2-stage rows with
  `use_nt() == True` (38 at `cu_num` 256, 8 at `cu_num` 304) keep the hint off until someone
  retunes them; retuning shipped configs is out of scope here.
* No C++ change: `ck_moe_stage{1,2}_fwd` already take the flag and `gen_instances.py` already
  compiles both NT instantiations.

## Verification

* Runtime decision table, all five cases checked against `get_2stage_cfgs` on **both** gfx942
  and gfx950: legacy CSV (no column) -> off; `nt=0` -> off; `nt=1` -> on; legacy +
  `AITER_USE_NT=1` -> on; `nt=1` + `AITER_USE_NT=0` -> off. At the parent commit all five
  return off, which is the bug.
* Shipped-config regression, exhaustive: all **179** `cu_num=256` blockscale 2-stage rows across
  the 7 shipped CSVs (`ds_v3`, `glm5`, `minimax-m2_5`, `qwen3_235b`, `qwen3_5_397b`, and the
  untuned files) resolved through `get_2stage_cfgs` on both arms and compared field by field —
  `block_m`, `ksplit`, both kernel names, `nt_stage1`, `nt_stage2`. **Zero differences.** 119 of
  those rows are ones where `use_nt()` would return `True`; they stay off on both arms,
  confirming the heuristic was already inert on the tuned path and that this change does not
  switch it on.
* Tuner smoke test: the dispatch list shows each CK kernel twice, once per value; the candidate
  table and the tuned CSV carry `nt`; `per_Token` keeps its candidate count.
* Hand-written rows confirm the column drives the kernel: the same shipped config with `nt=1`
  reproduces +5.0 % / +3.5 % / -6.6 % at tokens 16 / 64 / 128.
* Numerics: the flag only selects `AmdBufferCoherenceEnum`, no arithmetic changes. Measured on
  gfx950, per-candidate reference error is identical between the two arms and between `nt=0` and
  `nt=1` (stage1 0.1 % in every group; stage2 within 0.1 pp).
* `op_tests/test_moe_blockscale.py` exits 0 with the same six checks; instrumenting
  `get_2stage_cfgs` shows it never enters the tuned branch (asm path only), so it does not cover
  this change.
* `ruff` clean on both files; no new findings (3 pre-existing in the tuner, 34 pre-existing E501
  in `fused_moe.py`, unchanged).

## Caveats

* The rankings above were produced with the catastrophic-mismatch check relaxed locally, because
  the tuner's reference comparison rejects blockscale stage1 candidates — asm and CK alike — on
  both of my boxes, while `per_Token` is unaffected. That blocks blockscale tuning independently
  of this change: the two files involved are untouched by this PR, and the parent commit fails
  identically on the same shapes. On gfx950 it is what leaves the three shapes above unresolved.
  The measurements are unaffected, since both arms are gated identically and the per-candidate
  errors match between them.
* Per-stage tuning of the hint is deliberately not attempted: the runtime passes one flag to both
  stages, so the merge forces stage1 and stage2 of a row to agree.

## Duplicate check

This updates my own #5443. Of the 640 open PRs, none touch `use_nt` / `non_temporal_load` in
`aiter/fused_moe.py`: #5117 is MXFP6 non-temporal *stores* in GEMM, #2947 is a gfx942 CK stage2
OOB fix, #3493 adds gfx942 tuned rows (12 more `cu_num=304` blockscale 2-stage rows, all of which
this PR leaves at `nt=0` until retuned).

---

Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom); reviewed and measured by hand.

title: [HIP] [OPUS] [JIT] Add GPT-OSS IQ2R 2-bit MoE support
body:
## Summary

- Add a self-contained AITER implementation of the GPT-OSS O0/IQ2R approximately 2.39-bit expert-weight format, encoder, checkpoint ABI, loader, and overlay support.
- Add gfx950 IQ2R expert GEMMs plus fused top-k routing, stable task construction, dynamic MXFP8 packing, GPT-OSS SwiGLU/packing, and route-weighted BF16 reduction.
- Add graph-safe GPT-OSS TP1/EP1 orchestration through `QuantType.iq2r_2bit`.
- Add captured-production-route correctness and performance harnesses.
- Optimize decode and 16K-scheduler prefill shapes with route-qualified projection-specific dispatch.

## Scope

This is strictly a GPT-OSS MoE change. It does not modify or quantize QKV, O-projection, attention, or LM-head execution. Activations use dynamic per-1x32 MXFP8/E8M0 scaling; only expert weights use IQ2R. The implementation has no Redline source or runtime dependency.

Companion integration: ROCm/ATOM#2295.

## Isolated complete-MoE performance

title: [ASM] [HIP] [CI] Mixed MXFP6/MXFP4 GEMMs
body:
## Motivation

Add production-ready gfx950 GEMMs for mixed MXFP6/MXFP4 operand orders.
These formats target the performance-quality region between A4W4 and A6W6:
they preserve substantially more BF16 cosine similarity than A4W4 while
reducing operand traffic and GEMM latency relative to A6W6.

## Summary

This change adds gfx950 assembly GEMMs for both mixed MXFP operand orders:

- A6W4: MXFP6 E2M3 activations and MXFP4 E2M1 weights.
- A4W6: MXFP4 E2M1 activations and MXFP6 E2M3 weights.
- E8M0 block scaling with one scale per 32 K elements.
- A fused gfx950 HIP path for H32 rotation, MXFP4 quantization, compact C0
  packing, and scale packing.
- Python APIs, ctypes launchers, JIT recipes, AITER-mangled code-object
  manifests, and numerical/ABI/compile tests.
- Shape-tuned runtime dispatch and tuner entry points for both operand orders.

The implementation reuses the upstream MXFP6 H32 packing contract. Applying
the same orthonormal H32 transform to both operands preserves the underlying
GEMM while reducing the impact of per-block outliers.

The shared MXFP6 packer is hardened against oversized dimensions, misaligned
buffers, and extreme-value Hadamard overflow while preserving
`torch.ops.aiter.quant_mxfp6_gemm_hip_out`. The default gfx950 path uses the
full-range HIP packer. The legacy Triton packer remains only as a private
bounded-input parity reference; it is not publicly selectable because it
cannot safely cover the full BF16/FP16 and E8M0 ranges.

## Scope

- Hardware: gfx950.
- Output: BF16.
- Tile: 256x256x128.
- Eight generic MFMA32 code objects are included: four per operand order.
- No model-specific shape branches or Wan-only code objects are included.
- Low-level launch APIs require physically padded M/N multiples of 256 and a
  padded K multiple of 128. High-level APIs accept logical dimensions.

## Tuning

The tuners enumerate compatible prebuilt kernels from each HSA manifest,
validate output against the safe default, and retain a non-default winner only
when every paired repeat wins and median gain is at least 0.5%. Runtime lookup
tries an exact logical shape before its physical 256x256x128 padded shape.

```bash
python3 csrc/gemm_a6w4/gemm_a6w4_tune.py \
  --all --shape_grouped \
  --gain-guard-warmup 30 --gain-guard-iters 150 \
  --gain-guard-reps 15 --min-gain-pct 0.5

python3 csrc/gemm_a4w6/gemm_a4w6_tune.py \
  --all --shape_grouped \
  --gain-guard-warmup 30 --gain-guard-iters 150 \
  --gain-guard-reps 15 --min-gain-pct 0.5
```

Custom runtime tables can be selected with `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A6W4_ASM` and
`AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A4W6_ASM`. Tuner-generated keys and runtime dispatch both
honor the `CU_NUM` override.

### Tuning results

Both formats were tuned over the same 57 diffusion GEMM shapes used by the
A6W6 tuning flow. Every non-default winner was revalidated on one MI355X over
15 paired repeats.

| Format | Non-default winners | Maximum gain | Geometric-mean gain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A6W4 | 11 / 57 | 10.49% | 0.95% |
| A4W6 | 9 / 57 | 8.24% | 0.54% |

All 114 tuned dispatch cases produced exact output parity with zero
mismatches.

The `N == K` fallback difference is intentional and format-specific. For
`9450x5120x5120`, paired measurements selected:

- A6W4 grouped: 125.904 us versus natural 127.339 us (1.14% faster).
- A4W6 natural: 128.002 us versus grouped 129.181 us (0.92% faster).

## Performance

Measured on one 256-CU gfx950. Values are medians after 30 warmups,
100 iterations, and 15 alternating repeats. Inputs are synthetic BF16 tensors.
Quantization plus GEMM includes dynamic activation quantization; weights are
prepared ahead of time. Cosine similarity is against the BF16 GEMM.

### GEMM-only throughput (TFLOP/s)

| M x N x K | A4W4 | A4W6 | A6W4 | A6W6 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 x 5120 x 5120 | 2213.85 | 937.33 | 935.88 | 780.71 |
| 9450 x 5120 x 5120 | 3887.87 | 3881.78 | 3930.84 | 3449.79 |
| 9450 x 13824 x 5120 | 4714.27 | 3889.24 | 3983.04 | 3485.57 |
| 9450 x 5120 x 13824 | 5431.62 | 4330.75 | 4355.72 | 3846.43 |

### Quantization plus GEMM throughput (TFLOP/s)

| M x N x K | A4W4 | A4W6 | A6W4 | A6W6 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 x 5120 x 5120 | 1067.14 | 800.22 | 789.74 | 681.28 |
| 9450 x 5120 x 5120 | 3369.79 | 3195.18 | 3129.93 | 2811.88 |
| 9450 x 13824 x 5120 | 4284.04 | 3559.83 | 3601.38 | 3180.85 |
| 9450 x 5120 x 13824 | 4350.68 | 3448.80 | 3360.12 | 3041.51 |

### Cosine similarity versus BF16

| M x N x K | A4W4 | A4W6 | A6W4 | A6W6 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 x 5120 x 5120 | 0.986685 | 0.992918 | 0.992917 | 0.999192 |
| 9450 x 5120 x 5120 | 0.986704 | 0.992931 | 0.992928 | 0.999192 |
| 9450 x 13824 x 5120 | 0.986707 | 0.992927 | 0.992927 | 0.999192 |
| 9450 x 5120 x 13824 | 0.986700 | 0.992928 | 0.992926 | 0.999191 |

### A6W6 base-versus-head regression check

The shared MXFP6 quantization path was compared against benchmark base
`49c6fdd4558a45b2cd34e713b74d0280a2a61c88` (main at the time of measurement)
on the same GPU over all 57 shapes from
`a6w6_blockscale_untuned_gemm.csv`.

The protocol used three independent base and head sweeps per backend, each with
30 warmups, 100 iterations, and 15 alternating repeats. Unchanged GEMM-only
latency was the clock/contention control; a sweep sample was discarded only
when that control was more than 2% above the revision's fastest sample.

| Backend | Metric | Geomean delta | Median delta | P95 delta | Range | Shapes >1% |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| HIP | GEMM-only control | -0.023% | -0.021% | +0.572% | -1.059% to +0.677% | 0 / 57 |
| HIP | Quantize + GEMM | +0.181% | +0.138% | +0.815% | -0.886% to +0.949% | 0 / 57 |
| Triton | GEMM-only control | +0.011% | +0.030% | +0.410% | -0.507% to +0.452% | 0 / 57 |
| Triton | Quantize + GEMM | +0.045% | +0.078% | +0.461% | -0.790% to +0.744% | 0 / 57 |

All 57 base/head kernel selections matched.

The Triton figures measure the unchanged private legacy packer as a parity and
performance control. Production gfx950 dispatch uses the full-range HIP
packer.

## Test plan and results

- Clean-cache JIT builds pass for `module_quant`, `module_gemm_a6w4_asm`, and
  `module_gemm_a4w6_asm`.
- 96 focused mixed-MXFP operator tests pass on gfx950.
- 102 fast tuning/configuration tests pass.
- `mp=1` and an explicit two-GPU tuner pipeline pass for both operand orders.
- Tuned `--run_config` validation passes 57/57 shapes for each format.
- The A6W4/A4W6 test files follow
  `.claude/skills/aiter-op-test/SKILL.md`: `@benchmark`, candidate dictionaries,
  `run_perftest`, `checkAllclose`, us/TFLOPS/TB/s/err columns, standard CLI
  sweeps, and markdown summary tables.
- Fast deterministic tuning validation is included in normal PR test sharding.
  Long-running tuner pipeline and all-shape run-config tests remain
  scheduled/manual.
- Quantized-reference checks cover production projection shapes, simultaneous
  M/N/K tails, and every MXFP4 scale-round mode.
- Every retained MFMA32 variant is bitwise checked on simultaneous M/N/K
  padding; grouped and long-K dispatch paths are also exercised.
- Dynamic quantize-to-GEMM paths pass `torch.compile(dynamic=True,
  fullgraph=True)`, including exact and padded tuning-table matches.
- ctypes validation rejects undersized, oversized, and misaligned packed
  buffers.
- Manifest tests enforce exact manifest/directory membership, AITER-mangled
  symbols, layout metadata, ELF format, and tuned-kernel membership.
- Python formatting, Ruff, shell syntax, whitespace, and lint checks pass.

Focused command:

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 AITER_MXFP6_QUANT_BACKEND=hip \
python -m pytest -q \
  op_tests/test_mixed_mxfp_manifests.py \
  op_tests/test_quant_mxfp6_gemm.py \
  op_tests/test_quant_mxfp4_gemm_fused.py \
  op_tests/test_gemm_a6w4.py \
  op_tests/test_gemm_a4w6.py
```

The standard operator benchmark tables are emitted by:

```bash
python op_tests/test_gemm_a6w4.py
python op_tests/test_gemm_a4w6.py
```

The cross-format comparison can be reproduced with:

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 AITER_MXFP6_QUANT_BACKEND=hip \
python op_tests/op_benchmarks/hip/bench_gemm_mixed_mxfp.py \
  --output /tmp/mixed_mxfp.csv
```

## Downstream integration and relationship to #5358

[xDiT](https://github.com/xdit-project/xDiT) is the planned first downstream
consumer. Its downstream PR will follow after this AITER API lands. The
integration under development uses the public `gemm_a6w4` / `gemm_a4w6` APIs,
prepares packed weights during model setup, packs activations dynamically, and
shares one MXFP6 activation pack across Wan QKV/KV projections.

[#5358](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5358) is an independent FlyDSL W4
backend:

- This PR uses the H32-rotated A6W6 packed ABI and additionally provides A4W6.
- #5358 uses an unrotated, FP8-padded FP6 activation layout.
- The public APIs, packed buffers, dispatch, and tuning namespaces are
  distinct and cannot be substituted without repacking.
- This ASM backend uses `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A6W4_ASM` and
  `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A4W6_ASM`; the FlyDSL backend uses
  `AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A6W4`.

## JIT behavior

`develop=True` on the fused packer binding does not disable persistent JIT
caching. Module resolution and reuse occur before that branch. It enables the
torch-free `aiter_tensor_t` conversion, pybind ABI validation, and current HIP
stream handoff required by `module_quant`, matching the existing MXFP6 binding.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Kimi-K3][ROCm] Add merged MoE front
body:
## Summary

Adds a merged MoE-front kernel for Kimi-K3 on gfx950, plus tuned GEMM
configurations and numerical tests for it.

Kimi-K3's MoE front is three separate projections of the same `x[M, 7168]`:
shared gate/up `7168 -> 1536`, router logits `7168 -> 896`, and the routed
latent `7168 -> 3584`. This kernel combines them into one
`BF16 x BF16 -> FP32` GEMM (`7168 -> 6016`) followed by a Triton split/SiTU
epilogue that emits the BF16 shared SiTU intermediate, the FP32 router logits,
and the BF16 routed latent. Routed experts are untouched and still use the
existing AITER MXFP4 backend.

## Supported shapes

```text
1..16, 32, 48, 64, 80, 96, 112, 128, 192, 512, 1024, 1536, 2048
```

`32..192` is the MTP decode bucket. A pure-decode step submits
`num_seqs * (1 + num_speculative_tokens)` tokens, so with the usual
`num_speculative_tokens=3` any server past four concurrent sequences asks for a
count above 16. The gate itself lives in the companion vLLM change; what this
PR adds for those shapes is numerical coverage, since the decode test
previously stopped at `m=16`.

`kimik3_bf16_tuned_gemm.csv` gains FP32-output entries at `N=6016, K=7168,
gfx950, cu_num=256` for `M = 7, 14, 16, 512, 1024, 1536, 2048`. Config lookup
is keyed on output dtype and pads `M` up to the next multiple of 16 below 256,
so every `M` in `1..16` resolves to the `M=16` entry. The `32..192` bucket has
no FP32-output entry yet and therefore runs on torch's default hipBLASLt
heuristic; the end-to-end numbers below already include that fallback, so
tuning those shapes is remaining headroom rather than a prerequisite.

`M=4096` and `M=8192` are intentionally excluded after controlled retesting
showed regressions.

## Kernel results

Single-GPU gfx950, complete front, CUDA Graph:

| M | Speedup vs native front |
|---|---:|
| 1..16 | 1.645x – 2.140x |
| 512 | 1.224x |
| 1024 | 1.185x |
| 1536 | 1.162x |
| 2048 | 1.129x |
| 4096 | 0.960x, excluded |
| 8192 | 0.882x, excluded |

All tested shapes pass numerical checks, including exact router top-16
selection.

## End-to-end results

MI355X, TP8, DSpark MTP (`num_speculative_tokens=3`), via the companion vLLM
change. Both arms of each comparison ran back to back on one node with
identical server arguments, KV configuration and client invocation.

### 8K/1K fixed sequence length

ISL 8192, OSL 1024, prefix caching disabled, 610 requests per arm, zero
failures.

| Concurrency | Decode M | Output throughput | Median TPOT |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| 1 | 4 | 130.1 -> 135.9 tok/s, **+4.43%** | 7.15 -> 6.83 ms, **-4.53%** |
| 4 | 16 | 369.9 -> 380.5 tok/s, **+2.87%** | 9.25 -> 8.97 ms, **-2.98%** |
| 8 | 32 | 582.8 -> 606.5 tok/s, **+4.07%** | 11.99 -> 11.31 ms, **-5.66%** |
| 16 | 64 | 799.8 -> 814.3 tok/s, **+1.82%** | 18.00 -> 17.65 ms, **-1.98%** |
| 32 | 128 | 1030.2 -> 1044.7 tok/s, **+1.41%** | 28.95 -> 28.55 ms, **-1.37%** |

Median TTFT moves by at most 0.58% in any cell: prefill in this workload is
8130-8190 tokens per step and never matches a supported shape, so the gain is
decode-only. Repeating two of these rows independently bounds their
reproducibility at 0.13-0.80 pp.

### AgenticX trace replay, 3600 s per cell

| Metric | C1 | C4 |
|---|---|---|
| Total throughput | 10212 -> 10533 tok/s, **+3.14%** | 19211 -> 19617 tok/s, **+2.11%** |
| Output throughput | 84.77 -> 87.75 tok/s, **+3.52%** | 139.20 -> 146.61 tok/s, **+5.33%** |
| P90 TPOT | 8.92 -> 8.47 ms, **-5.03%** | 13.52 -> 13.36 ms, **-1.19%** |
| P90 interactivity | 112.1 -> 118.1 tok/s, **+5.29%** | 73.9 -> 74.8 tok/s, **+1.20%** |

Read the total-throughput row with care: it does not measure this change.
Input tokens are over 99% of all tokens in this trace and 97.6% of them hit the
prefix cache, so total throughput is close to (input tokens handed to this arm)
/ wall clock. Trace replay assigns sessions dynamically and the two arms did
not get an identical token mix -- the optimized arm received 3.04% more input
tokens at C1 and 2.81% more at C4. Dividing the measured total-throughput delta
by each arm's input-token and duration ratio leaves a residual of +0.00% at C1
and +0.02% at C4, so that row is token mix and nothing else.

Output throughput and P90 TPOT are the rows that carry the effect: both are
normalized per output token, so neither depends on how much input the arm
happened to receive. Note that they disagree in shape with the total row at C4,
where output throughput is +5.33% against a total of +2.11% -- the smaller
number there is the noisier one, not the more conservative one.

## Accuracy

GSM8K, full 1319-question test split, 5-shot, greedy. This is the check the
numerical tests structurally cannot make: they compare the fused kernel against
a `torch.mm` reference built from the same merged weight, so they are blind to
the merged front slicing its router logits out of a `7168 -> 6016` accumulator
where the native front runs a separate `7168 -> 896` GEMM. Both are
BF16 x BF16 -> FP32, but the wider shape picks a different solution with a
different accumulation order, and that rounding difference can flip a borderline
top-16 expert selection.

Both arms ran back to back on one node at `max_num_seqs=8` with
`num_speculative_tokens=3` and block rejection sampling, so a saturated decode
step submits 32 tokens and the merged front is the decode path for effectively
the whole run.

| Filter | Baseline | Merged |
|---|---:|---:|
| strict-match | 0.9659 | 0.9719 |
| flexible-extract | 0.9651 | 0.9712 |

Both arms answer the same questions, so the paired view is the informative one:
1295 of 1319 answers agree, 16 flip to correct and 8 flip to incorrect, an exact
two-sided sign test on the 24 discordant pairs giving p = 0.15. The merged front
is therefore indistinguishable from the native front on accuracy. The +0.6 pp is
run-to-run nondeterminism, not a claimed improvement.


## Validation

- Ruff (`ruff==0.16.0`, the version `pre-checks.yaml` pins), `ruff format` and
  `git diff --check`: passed. The two `EXE001` findings that remain in the
  repository are in unrelated flydsl files and predate this PR.
- gfx950 AITER tests: `17 passed`.
- Dependent vLLM Kimi-K3 tests: `59 passed`.

Companion vLLM PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55811

title: [Triton/Gluon] [GFX950] Keep unified-attention block-table stride runtime
body:
## Summary

- Remove `block_table_stride` from compile-time `AttentionConfig`.
- Pass the stride as runtime `tl.int32` state through both gfx950 Gluon KV loaders.
- Keep the allocated-once KV-cache layout strides as `constexpr`.
- Keep the diff code-only, without adding to CI runtime.

## Root cause

SGLang serving can produce padded block tables with different row strides across batches. The gfx950 Gluon kernel stored `block_table_stride` in `AttentionConfig`, making every new stride part of the JIT compile key.

A matched serving profile observed seven Gluon compilations inside the measured request, adding 5.75 seconds of gaps immediately before unified-attention launches even though the compiled Gluon kernels themselves were faster than the Triton kernels.

The stride is bounded by the per-request block-table width, so runtime `tl.int32` is sufficient. `AsyncKVLoader` and `AsyncGatherKVLoader` now receive it as runtime state. The gather loader explicitly narrows its clamped block-table indices to `gl.int32`, as required by the CDNA buffer-load interface.

## Validation

### Changing-stride probe

The same logical page table was invoked with seven padded strides from 60000 through 60511.

| Measurement | Compile-time stride | Runtime `tl.int32` stride |
|---|---:|---:|
| Cold total | 5,858.85 ms | 2,371.42 ms |
| Cached total | 330.66 ms | 332.07 ms |
| Compile-like cold calls | 7 | 2 |
| Finite-output failures | 0 | 0 |
| Maximum output difference | — | `6.11e-5` |

The initial variants are bounded; subsequent changing stride values no longer create a new binary.

### Loader coverage

External focused validation exercised changing padded widths through:

- `AsyncGatherKVLoader` with block size 1.
- `AsyncKVLoader` with block size 64.

Both paths remained finite and produced identical outputs across the tested widths.

### Matched serving profile

The same 60K-input, 128-output, concurrency-4 profile was run before and after the change.

| Metric | Compile-time stride | Runtime `tl.int32` stride |
|---|---:|---:|
| Successful requests | 8/8 | 8/8 |
| Benchmark duration | 130.37 s | 108.31 s |
| Input throughput | 3,681.93 tok/s | 4,431.69 tok/s |
| Output throughput | 7.85 tok/s | 9.45 tok/s |
| Main-run Gluon compilations | 7 | 0 |
| Prefill gaps | 5,724.51 ms | 31.22 ms |
| Decode gaps | 8.08 ms | 8.04 ms |

This is a 20.4% input-throughput recovery and a 16.9% duration reduction, with no main-run compilation left in the trace.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m py_compile aiter/ops/triton/_gluon_kernels/gfx950/attention/unified_attention.py`
- [x] Ruff check and format check.
- [x] Seven-width compile/cache probe.
- [x] Direct and gather KV-loader output comparison.
- [x] Matched serving profile with trace inspection.
- [ ] Upstream CI.

title: [Triton/Gluon] Add gluon support for MXFP4 and MXFP8 quant kernel in gfx1250
[HIP] [Bugfix] paged_attention_ragged: scale FP8 softmax probabilities into the e4m3 normal range
body:
## Summary

On the FP8 KV-cache path, `paged_attention_ragged` normalizes the softmax
probabilities to sum = 1 within a partition and *then* casts them to
`fp8_e4m3` for the PV MFMA. With the default `partition_size = 256` and a
typical near-uniform attention distribution, every probability lands at ≈2⁻⁸ —
**subnormal in e4m3** (min normal 2⁻⁶, subnormal step 2⁻⁹), where the relative
ulp is ½. The result is ~15% RMS error on `P`, which propagates 1:1 to the
attention output.

The BF16 path does not have this problem, and **aiter's own Gluon paged-decode
kernel already implements the fix**.

## Reproduction

aiter's only FP8-KV test for this op fails on a stock image:

```console
$ python3 -m pytest op_tests/test_pa_ragged.py -k fp8_kv_nhd -x -q
FAILED op_tests/test_pa_ragged.py::test_paged_attention_ragged_glm_gqa_fp8_kv_nhd
1 failed, 13824 deselected, 2 warnings in 19.52s

Greatest relative difference: 0.355 (up to 0.03 allowed)
```

Environment: MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.0, torch 2.9.0a0, image
`lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.19-rocm700-mi35x-20260910` + aiter
`4ad99832823dde2315b361cbd3b54b1c5c12acd5`.

That test uses head_size 128, 8 KV heads, seq_len **128** — a single partition —
and it *barely* fails (3 of 24576 elements). At realistic decode contexts the
mechanism is pervasive. Measured against an fp32 PyTorch reference at
head_dim 256, 1 KV head, 4 query heads, context 8192 (32 partitions):

| KV cache | `kv_cache_dtype` | mean relative error |
|---|---|---|
| bf16 | `"auto"` | **0.0032** |
| fp8_e4m3fn | `"fp8_e4m3"` | **0.1422** |

Error is flat in context length (0.140 / 0.147 / 0.149 at ctx 256 / 1024 / 4096)
— consistent with per-token independent rounding rather than an accumulation
problem — and identical for `"NHD"` and `"HND"`, so it is not a layout issue.

## Root cause

`csrc/cpp_itfs/pa/pa_kernels.cuh`:

* **`:586-588`** — `inv_sum_scale = 1/(partition_exp_sum + 1e-6) * exp(warp_max - partition_max)`.
  `P` is fully normalized to sum 1.
* **`:633-647`** — `d_out *= inv_sum_scale`, then
  `__builtin_amdgcn_cvt_pk_fp8_f32(...)`. The **already-normalized** `P` is cast
  to e4m3.
* **`:794`** — `gcn_mfma16x16x32_instr<__hip_fp8_e4m3, ...>` consumes it.
* **`:596-621`** — the `kAuto`/bf16 branch keeps `P` in bf16, which represents
  2⁻⁸ exactly. Hence the 0.3% agreement there.

`Q` is also cast to fp8 on this path (`:379-409`), contributing a further ~0.7%.

At `partition_size = 256`, **100% of P values measured fall in the e4m3
subnormal range**, with RMS relative rounding error 0.163 — matching the observed
0.153. Raising `partition_size` to 512 (p ≈ 2⁻⁹) drives the error to **1.04**,
which is the predicted behaviour if this diagnosis is right.

### Attribution, by emulation

A partition-aware fp32 model with each rounding step toggled independently
(ctx 2048, partition 256; shipped kernel vs exact = 0.1534):

| emulated model | kernel-vs-model | model-vs-exact |
|---|---|---|
| exact fp32 | 0.1534 | 0.0000 |
| + bf16 partial writeback | 0.1534 | 0.0017 |
| + fp8 Q only | 0.1528 | 0.0070 |
| + fp8 P only | 0.0468 | 0.1523 |
| **+ fp8 Q and fp8 P** | **0.0014** | **0.1534** |

Adding only the two fp8 casts reproduces the shipped kernel to 0.14%.

## Fix (implemented and validated)

Normalize `P` by the partition **max** rather than the sum — putting the largest
value inside the e4m3 normal range — and fold `1/exp_sum` into the fp32 output
after the MFMA. Same instruction count, same MFMA, no extra memory traffic.

`upstream/aiter-pa-ragged-fp8-fix.patch` (54 insertions in `pa_kernels.cuh`)
splits `inv_sum_scale` into a pre-cast and a post-MFMA factor inside the existing
`if constexpr(KV_DTYPE != kAuto)` branches, so the BF16 path is untouched. The
scale is the largest **power of two** inside the normal range (256 on gfx950,
128 on gfx942 where e4m3 is fnuz) rather than the range maximum: a power of two
is exact in binary, so the rescale introduces no rounding of its own and cannot
push the cast into saturation. The two factors multiply back to `inv_sum_scale`
exactly, so the result is unchanged in exact arithmetic — only the rounding
improves.

Only `_paged_attention_kernel` needs it. `_paged_attention_kernel_EXPERIMENTAL`
shares the pattern but is bf16-only (`pa_ragged.py:32` requires
`kv_dtype == "__hip_bfloat16"`), so it never reaches the fp8 branch.

### Validation

MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.0, same container before and after:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `test_paged_attention_ragged_glm_gqa_fp8_kv_nhd` | **FAIL** (rel diff 0.355 vs 0.03) | **PASS** |
| fp8 error vs fp32 reference, bs 1 / 8 / 32 / 64 | 0.1417 / 0.1432 / 0.1420 / 0.1426 | **0.0273 / 0.0277 / 0.0276 / 0.0276** |
| bf16 error, same shapes | 0.00317 / 0.00325 / 0.00322 / 0.00319 | 0.00317 / 0.00325 / 0.00322 / 0.00319 |
| bf16 output checksum | 0.037695 / 0.706248 / 0.237597 / −1.877981 | **bit-identical** |
| fp8 kernel time (µs) | 13.49 / 14.57 / 35.36 / 59.68 | 13.51 / 14.58 / 35.65 / 59.50 |
| bf16 kernel time (µs) | 14.82 / 20.21 / 62.96 / 137.99 | 14.82 / 20.26 / 62.82 / 138.03 |

**5.2× error reduction, timing neutral to within noise, BF16 bit-identical.**
Broader regression: 192 passed / 0 failed on a BF16 slice of
`test_pa_ragged.py`. Harness: `notes/pa_fix_validate.py`.

The residual 0.0277 is expected and is not this defect — the KV cache is
genuinely fp8, and Q is also cast to fp8 for the QK MFMA (`:379-409`), which the
emulation attributed ~0.007 to. Both are deliberate design choices, unlike the
subnormal P.

This is what aiter's own Gluon kernel does, so the approach is already
established in-tree —
`aiter/ops/triton/gluon/pa_decode_gluon.py`:

* **`:918`** keeps `attention_probs = exp2(qk - max)` unnormalized
* **`:943`** multiplies by `FP8_MAX_VALUE` (448) before the cast, with a
  compensating `probability_scale` at **`:944` / `:975`**
* **`:990`** applies `1/exp_sums` only after the MFMA
* **`:933`**, in as many words: *"Scale the maximum value of value_scale to
  FP8_MAX_VALUE to improve the precision of P * V."*

## Test coverage gap

`op_tests/test_pa_ragged.py:686-688` — the main parametrized `test_paged_attention`
**skips every quantized-cache case** for the `Shomy` variant, so
`paged_attention_ragged` has no FP8-KV coverage in the main matrix. The single
dedicated test at `:452-514` uses `rtol = atol = 3e-2`, head_size 128, seq_len
128, and never exercises a multi-partition context or head_dim 256.

Suggest extending it to cover multi-partition contexts (≥ 1024 tokens) and
head_dim 256, which is where the defect is largest.

## Impact

`paged_attention_ragged` is the decode attention op SGLang's aiter backend calls
for non-MLA models on ROCm
(`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py:3312`), and
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` is a common production setting. Any deployment
combining the two is running decode attention with ~15% error on the attention
probabilities.

I have not measured downstream task-accuracy impact — softmax outputs are
averages over many values and the error is zero-mean, so end-to-end damage may
be much smaller than the per-tensor number suggests. The kernel-level error is
nonetheless far outside the op's own stated tolerance.

title: [Triton/Gluon] Fused Qwen3-Next GDN decode op for gfx950
body:
# [Triton/Gluon] Fused Qwen3-Next GDN decode op for gfx950

## Motivation

Qwen3-Next's Gated DeltaNet decode step runs as four separate kernels today:

```
fused_qkvzba_split_reshape_cat  ->  causal_conv1d_update
  ->  fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode  ->  gated RMSNorm
```

aiter has all the pieces for GDN — `chunk_gated_delta_rule`,
`fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule`, `causal_conv1d_update_split_qkv`,
`gated_rmsnorm_fp8_group_quant` — but **not the single-launch fusion**, and not
one that consumes the packed `qkvz`/`ba` projections directly.

This adds that op. On 4x MI355X / TP4 with Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 it is
worth **+6.0% to +9.1% end-to-end output throughput** when wired into SGLang
(companion PR), with no accuracy regression.

### Why a new op rather than a mode on `fused_kda_decode`

`fused_kda_decode` is the same *shape* of fusion — conv, recurrence, gated norm,
one launch — but it implements **KDA**, and the differences are structural, not
parametric:

| | `fused_kda_decode` | this op |
|---|---|---|
| head topology | one `H`; q/k/v all `H` heads | `VH == 2*KH` |
| gate | `lower_bound * sigmoid(exp(A)*(a+dt))`, vector over K | `exp(-exp(A_log)*softplus(a+dt))`, scalar per head |
| output gate | `sigmoid(z)` | `z * sigmoid(z)` (SiLU) |
| conv bias | none | seeds the accumulator |
| input | pre-split `mixed_qkv`/`gate`/`beta` | packed `qkvz`/`ba`, split internally |

The head topology alone settles it: KDA's `lp = H*K`, `q_off = i_h*K`,
`v_off = 2*lp + i_h*V` offsets cannot express `VH = 2*KH`. A mode flag would
double an existing kernel's branch factor to host a different algorithm, so this
ships as a sibling instead. `fused_kda_decode` is not exported from
`gated_delta_net/__init__.py`, so no existing interface is perturbed.

## Modifications

New:
  * `aiter/ops/triton/_gluon_kernels/gfx950/gated_delta_net/fused_gdn_decode_qkvz.py`                            
    — the Gluon kernels. Two decompositions behind one entry point:                                              
    * **batch < 128** — `_fused_decode` / `_fused_decode_tiled`. One eight-wave                                  
      workgroup owns a token/key-head group's convolution history and both FP32                                  
      value-head states, with prefetch and tiling to hide memory latency while                                   
      the machine is under-occupied.                                                                             
    * **batch >= 128** — `_decode_group`, which keeps the whole `[V, K]` state                                   
      tile in registers across both matrix-vector products. Above that threshold                                 
      the kernel is bandwidth-bound, where the latency-hiding machinery stops                                    
      paying and the simpler traffic pattern reaches a better fraction of peak.                                  
                                                                                                                 
    Selection is a **range check, not a shape table**, so every batch size is                                    
    covered.  
* `aiter/ops/triton/gated_delta_net/fused_gdn_decode_qkvz.py` — public wrapper,
  shape/dtype validation and the support predicate.
* `op_tests/triton_tests/test_fused_gdn_decode_qkvz.py` — a pure-torch fp32
  reference plus correctness, pad-slot, bf16-only and determinism tests.
* `op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_fused_gdn_decode_qkvz.py` — bandwidth and
  roofline sweep.

Modified:
* `aiter/ops/triton/gated_delta_net/__init__.py` — export the op and its
  predicate.

### What it fuses

1. unpack packed `projected_qkvz` -> Q/K/V/Z and `projected_ba` -> b/a
2. depthwise causal conv1d against the rolling window, **with bias**, + SiLU
3. delta-rule gating, `decay = exp(-exp(A_log) * softplus(a + dt_bias))`
4. FP32 recurrent state update at `ssm_state[indices]`
5. gated RMSNorm with a SiLU gate
6. *optional* per-head group-128 FP8 quantization

Stage 6 is opt-in via `quant_dtype=`. With `None` the op returns bf16 only,
because an unquantized `Linear` consumer cannot accept an `(fp8, scales)` tuple.

### `pad_slot_id`

Rows whose state index equals `pad_slot_id` (default `-1`) are skipped without
reading or writing state. This matches what the other indexed-state ops in this
directory already do — `fused_conv_recurrent_norm` returns on `state_idx < 0`,
`causal_conv1d_update_split_qkv` takes an explicit `pad_slot_id` — and it is the
contract SGLang's `replay_state_indices_validator` documents. Measured cost:
**0.2-0.3%**, i.e. within noise.

## Scope and supported shapes

Deliberately narrow, and **reported rather than asserted**:
`fused_gdn_decode_qkvz_supported()` returns `(bool, reason)` so callers fall
back and can log why.

* gfx950 only — CDNA buffer addressing, `v_exp_f32`/`v_rcp_f32` inline asm,
  explicit register layouts
* `num_v_heads == 2 * num_k_heads`; `head_k_dim == head_v_dim == 128`
* conv width 4; contiguous conv and recurrent state pools
* bf16 packed projections / conv weight / conv bias / `dt_bias` / `norm_weight`;
  fp32 `A_log` and `ssm_state`; int32 state indices
* fp8 output, when requested, is `e4m3fn` or `e4m3fnuz`

**No CUDA path is affected.** The op is reachable only through its own module,
and every caller is expected to gate on the predicate.

## Accuracy Tests

`pytest op_tests/triton_tests/test_fused_gdn_decode_qkvz.py` — **22 passed** on
MI355X / ROCm 7.0 / Triton 3.8.

* `test_fused_gdn_decode_correctness` at batch 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 —
  output, scales, and both mutated state pools against the fp32 reference at
  ATOL/RTOL 0.05, the bar this directory already uses for `fused_kda_decode`.
* `test_fused_gdn_decode_pad_slot` — `PAD_SLOT_ID` rows leave `ssm_state` and
  `conv_state` bit-unchanged.
* `test_fused_gdn_decode_bf16_only` — `quant_dtype=None` returns `(out, None, None)`.
* `test_fused_gdn_decode_determinism` — same inputs twice, bit-identical.
* Eleven reference-only tests pin the packed layout, gate algebra and quant
  round-trip independently of the kernel.

The reference itself was validated before being trusted: run against **seven
independent implementations of this kernel across nine batch sizes**, it agrees
on every one, and `conv_state` matches **bit-exactly** on all 63 combinations.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Hardware: 4x AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), TP4 / EP1.
Image: `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.19-rocm700-mi35x-20260910` (ROCm 7.0,
Triton 3.8.0, torch 2.9). Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8`.

### Kernel level

Per-launch time under **CUDA graph replay** with a fixed 512-slot state pool.
Both matter: timing the Python call instead of the kernel produces a flat ~25 us
floor that is host overhead, and sizing the pool to the batch puts small batches
entirely in cache.

  | batch | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 | 128 | 192 | 256 |                                                     
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|                                                                  
  | this op (us/call) | 9.70 | 9.73 | 9.80 | 10.02 | 9.84 | 10.40 | 14.24 | 26.95 | 36.81 | 46.52 | 

Replaced chain, same conditions, per decode step over 36 GDN layers:
**830.8 us -> 279.2 us (2.98x)** for the four kernels listed in Motivation.

### Roofline

`python3 op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_fused_gdn_decode_qkvz.py`, MI355X
(8.0 TB/s peak HBM). The op performs no MFMA and no `gl.dot`; it is bound by the
FP32 recurrent state, read and written once per token per value head, which
dominates every other tensor by an order of magnitude.

  | batch | 1 | 8 | 32 | 64 | 128 | 192 | 256 |                                                                  
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|                                                                              
  | us/call | 9.39 | 9.69 | 10.40 | 14.24 | 26.95 | 36.81 | 46.52 |                                              
  | TB/s | 0.12 | 0.89 | 3.33 | 4.87 | 5.14 | 5.65 | **5.96** |
  | % peak | 1.4% | 11.2% | 41.6% | 60.8% | 64.3% | 70.6% | **74.5%** |

  Two regimes, and they are why the op carries two decompositions. Up to batch
  ~32 it is **latency-bound** — there is not enough state traffic to fill the
  machine, and time is nearly flat at ~9.4-10.4 us regardless of batch, so
  prefetch and tiling pay. From batch 64 it becomes **bandwidth-bound**, where
  that machinery stops paying and the register-resident tile reaches a better
  fraction of peak: **74.5% at batch 256**.

  A single decomposition plateaued at 5.20 TB/s (65%) there. Three candidate fixes
  were tested and rejected before concluding the gap was structural: extra HBM
  passes (identical byte counts, by source-level count of the state load/stores),
  launch-order locality (rewriting the grid to the other kernel's order gained
  0.75%), and store cache policy (`.cs` to `.wt`, slightly worse). What remains is
  the register layout and reduction structure — a different algorithm, not a
  tuning constant. 

### End to end (companion SGLang PR)

Un-profiled, random dataset ISL/OSL 1024/1024, `num-prompts == max-concurrency`.

| conc | baseline tok/s | with this op | delta | baseline TPOT | with op TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 459.9 | 487.4 | **+6.0%** | 4.27 ms | 4.03 ms |
| 8 | 3072.1 | 3262.3 | **+6.2%** | 5.07 ms | 4.76 ms |
| 32 | 8858.2 | 9666.3 | **+9.1%** | 6.86 ms | 6.26 ms |
| 64 | 13974.7 | 15109.6 | **+8.1%** | 8.60 ms | 7.91 ms |

GSM8K 1319q: 0.941 baseline vs 0.941 with the op, `Invalid: 0.000` on both.

  ### End to end at a raised graph cap

  The large-batch band only fires above batch 128, which requires
  `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode` above its default of 64. At a cap of 256, two arms
  on the same base, un-profiled:                         

  | conc | baseline tok/s | with this op | delta | baseline TPOT | with op TPOT |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|                              
  | 128 | 21528.0 | 22596.2 | **+5.0%** | 11.00 ms | 10.43 ms |
  | 256 | 30926.3 | 32276.3 | **+4.4%** | 14.97 ms | 14.29 ms |

## Reproduction

```bash
docker run --rm -it --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri --network host \
  --group-add video --ipc host --shm-size 32g \
  -v $HF_HOME:/hf lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.19-rocm700-mi35x-20260910

pytest op_tests/triton_tests/test_fused_gdn_decode_qkvz.py -q
```

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added, mirroring the op tree (`op_tests/triton_tests/`)
- [x] `black` / `ruff` clean
- [x] DCO sign-off on every commit
- [x] gfx950-gated; no CUDA path affected
- [x] Benchmark (`op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_fused_gdn_decode_qkvz.py`)
