title: [Triton/Gluon] [FlyDSL] [CI] feat(flydsl): Add paged-attention Tile kernel
body:
## Motivation

Add a FlyDSL paged-attention decode implementation to AITER for FP8 KV caches.

The kernel provides explicit control over MFMA execution, KV-page loading, LDS
layout, softmax, partition scheduling, and native FlyDSL partition reduction.

## Technical Details

- Add FlyDSL paged-attention decode under `aiter.ops.flydsl`.
- Support:
  - FP8 K/V caches
  - BF16/FP16 queries
  - Block sizes 16, 64, and 128
  - Per-tensor and per-token KV scales
  - GQA and multi-token prediction
  - Plain and transposed V-cache layouts
- Process context in 256-token tiles using four wave64 waves per CTA.
- Use wide K=128 FP8 MFMA for the tuned MTP3/MTP4 gfx950 path.
- Split small MTP2/MTP4 grids into one query per CTA; keep larger grids and
  MTP3 fused to share KV/scales.
- Select the single-M per-token V-prefetch pipeline from one layout/workgroup
  policy; static Hkv2 uses the tuned path while high-grid page128 transposed V
  retains the lower-register schedule.
- Support explicit partition counts up to 256 and a caller-configurable clamp for
  automatic partition selection.
- Use the native FlyDSL reducer for partition outputs.

## Test Plan

`op_tests/test_flydsl_pa_decode.py` has one generic parametrized pytest function
with 14 real-kernel/reference configurations covering QL1/2/3/4, page16/64/128,
plain/transposed V, BF16/FP16, scalar/per-token scales, automatic/explicit
partitions, Hkv2 prefetch policy boundaries, C200k, and a BS200 smoke case. The
same file also covers dynamic planning, graph replay, high-partition reducers,
and provides a direct correctness + performance CLI for larger sweeps.

```bash
pytest -q op_tests/test_flydsl_pa_decode.py

HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=5 python3 op_tests/test_flydsl_pa_decode.py \
  -d bf16 -b 200 -q 4 -s 16,1,128,200000 \
  --block-size 16 128 --trans-v 0 1 --per-token 1
```

Latest MI355 validation:

```text
285 passed in 190.50s
```

Black, Ruff, Python syntax, Bash syntax, and `git diff --check` also pass.

## Performance

### Earlier representative cases

MI355/gfx950 CUDA Graph end-to-end latency, including compute and reduce:

| Case | Block size | PA Tile | PA Gluon | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| small | 16 | 11.79 us | 12.24 us | 1.04x |
| small | 64 | 11.75 us | 12.07 us | 1.03x |
| batch | 16 | 14.20 us | 20.43 us | 1.44x |
| batch | 64 | 13.76 us | 20.32 us | 1.48x |
| MTP3 | 16 | 22.90 us | 41.52 us | 1.81x |
| MTP3 | 64 | 22.81 us | 41.08 us | 1.80x |
| MTP4-var | 16 | 28.72 us | 38.14 us | 1.33x |
| MTP4-var | 64 | 23.91 us | 38.53 us | 1.61x |
| long | 16 | 35.93 us | 43.69 us | 1.22x |
| long | 64 | 35.24 us | 43.52 us | 1.23x |

PA Tile wins all 10 cases with a 1.37x geometric-mean speedup. Workloads use
Hkv=1, head dimension 128, and transposed V. `small` is B3/Hq8/Q1/C1027
per-tensor; `batch` is B81/Hq8/Q1/C1027 per-tensor; `MTP3` is
B81/Hq16/Q3/C1027 per-token; `MTP4-var` is B81/Hq16/Q4/C1027 per-token with
variable KV lengths; and `long` is B81/Hq16/Q1/C8192 per-token.

### MI355: BS=200, MTP4, C=200k

Measured on MI355 (`gfx950`, 256 CUs) with `QL=4`, `Hq/Hkv=16/1`, `D=128`,
BF16 Q/O, FP8 E4M3FN KV, FP32 per-token KV scales, dense attention, and the
native FlyDSL reducer. Each value is the median of three `perftest` profiler
means (101 iterations, 2 warmups). Bandwidth is decimal logical TB/s; KV and
scales are counted once per PA call, not multiplied by MTP4.

#### Equal-length context, backend auto NP

Every sequence has context length 200,000. FlyDSL and Gluon use the same input,
block table, and reference within each row. Each backend uses its own automatic
partition selection: FlyDSL chooses NP8 for page16 and NP4 for page128, while
Gluon chooses NP3.

| Page | V layout | FlyDSL auto NP | FlyDSL us | FlyDSL TB/s | Gluon auto NP | Gluon us | Gluon TB/s | Speedup | `.005` |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 16 | rank-4 | 8 | 2409.320 | 4.3898 | 3 | 6751.326 | 1.5666 | **2.8022x** | PASS |
| 16 | trans-V | 8 | 2372.853 | 4.4573 | 3 | 6719.592 | 1.5740 | **2.8319x** | PASS |
| 128 | rank-4 | 4 | 2387.181 | 4.4269 | 3 | 6441.091 | 1.6407 | **2.6982x** | PASS |
| 128 | trans-V | 4 | 3415.613 | 3.0940 | 3 | 6309.910 | 1.6748 | **1.8474x** | PASS |

For page128 rank-4 V, a separate controlled FlyDSL NP3/4/5/8 tuning sweep
measured 3.4866/4.4269/5.1639/4.4958 TB/s. Explicit NP5 is faster than auto
NP4 for that layout, but it is a manual tuning result and is not used in the
auto-NP comparison table above.

The earlier page-16 variable-length measurements showed 2.1779x (rank-4 V) and
2.1964x (trans-V) speedups, but both implementations failed the additional
strict `.005` check against the reference and also failed their mutual `.005`
comparison. Those rows are excluded from the performance claims above. Their
total context was 19,500,374 tokens, versus 40,000,000 for the equal-length rows.

title: [Triton/Gluon] Add 3D neighborhood flash attention (na3d_flash)
body:
## Motivation

Video diffusion models such as LTX-2.5 use 3D neighborhood attention in
the VAE diffusion decoder: each token at grid position (t, h, w) attends
only to its (KT x KH x KW) neighbors rather than the full sequence. This
PR adds a BF16 MFMA flash-style kernel for that operation targeting gfx942
and gfx950, plus a reference, tests and benchmarks.

**Use case example**
LTX-2.5 Diffusion decoder attention processor [in xDiT](https://github.com/xdit-project/xDiT/pull/773) inference framework.

## Technical Details

Six new files:

**`aiter/ops/triton/_triton_kernels/attention/na3d_flash.py`**

`_na3d_flash_fwd`:  flash attention inner kernel.
- Inward border-shift: every window contains exactly KT x KH x KW keys
- Q loaded once into registers; K/V iterated over KT x KH rows
- Online softmax in log2 space (exp2, log2(e) folded into scale factor)
- Flat KT x KH loop with static trip count enables Triton's software pipeliner

**`aiter/ops/triton/attention/na3d_flash.py`**

`na3d_flash_attn(q, k, v, kernel_size)` -
public launcher. Input/output shape: (B, T, H, W, NH, HD) bfloat16,
Q pre-scaled by head_dim**-0.5.
Tuned configs provided for gfx950/gfx942 for ltx-2.5 model default shapes.

**`aiter/op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_na3d_flash.py`**

- `_na3d_sdpa_exact(q, k, v, kernel_size, w_offset=0)` - Reference method. Exact per-query
neighborhood SDPA. Groups queries by shared relative-window geometry and
calls `F.scaled_dot_product_attention` per group with a cached additive mask.
With w_offset=0 and full q/k/v this is equivalent to a per-query FP32
reference but runs on the GPU. With w_offset>0, q is a W sub-slice and
k/v are the full tensors; neighborhood bounds use global W coordinates.

- `test_na3d_flash`: 9 shapes (5 LTX-2.5 default + 5 edge cases); reference
  is `_na3d_sdpa_exact`, atol=5e-2
- `test_na3d_sdpa_exact_vs_ref`: 6 small shapes; cross-checks `_na3d_sdpa_exact`
  against the FP32 per-query loop

**`op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_na3d_flash.py`**
- Performance benchmark for 3D neighborhood flash attention (na3d_flash) that compares against `_na3d_sdpa_exact` reference method from `aiter/op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_na3d_flash.py`.
- Measures TFLOPS and TB/s per shape

- **`aiter/ops/triton/configs/gfx950/triton/attention/na3d_flash/DEFAULT.json`**: Tuned config for gfx950
- **`aiter/ops/triton/configs/gfx942/triton/attention/na3d_flash/DEFAULT.json`**: Tuned config for gfx942

## Test Plan

Run pytest on gfx950:

    pytest op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_na3d_flash.py -v

## Test Result

All tests pass on gfx950 (MI350X) in ~30 s.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Bugfix] [Perf] Fix non-preshuffle MQA paging and large KV offsets, retune the decode grid, and cut plain-path instruction count
body:
## Summary

Four defects in the paged MQA logits decode path, all silent: no fault, no NaN or Inf, just wrong or missing logits.

The branch has since picked up two pieces of performance work on the same path, both originally reviewed as stacked PRs and now folded in: the decode grid sizing from #5711 and its follow-up, and the two instruction-level changes to the plain kernel from #5700. They are described in their own sections below and neither touches the correctness of the four fixes.

**1. Block paging for non-preshuffled multi-token blocks.** With `Preshuffle=False` and `KVBlockSize > 1` the Gluon kernel used token positions as page-table columns and always read token 0's K values and scale from each physical block. Compact block tables caused illegal memory accesses; padding the table kept the reads in allocated memory but produced incorrect logits. Resolve the physical block with `token_pos // KVBlockSize` and add the in-block token offset to both the K and the scale address, in the initial loads and in the prefetch loop. This fixes the failures reproduced in #5591. Related: #5600.

**2. KV caches past 2 GiB in the plain kernel.** That kernel forms a per-token address from the page table, so `physical_block * stride` overflowed a 32-bit product and wrapped into another page once the cache crossed 2 GiB. Its KV and scale strides are now 64-bit for every shape and the loads go through global pointers. A size-dependent switch between a 32-bit and a 64-bit variant was considered and dropped: it gives one shape two ABIs behind one AOT directory name, and the measured cost of always using 64-bit is bounded (see Performance).

**3. KV caches past 2 GiB in the preshuffle kernel.** When `ChunkKPerStage % KVBlockSize != 0`, which is `KVBlockSize=256` at `ChunkK=256`, the K and scale addresses came from the same 32-bit page-index product. Read them through a global pointer with the index promoted to 64 bits, the way the other branch of that kernel already does.

**4. Preshuffle tail store reaching into the next output row.** The branch that loads a page index per lane stored its last stage across the whole tile, including the columns past `context_length` that hold `-inf`. When the output width equals an unaligned context those columns land in the next row: with `context_lengths=(3001, 513)` and a compact output, row 1 lost its first 7 logits. Those three stores are now bounded by `max_model_len`, which the kernel's six other stores already did.

## Changes

- Correct block-table, K and scale addressing for sectioned, non-preshuffled caches, and keep negative positions in the backward-shifted first tile mapped to token 0 of physical block 0 after masking the page-table load.
- Generate the new address arithmetic only for `KVBlockSize > 1`, preserving the original scalar-first expressions, code generation and register usage for `KVBlockSize=1`.
- Use 64-bit KV and scale strides in the plain kernel unconditionally, and drop the now dead 32-bit load paths.
- Promote the preshuffle per-stage K and scale addresses to 64 bits.
- Bound the preshuffle per-lane stores by `max_model_len`.
- Extend `op_tests/test_pa_mqa_logits_offset.py`: 48 paging cases (block sizes 1/16/64/128, chunks 64/256, compact and padded tables, randomized physical pages, per-token scales, short and empty contexts, MTP, multiple prefetch iterations) and 12 large-offset cases (plain `B1`/`B64` and preshuffle `B64`/`B256`, each at the 2, 4 and 8 GiB boundaries) against an independent FP32 reference, plus the two existing output-offset cases.

Note for AOT users: the plain kernel's stride arguments changed from `i32` to `i64`, its instruction stream changed again with the two optimizations below, and the preshuffle kernel's instruction stream changed, so cached `.hsaco` artifacts have to be regenerated from this branch. The grid change does not add to that — `SplitKV` is a runtime `i32` argument, not a `constexpr`, so it is not part of the compile key.

## Decode grid sizing

`deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` derived `SplitKV` from the batch and rounded **SplitKV** up to a multiple of five, but the thing that has to line up with the CU count is the **grid**, and the two differ by a factor of `TileQCount`. At batch 16/32/64 on 256 CU that landed on 2.5 workgroups per CU, so half the CUs ran three and half ran two and the kernel waited for the deeper half. The grid is now sized directly at two workgroups per CU, clamped so splits that start past the end of the context are not launched.

Two per CU is not enough at the top of the batch range, where each workgroup ends up chewing 128 to 256 chunks with no queue behind it, so a second term raises `SplitKV` toward 32 chunks per workgroup — by at most 2x, because `max_model_len` is only an upper bound on the real context and a loose bound must not be able to over-split without limit.

Scoring each candidate rule by how far its pick sits from the best `SplitKV` measured at each of 42 shapes:

| rule | exact | 4x over-estimate | 16x | 64x |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| the original formula | 7.69% | 7.69% | 7.69% | 7.69% |
| two per CU (context-free) | 0.85% | 0.87% | 0.89% | 0.89% |
| + cap 32 chunks/WG, unbounded | 0.46% | 1.69% | 7.45% | 20.11% |
| **+ cap 32, at most 2x** | **0.56%** | **1.40%** | **2.87%** | **4.08%** |

Against the original formula, at `N=131072`:

| layout | batch | SplitKV | grid | before | after | change |
| --- | ---: | :---: | :---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| plain | 1 | 520→512 | 520→512 | 5.95 | 5.96 | +0.22% |
| plain | 16 | 40→32 | 640→512 | 60.32 | **51.59** | **−14.46%** |
| plain | 64 | 10→16 | 640→1024 | 274.44 | **233.42** | **−14.95%** |
| plain | 128 | 10→8 | 1280→1024 | 469.96 | **456.88** | −2.78% |
| plain | 256 | 10→4 | 2560→1024 | 913.21 | 926.29 | **+1.43%** |
| preshuffle | 16 | 40→32 | 640→512 | 49.54 | **42.65** | **−13.92%** |
| preshuffle | 64 | 10→16 | 640→1024 | 249.40 | **220.28** | **−11.68%** |
| preshuffle | 128 | 10→8 | 1280→1024 | 465.27 | **445.93** | −4.16% |

Over 48 shapes (batch 1..256, context 8k/32k/128k, `next_n` 1 and 2, both layouts) the median is −2.01%, 21 shapes improve by more than 5%, the best is −18.90%, and zero mismatches. Batch 256 at a 128k context is the one shape that stays slower: its grid was already an exact 10 per CU so it never paid the quantisation cost, and its curve is a broad plateau on which the old value sat near the middle. Closing the remaining 1.9% would need the real context length, which lives in a device tensor.

The optional `SplitKV` argument added here is an override in the same spirit as the existing `TotalCuCount`; it is what lets both arms of the measurements come from a single binary. `gfx1250` keeps its own formula, having had no part available to re-tune on.

Correctness for this part: 62 passed, plus a 91-case scan aimed at the split seams — awkward chunk counts, non-uniform context lengths including `(8192, 8191, 1, 256, 257, 255, 65536, 3)` and `(20000, 3001, 513, 131072)`, contexts of length 1 and 2, exact multiples of `ChunkK` and one less, and `KVBlockSize` 1/16/64/256 on both layouts — zero mismatches over the whole output, masked region included.

## Plain-path instruction-level optimizations

Two changes to the `Preshuffle=False` Gluon kernel. Both are unconditional; the shape gate on the first is a correctness condition, not a switch.

**1. Hoist the KV block index and in-block offset out of the loop.** The kernel recomputed `token // KVBlockSize` and `token % KVBlockSize` over a `ChunkK`-wide vector every iteration. `KVBlockSize` is a `constexpr` power of two, so that should be one shift and one AND per register, but it expanded to 64 instructions because `context_idx` is loop-variant and the compiler cannot fold through it. `context_idx` advances by `ChunkK` and the gate requires `ChunkK % KVBlockSize == 0`, so the modulo is loop-invariant and the quotient grows by a constant. The identity does not require `context_idx` to be `KVBlockSize`-aligned, and `KVBlockSize > ChunkK` leaves the quotient without a constant stride, so those shapes keep the general form.

**2. Mask the logits after the head reduce, not before.** The kernel wrote `-inf` into the whole `(ChunkQ, ChunkK)` accumulator before reducing over heads, one `v_cndmask` per accumulator register: 32 in the loop and 32 more in the epilogue. Masking the reduced logits needs four and is the same value, since summing `ChunkQ` copies of `-inf` is `-inf`. The preshuffle kernel already masks after its reduce at all four of its store sites. Removing the `-inf` write also unblocks packed FP32 in the epilogue.

| | in-loop integer address ops | `v_cndmask` | `v_mul_f32` | `v_pk_add_f32` | `v_pk_mul_f32` | `v_pk_fma_f32` | VGPR |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| before | 168 | 98 | 132 | 35 | 0 | 0 | 186 |
| + 1 | **76** | 98 | 132 | 35 | 0 | 0 | 188 |
| + 2 | **76** | **42** | **68** | **18** | **16** | **16** | 190 |

Neither improves register pressure: all three allocate 192 VGPR, so occupancy stays at 2 waves/SIMD.

Measured on top of the grid change above. Three worktrees run back to back inside each round with the arm order rotated, eight rounds; the statistic is the median of the per-round paired ratio, since clocks are not locked here and only pairing cancels the drift. `Preshuffle=True` is untouched by both, so its paired ratio is the noise floor.

| Batch | change 1 | change 2 | both | control (noise floor) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16 | −0.58% | **−2.83%** | **−3.57%** | +0.09% |
| 64 | −0.40% | **−1.02%** | **−1.36%** | +0.01% |
| 128 | −0.12% | **−0.69%** | **−0.80%** | +0.06% |

Change 2 carries almost all of the gain. Change 1 only just clears the noise floor at batch 16 and sits inside it at batch 128; it is worth keeping because it costs nothing and the instruction count genuinely drops, not because it is a measurable speedup on its own. **Batch 1 does not resolve and no claim is made for it**: over 16 paired rounds plain moves −0.97% with an IQR of [−3.08%, +0.28%] while the unchanged control moves +0.61% with an IQR of [−0.75%, +9.18%].

Both sides of the `HoistKvAddr` gate were measured at the same production scale:

| KVBlockSize | ChunkK | gate | b=16 | b=128 |
| ---: | ---: | :---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16 | 256 | on | −2.88% | −0.66% |
| 64 | 256 | on | −3.57% | −0.80% |
| 128 | 256 | on | −3.95% | −0.89% |
| 256 | 256 | on | −5.02% | −1.38% |
| 128 | 64 | **off** | −2.21% | −1.38% |
| 256 | 128 | **off** | −0.58% | −0.35% |
| 1 | 256 | **off** | −2.96% | — |

No shape regresses. The gated-off shapes still gain because change 2 is unconditional. `KVBlockSize=1` takes the branch where the logical index is never computed and `KVBlockSize > ChunkK` takes the branch where it is computed but the hoist is off, so all three paths are exercised; `op_tests/test_pa_mqa_logits_offset.py` already parametrises `block_size ∈ {1, 16, 64, 128} × chunk_k ∈ {64, 256}`, which covers the same split for correctness.

Change 1 is bit-identical to its parent. Change 2 is not, because folding a multiply and an add into `v_pk_fma_f32` skips the rounding of the intermediate product: 410363 of 2097152 logits move by at most `3.05e-05` on a `±273` range. Against an fp64 reference the two are equally far from the truth (mean absolute error `4.615302e-04` before, `4.615247e-04` after, identical maxima), because the error floor is the fp8 quantisation of `q` and `k`, not the fp32 epilogue.

All 430 measurement processes across these campaigns were 0-mismatched against the fp32 reference, with no NaN or Inf.

## Testing

Environment: gfx950 (256 CU), ROCm 7.2.4, PyTorch `2.10.0+rocm7.2.4.git3d3aa833`, Triton 3.7.0, one physical GPU pinned per process, clocks not locked.

```bash
# regression module, JIT gluon kernels
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest -q op_tests/test_pa_mqa_logits_offset.py
# -> 62 passed

# the original #5591 repro, unmodified
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 PYTHONPATH=. python repro_paged_mqa_logits_preshuffle_false.py
# -> [issue2] allclose=True mismatch=0/6000   (was 5968/6000)
# -> [issue1] no illegal access, exit code 0  (was HIP error 700, exit code 1)

# same repro with AOT loading enabled, after regenerating the artifacts
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 AITER_ENABLE_AOT_GLUON_PA_MQA_LOGITS=1 PYTHONPATH=. \
  python repro_paged_mqa_logits_preshuffle_false.py
# -> mismatch=0/6000, no illegal access
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 AITER_ENABLE_AOT_GLUON_PA_MQA_LOGITS=1 PYTHONPATH=. \
  python -m pytest -q op_tests/test_pa_mqa_logits_offset.py
# -> 2 passed, 60 skipped (the JIT-gated cases skip in AOT mode)
```

The repro script is [PR #5591's file at commit `81d4380`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/81d43801111868be953c360bed9ee60c5e193378/tests/repro_paged_mqa_logits_preshuffle_false.py).

Defect 4 was also swept outside pytest with the same shape at cache sizes from 1 MiB to 8 GiB, context pairs `(3001, 513)`, `(3001, 512)`, `(513, 3001)`, `(513, 1025)`, `(3072, 513)` and `(3001,)`, and `TotalCuCount` of 1, 2, 8, 256 and the default: `KVBlockSize=64` and `256` now match the reference everywhere. Before the fix, every case whose first context was not a multiple of the KV block lost the leading logits of the next row.

## Cost of the four fixes

This section predates the two performance sections above and is the cost of the correctness fixes alone, measured before the grid change; its absolutes are not comparable with the numbers there.

Decode, `N=131072`, `H=32`, `D=128`, `next_n=1`, `ChunkK=256`, `WavePerEU=2`, one process per point, median of three, accuracy checked over the whole output on every run.

```bash
# both files in one directory: the fixed test_mqa_logits.py from #5434 (commit
# 849c7c2) for input generation, packing and the FP32 reference, plus the
# driver below
for round in 1 2 3; do
  for batch in 1 16 64 128; do
    for layout in preshuffle plain; do
      ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 PYTHONPATH=. python run_perf.py \
        --batch "$batch" --layout "$layout" --kv-block 64 \
        --output "out/$layout-b$batch-r$round.json"
    done
  done
done
```

Measured on this branch:

| Layout | KVBlock | Batch | KV cache | us | TFLOPS | TB/s | mismatch |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Preshuffle=False | 64 | 1 | 0.02 GiB | 7.258 | 147.9 | 2.457 | 0/131072 |
| Preshuffle=False | 64 | 16 | 0.26 GiB | 58.647 | 292.9 | 4.864 | 0/2097152 |
| Preshuffle=False | 64 | 64 | 1.03 GiB | 274.822 | 250.1 | 4.152 | 0/8388608 |
| Preshuffle=False | 64 | 128 | 2.06 GiB | 470.838 | 291.9 | 4.847 | 0/16777216 |
| Preshuffle=True | 64 | 1 | 0.02 GiB | 5.004 | 214.6 | 3.563 | 0/131072 |
| Preshuffle=True | 64 | 16 | 0.26 GiB | 50.272 | 341.7 | 5.675 | 0/2097152 |
| Preshuffle=True | 64 | 64 | 1.03 GiB | 250.720 | 274.1 | 4.551 | 0/8388608 |
| Preshuffle=True | 64 | 128 | 2.06 GiB | 463.818 | 296.3 | 4.921 | 0/16777216 |
| Preshuffle=True | 256 | 64 | 1.03 GiB | 237.888 | 288.9 | 4.797 | 0/8388608 |
| Preshuffle=True | 256 | 128 | 2.06 GiB | 451.407 | 304.5 | 5.056 | 0/16777216 |

Per-change cost, from paired runs that alternate the two versions within each round. These are deltas only; absolute numbers from different sessions are not comparable, since an unchanged control moved by more than 10% between sessions on this unlocked machine.

Unconditional 64-bit strides in the plain kernel, `KVBlockSize=64`:

| Batch | conditional | unconditional | delta |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 5.728 | 6.677 | +16.55% |
| 16 | 55.701 | 57.955 | +4.05% |
| 64 | 270.004 | 274.738 | +1.75% |
| 128 | 418.183 | 417.427 | -0.18% |

Batch 128 crosses 2 GiB, so both versions compile the same kernel there; its -0.18% is the noise floor of the setup. With `KVBlockSize=1` the unconditional kernel is faster instead: 247.617 -> 95.281 us at batch 16 and 1053.010 -> 463.740 us at batch 64.

Preshuffle 64-bit addressing and the store bound:

| KVBlock | Batch | before | after | delta | accuracy |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 256 | 64 | 250.599 | 238.254 | -4.93% | 0 -> 0 mismatched |
| 256 | 128 | 449.150 | 451.121 | +0.44% | 508281/16777216 -> 0 |
| 64 | 128 | 464.583 | 463.802 | -0.17% | 0 -> 0 mismatched |

Folding the page base into a `buffer_load` pointer fixes the same addressing but pays a descriptor setup per stage: +4.59% at batch 64 and +3.74% at batch 128, against +0.44% and -4.93% for the global-load form that was kept. Rounds did not overlap between arms, e.g. 247.898/250.599/251.677 before against 238.032/238.254/238.422 after at batch 64.

<details>
<summary>run_perf.py</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Decode perf/accuracy driver for one (batch, layout) pair per process.

Reuses the input generation, fp32 reference and packing helpers of the fixed
op_tests/test_mqa_logits.py (PR #5434, commit 849c7c25), and switches both the
KV packing and the interface Preshuffle flag together. Counts mismatches over
the whole output and returns exit code 2 on an accuracy failure.
"""

import argparse
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import sys

SCRIPT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
    "fixed_test_mqa_logits", os.path.join(SCRIPT_DIR, "test_mqa_logits.py")
)
fixed = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
_spec.loader.exec_module(fixed)

import torch  # noqa: E402

from aiter import dtypes  # noqa: E402
from aiter.jit.utils.chip_info import get_gfx  # noqa: E402
from aiter.ops.triton.attention.pa_mqa_logits import (  # noqa: E402
    deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits,
)
from aiter.ops.triton.utils.types import get_fp8_e4m3_dtype  # noqa: E402
from aiter.test_common import run_perftest  # noqa: E402


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--batch", type=int, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--layout", choices=["preshuffle", "plain"], required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=131072)
    parser.add_argument("--heads", type=int, default=32)
    parser.add_argument("--head-dim", type=int, default=128)
    parser.add_argument("--next-n", type=int, default=1)
    parser.add_argument("--kv-block", type=int, default=64)
    parser.add_argument("--chunk-k", type=int, default=256)
    parser.add_argument("--wave-per-eu", type=int, default=2)
    parser.add_argument("--num-iters", type=int, default=101)
    parser.add_argument("--num-warmup", type=int, default=2)
    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if os.path.exists(args.output):
        sys.exit(f"refusing to overwrite {args.output}")

    preshuffle = args.layout == "preshuffle"

    batch, n, heads, dim = args.batch, args.n, args.heads, args.head_dim
    next_n, kv_block = args.next_n, args.kv_block

    torch.manual_seed(0)
    fp8_dtype = get_fp8_e4m3_dtype()

    rows = batch * next_n
    blocks_per_seq = (n + kv_block - 1) // kv_block
    num_blocks = batch * blocks_per_seq

    q = torch.randn(batch, next_n, heads, dim, dtype=dtypes.bf16)
    q_fp8 = q.to(fp8_dtype)
    del q

    kv = torch.randn(num_blocks * kv_block, dim, dtype=dtypes.bf16)
    kv_q, kv_sf = fixed._pertoken_cast_to_fp8(kv, fp8_dtype)
    del kv
    kv_q = kv_q.view(num_blocks, kv_block, dim)
    kv_sf = kv_sf.view(num_blocks, kv_block)

    weights = torch.randn(rows, heads, dtype=dtypes.fp32)
    context_lens = torch.full((batch,), n, dtype=dtypes.i32)
    block_tables = torch.randperm(num_blocks).to(dtypes.i32).view(batch, blocks_per_seq)

    ref, inside = fixed.run_torch_decode(
        q_fp8.float(), kv_q, kv_sf, weights, context_lens, block_tables, n
    )

    kv_cache = fixed._pack_paged_kv(kv_q, kv_sf, preshuffle=preshuffle)
    out_logits = torch.full((rows, n), -float("inf"), dtype=dtypes.fp32)

    def run_triton():
        deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits(
            q_fp8,
            kv_cache,
            weights,
            out_logits,
            context_lens,
            block_tables,
            n,
            Preshuffle=preshuffle,
            KVBlockSize=kv_block,
            ChunkK=args.chunk_k,
            WavePerEU=args.wave_per_eu,
        )
        return out_logits

    total_ctx = int(context_lens.sum().item())
    flops = 2.0 * heads * dim * next_n * total_ctx
    read_bytes = q_fp8.nbytes + total_ctx * (dim + 4) + weights.nbytes
    nbytes = read_bytes + rows * n * 4

    out, us = run_perftest(
        run_triton,
        num_iters=args.num_iters,
        num_warmup=args.num_warmup,
        num_rotate_args=fixed._rotate_args(read_bytes),
    )

    close = torch.isclose(out, ref, rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-2)
    mismatch = int((~close).sum().item())
    total = out.numel()
    inside_mismatch = int((~close[inside]).sum().item())
    nan_inf = int((~torch.isfinite(out[inside])).sum().item())

    record = {
        "gfx": get_gfx(),
        "batch": batch,
        "layout": args.layout,
        "n": n,
        "heads": heads,
        "head_dim": dim,
        "next_n": next_n,
        "kv_block": kv_block,
        "chunk_k": args.chunk_k,
        "wave_per_eu": args.wave_per_eu,
        "num_iters": args.num_iters,
        "num_warmup": args.num_warmup,
        "us": us,
        "TFLOPS": flops / us / 1e6,
        "TB/s": nbytes / us / 1e6,
        "mismatch": mismatch,
        "total": total,
        "inside_mismatch": inside_mismatch,
        "inside_total": int(inside.sum().item()),
        "nonfinite_inside": nan_inf,
        "kv_bytes": num_blocks * kv_block * (dim + 4),
        "aot": os.environ.get("AITER_ENABLE_AOT_GLUON_PA_MQA_LOGITS", "0"),
    }
    with open(args.output, "w") as f:
        json.dump(record, f, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
    print(json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True))

    if mismatch:
        print(f"ACCURACY FAILURE: {mismatch}/{total} mismatched", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

title: [Test] Sweep the MQA logits indexer's M and N across prefill and decode
body:
## Summary

Adds `op_tests/test_mqa_logits.py`, an M x N sweep for the MQA-logits lightning
indexer, with one table for prefill and one for decode.

## Motivation

The model fixes the indexer's head geometry -- KV is a single head, `head_dim`
is 128, Q has 32 or 64 heads -- so M (query rows) and N (KV length) are the axes
that decide which kernel config actually runs. Nothing in-tree sweeps them:

* `op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_fp8_mqa_logits.py` is a correctness UT
  that tops out at `(s_q, s_k) = (1024, 1560)`, plus two >2 GiB regression shapes.
* `bench_fp8_mqa_logits.py` and `bench_deepgemm_attention.py` each take one
  shape per process and report no accuracy.

So there was no single place to answer "what does this op do across the shapes
a model actually serves, and is it still correct there".

## Changes

One new file. Prefill and decode are different kernels with different calling
conventions, so they get one `@benchmark` function and one table each:

| phase | kernel | shape mapping |
|---|---|---|
| prefill | `fp8_mqa_logits` | contiguous KV `[N, 128]`, Q `[M, H, 128]`, causal chunked-prefill window |
| decode | `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` | paged cache, Q `[B, next_n, H, 128]`, M = `B * next_n` |

Decode reproduces ATOM's `Indexer._score_topk_decode` convention: preshuffled
64-token KV blocks, `ChunkK=256`, `WavePerEU=2`, caller-owned output buffer, and
randomized (fragmented) block tables rather than a sequential one a real KV
cache never hands the kernel.

Two things worth flagging for review:

* **`err` measures the kernel, not the quantization.** Both references
  dequantize the same fp8 bytes the kernels read, so a non-zero `err` column is
  a real bug rather than fp8 rounding noise.
* **Prefill's reference is row-sampled, deliberately.** The full `[H, M, N]`
  fp32 score tensor is ~69 TB at `H=32/M=8192/N=65664`. The sample takes the
  grid edges and the `BLOCK_M=2` block seam first (where a row-indexing bug
  lands), then an even spread; the `ref_rows` column records how many rows were
  actually compared.

`TB/s` is compulsory traffic only. Prefill re-reads KV per query row, so that
column is a lower bound there and TFLOPS is the metric to read; decode is
genuinely bandwidth-bound and TB/s is the one that matters.

## How to run it

```bash
python op_tests/test_mqa_logits.py                          # both tables, ~24 s
python op_tests/test_mqa_logits.py -p prefill -hq 64        # one phase, one head count
python op_tests/test_mqa_logits.py -p decode -b 128 256 -n 131072
python op_tests/test_mqa_logits.py -m 4096 -n 8192 -hq 32   # one shape
```

Every flag is a swept list (`-m`, `-n`, `-b`, `-hq`, `-dh`, `-mtp`, `-kb`, `-c`,
`-p`), so a different model's shapes go in without touching the file. Prefill
skips `n < m`; `-n` is shared by both phases.

## Performance

Environment: MI355X (gfx950, 256 CU, 288 GB HBM), run on this branch. All 76 shapes report `err == 0`. Both tables below come from one invocation:

```bash
$ python op_tests/test_mqa_logits.py
```

Prefill: 64 heads is the faster configuration at every shared shape (18/18 of them), at 1215-1990 TFLOPS against 32 heads' 927-1567. Both climb with M -- `BLOCK_M=2` engages above M=4096, and the slowest column is M=1024 where the grid cannot fill 256 CUs.

Decode is bandwidth-bound: 1.9-6.2 TB/s of compulsory traffic once batch >= 16. 64 heads roughly doubles decode TFLOPS there (229-740 against 130-373) at the same TB/s, so head count is nearly free and KV traffic is the whole story. `batch=1` never reaches that band -- it is launch-bound, with N from 4K to 128K moving latency only from 3.8 to 4.9 us at 32 heads, and 4.3 to 5.8 us at 64.

      run it there yet.

* Variable context lengths -- decode currently runs all sequences at the same
  length, so the kernel's varctx scheduling path is never exercised.
* MTP: `-mtp` defaults to 1, so the `next_n > 1` decode layout is untested.
* A FlyDSL candidate alongside the Triton one in the prefill table. It is
  gfx942-only and I have no gfx942 to validate it on, so it is left out rather
  than shipped unrun.

title: [FlyDSL] perf(pa_decode): tune MTP work budgets and planned reduction
body:
Large MTP batches can receive only two or three partitions per request under the default two-CTA-per-CU plan budget. Size long-MTP plans from host-known KV work and use a compact reducer for large output grids. For B200/C200000/MTP4, measured plan + attention + reduction latency drops from 3.00–3.23 ms to 2.30–2.46 ms on gfx950.

Targets `flydsl-pa-decode-tile` (#4332), building on #5546 and the tile branch's sliding-window and attention-sink support.

## Changes

- Let planned calls infer `max_context_partition_num` from `work_plan`, expose actual GPU counts through `plan.num_partitions`, and inherit the partition limit when refreshing a plan. Existing explicit matching arguments remain supported.
- Add an optional host `total_context_length` hint. Together with `query_length`, it supplies a work-based partition floor for long MTP workloads. B200/C200k/MTP4 selects 16 partitions per request and capacity 3200. Explicit budgets and partition caps retain precedence; windowed hints are capped by the causal-window union and tile alignment.
- Use a 128-thread register reducer for sufficiently large D128 planned grids and iterate only each request's actual partitions, while retaining a maximum of 256. Preserve the target branch's sink normalization, masked fallback, and window consistency checks.
- Add static/planned benchmark entry points with time, effective bandwidth, partition metadata, and configurable timer settings. Keep new correctness coverage in the existing PA CI test module.

The B200 planned scratch allocation grows from 8.25 MiB to 51.56 MiB per rank. Work hints size buffers at creation; length changes still refresh the existing GPU metadata, with fixed capacity for graph replay.

## Performance

Compared against target commit `fd825332f`, alternating base and PR runs on GPU 7 (gfx950, 256 CUs). BF16 Q/O, FP8 KV with per-token FP32 scales, MTP4, Hq16/Hkv1/D128 (one TP=4 rank). Each value is the median of three runs with 101 iterations, five warmups, and three allocation sets, using the same sparse-page helper. **Time includes a plan refresh on every call, attention, and reduction.**

| Contexts | Page | V layout | Base (µs) | PR (µs) | PR effective TB/s | Time reduction |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| B200, all 200000 | 16 | plain | 3000.13 | 2295.66 | 4.607 | 23.5% |
| B200, all 200000 | 16 | transposed | 2999.26 | 2332.80 | 4.534 | 22.2% |
| B200, all 200000 | 128 | plain | 2999.39 | 2325.20 | 4.545 | 22.5% |
| B200, all 200000 | 128 | transposed | 3227.13 | 2459.28 | 4.297 | 23.8% |

title: [FlyDSL] perf(pa_decode): improve page-16 and page-128 load scheduling
body:
On gfx950 with D128, per-tensor KV scales and transposed V, page-16 single-query decode now overlaps early V loads with QK/softmax and removes the corresponding scheduling fences. Page-128 single-query decode enables V prefetch on smaller grids up to two CTAs per CU; MTP keeps the existing one-to-two-CTA interval.

The change expands coverage for prefetch boundaries, transposed V, variable lengths and empty contexts, and runs the mixed-context regression from the standard CI entry point. This PR targets `flydsl-pa-decode-tile` (the branch behind #4332).

Validation:
- The optimized repository tree is identical to the previously tested `60d4474fa` tree: the recorded post-sync correctness suite had **258 passed, 1 skipped**.

title: [FlyDSL] Optimize gfx950 A8W8 preshuffle GEMM shape coverage
body:
## Summary

- add gfx950 2-wave `tile_n=32` candidates, including `tile_k=1024`, for under-filled low-M grids
- support ragged-M tuning and masked ragged-N execution for non-split preshuffle kernels
- keep existing kernel IDs stable by appending the new 2-wave candidate space
- bound split-K tuning candidates by the runtime workspace capacity
- retune validated gfx950 rows in Kimi-K3, GLM5.2 and MiniMax-M3 configs

This PR deliberately contains no CUDA-graph scratch-allocation fix. That work is handled by #5430; the changes here are complementary and avoid touching the same allocator logic.

## Performance

Measured on one MI355X/gfx950 GPU. Each shape's baseline and candidates stayed on the same GPU and all selected rows were revalidated through the production `--run_config` path. A row was retained only when the production replay remained at least 2% faster.

| Model | Initial candidates | Production-accepted | Accepted geomean speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Kimi-K3 | 225 | 157 | 1.209x |
| GLM5.2 | 49 | 39 | 1.088x |
| MiniMax-M3 | 49 | 49 | 1.297x |
| **Total** | **323** | **245** | **1.206x** |

Representative measurements from the expanded kernel families:

| Shape | Before | After | Improvement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Kimi `M=64,N=2048,K=512` | 3.61 us | 3.39 us | 6.5% |
| Kimi `M=256,N=2176,K=7168` | 19.63 us | 17.41 us | 12.8% |
| Kimi `M=2368,N=7168,K=4224` | 85.68 us | 82.18 us | 4.3% |
| GLM5.2 `M=8,N=6144,K=12288` | 15.81 us | 14.70 us | 7.6% |
| GLM5.2 `M=192,N=2688,K=6144` | 17.19 us | 13.49 us | 27.4% |
| MiniMax-M3 `M=1,N=6144,K=6144` | 11.00 us | 9.13 us | 20.5% |
| MiniMax-M3 `M=8,N=6144,K=6144` | 11.30 us | 8.62 us | 31.1% |

Only shape families exposed to the new tile/ragged candidate space were re-tuned. Rows that improved in the isolated tuner but failed to retain at least 2% production speedup were reverted.

## Validation

- fixed-GPU baseline and candidate profiling for all Kimi-K3, GLM5.2 and MiniMax-M3 model shapes
- same-GPU production revalidation: 245 / 323 candidates retained at >= 1.02x
- post-rebase production `--run_config` verification passed for all three final configs
- `pytest -q op_tests/test_gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle_pad_k.py op_tests/tuning_tests/test_csv_validation.py`: 24 passed, 37 subtests passed
- both `lds` and `plain` `test_route_g2l` paths pass after rebasing to current `main` (covers the previous CI failure)
- ragged-N epilogue now masks both row/column tails and rejects flat buffers at the 4 GiB descriptor boundary
- no duplicate model-config keys, invalid timings, or diff whitespace errors

## Review notes

- Existing `tile_n >= 64`, divisible-N kernels retain the original 4-wave layout and fast epilogue.
- Ragged-N is compile-time gated and currently rejects `split_k > 1`.
- `tile_n=32` uses an isolated 2-wave/128-thread layout; its candidates are appended after the old ID range so committed kernel IDs are not renumbered.

title: [HIP] [OPUS] [JIT] [GFX1250]OPUS PA MQA Logits MXFP4
body:
## Motivation

An MXFP4 paged MQA-logits kernel for DeepSeek-V4-style sparse-attention indexers on **gfx1250**,
the sibling of the gfx950 op in #5332. There is no FlyDSL fp4 kernel on this target, so the
indexer runs the FP8 Triton path today and this is what would replace it.

Two things shape the interface: the **per-row window is an input** (`local_ends` per query row),
so a CSA-compressed cache's `floor((pos + 1) / ratio)` works where no `ctx - (next_n - 1 - n)`
derivation can; and **prefill and decode are one launch** over a per-tile schedule table built
on device once per forward, without which every tile gets one CTA however long its window and a
decode forward cannot fill the part.

## Technical Details

**The kernel.** wave32 and `v_wmma_scale_f32_32x16x128_f4`, where `K = 128` is the whole
head_dim in one instruction (gfx950 needs two), with TDM for HBM→LDS and a double-buffered
accumulator. A CTA is 4 waves × 32 lanes sharing one 64-token KV tile — one page — each wave
owning one of the tile's up-to-4 query rows; the loop bound is the tile's **union** window and
CTA-uniform, the store mask each wave's **own** row. **269 VGPR, occupancy 3, LDS 9728, no
spill.**

**Two entry points**, both cudagraph-safe, in `aiter.ops.opus.pa_mqa_logits_mxfp4`:
`pa_mqa_logits_mxfp4_plan` cuts the tiles and builds the schedule device-side with no readback,
once per **forward**; `pa_mqa_logits_mxfp4` launches, once per **CSA layer**, of which
DeepSeek-V4 has 61. `pa_mqa_logits_mxfp4_plan_buffers` sizes the buffers and settles the grid
from the static shapes alone. Slots past the work carry `chunk_count = 0` and return before any
load, so the grid never depends on device data.

**Two kernel instances, and the caller names one.** They differ only in how many query rows a
CTA covers — `qlen4_kv64` is the four-wave CTA above, `qlen1_kv64` a single wave32 — and take
byte-identical inputs, so the choice costs a caller nothing but the plan's own buffers. It is
made once per buffer pool, `pa_mqa_logits_mxfp4_plan_buffers(..., variant="qlen1_kv64")`, never
per launch; `pa_mqa_logits_mxfp4_variants()` lists them and
`pa_mqa_logits_mxfp4_block_table_width()` sizes `block_tables`, both without touching the GPU.
**Nothing infers the choice from the shape** — a mean over the batch misroutes a mixed forward,
and no rule survives a third instance — so the default is `qlen4_kv64` and **an `MTP = 1` decode
path has to ask for `qlen1_kv64`**, which the decode table below prices.

**All five inputs take their natural layout**, there being no FlyDSL kernel here to be
byte-compatible with:

| tensor | gfx950 (#5332) | gfx1250 |
|---|---|---|
| `q` | `[total_q, H, D/2]` uint8 | same |
| `weights` | `[total_q, H]` bf16 | same |
| `q_scale` | `[total_q, 2, 32, 4]` MFMA-permuted | `[total_q, H, 4]` natural |
| `kv_scale` | `[num_blocks, 2, 32, 4]` permuted | `[num_blocks, PAGE, 4]` natural |
| `kv_cache` | `[num_blocks, 4, PAGE, 16]` | `[num_blocks, PAGE, D/2]` natural |

Every fp4 scale layout has the same BYTE COUNT, so both C++ launchers check `numel`, accept the
other target's arrays and return plausible wrong logits. The *shapes* differ (permuted 4-D,
natural 3-D), and the Python entry points — dispatching on the tensor's own device — are the
only place one is seen before the pointer is taken. That is also how the gfx950 op lands behind
these same two names when #5332 merges.

## Test Plan

gfx1250, random data:

```
python3 op_tests/test_pa_mqa_logits_mxfp4_opus.py
```

`main()` carries a positive arch allow-list, so the gfx942 / gfx950 CI shards skip and stay green.

**Data and scale are two independent axes**, the ubench convention — nibbles from `fill_fp4`,
E8M0 exponents from `fill_scale_e8m0`, selected by `--data-init` / `--scale-init` / `--seed`.
Every table is emitted as markdown and as a one-line JSON record a combined benchmark driver can
forward.

**That split is what keeps the suite able to fail.** Where neighbouring KV tokens share an
exponent, a misrouted scale reads one that happens to be right: a broken `b_scale_sel` passes at
`cos = 0.999952` on flat data and only fails at 0.396 once the exponents spread. It misroutes
across a lane **half**, so what decides is how often rows 16 apart disagree — `scale_spread`
measures that, and `correctness_blindness` **skips** the sweep, reason in its own table, for an
init pair that cannot judge.

Five tables: **corner** (14 cases — short groups at every residue mod `Q_PER_BLOCK`, offset
starts, the `KV_TILE = 64` neighbourhood, every start mod 128, both CSA regimes — **run on both
kernel instances**, since the probes' coverage is stated in tile units and a tile is four rows
for one of them and one for the other); **prefill causal** and **fresh**; **prefill chunked** at
**#5332's three shapes**, reproduced to the digit by reusing that PR's ragged `total_q = 16384`
split, so the two tables are comparable rather than merely similar; and **decode**, MTP with
windows as compressed column counts — an `MTP = 1` batch sweep over 1..128 sequences plus the
`mtp` 4/8 lines, and ragged lines that hold the tile count while moving only how many sequences
are long.

Every perf table carries a `variant` column. The decode table names an instance per shape; the
three prefill tables pass none and report what the op settled on, so the default path and the
explicit path are both exercised and which is which is visible rather than implied.

## Test Result

**Resources**: **269 VGPR, occupancy 3, LDS 9728, no scratch, no spill.**

**Correctness — all pass**, 50 rows from one run. `err` is `checkAllclose`'s mismatch fraction,
so 0 is exact agreement within tolerance:

| table | rows | err | oob -inf | window written |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| corner | 28 (14 cases × 2 instances) | 0 | all True | all True |
| prefill causal | 5 | 0 | — | — |
| prefill fresh | 3 | 0 | — | — |
| prefill chunked (#5332 shapes) | 3 | 0 | — | — |
| decode | 11 | 0 | — | — |

At the default `--scale-init auto` the E8M0 axis spreads 18 exponents with rows 16 apart
disagreeing 88.8%; `--scale-init constant` and `--data-init zero` are both correctly refused as
unable to judge. `ruff` and `black` pass.

## Performance
### Method

`run_perftest(num_iters=50, num_warmup=10)` — torch-profiler GPU kernel time — which is the
same harness and the same iteration budget #5332 uses, so the two PRs' tables are directly
comparable. The plan (tile cut + schedule) is built OUTSIDE the timed region: both are
per-forward against a per-layer kernel, so a builder left inside lands in the reported time.
Correctness is scored after timing, not before, for the same reason.

Data is `--data-init norm --scale-init auto --seed 0`. The two axes are sampled independently:
the fp4 nibbles come from `fill_fp4` and the E8M0 exponents from `fill_scale_e8m0`, rather than
the scales being derived by quantizing the data. Nothing here is broadcast — a single quantized
row replicated into every token is worth 8–11% on this kernel and makes a number
non-comparable against anything.

`H = 64`, `D = 128`, `PAGE = 64`, CSA ratio 4. Kernel resources **269 VGPR / occupancy 3 /
LDS 9728 / no spill**.

Card: one gfx1250, `rocm/fw-bringup:gfx1250-atom-20260911` (ROCm 10.1, clang 23.0.0git).

### Prefill — fresh

The sequence starts empty, so row `n` sees `(n + 1) // 4`. `total_q = 16384` split across `bs`.

| bs | qlen | total_q | tiles | ctas | min_win | max_win | max_seq_len | n_logits | us | TFLOPS | TB/s | err |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 16384 | 16384 | 4096 | 4608 | 0 | 4096 | 4096 | 33550336 | 101.77 | 5401.3 | 2.043 | 0 |
| 2 | 8192 | 16384 | 4097 | 4608 | 0 | 2048 | 2048 | 16773120 | 58.18 | 4723.7 | 2.420 | 0 |
| 4 | 4096 | 16384 | 4099 | 4608 | 0 | 1024 | 1024 | 8384512 | 37.53 | 3660.0 | 2.857 | 0 |

### Prefill — chunked, at #5332's shapes

The sequence ends this forward with `kvlen` **compressed** rows committed and this chunk is its
tail, so row `n` of a `qlen`-row sequence sees `kvlen - (qlen - 1 - n) // 4`. `kvlen = 25000`
compressed rows is roughly a 100k-raw-token context.

`total_q = 16384` split **raggedly** across `bs` by the same generator #5332's sweep uses. That
is what makes these the same shapes rather than merely similar ones — `n_logits` and `min_win`
below reproduce #5332's chunked table to the digit. An even split does not: it lands 256 logits
away at `bs = 2` and 1.3 M away at `bs = 4`.

| bs | kvlen | total_q | tiles | ctas | min_win | max_win | max_seq_len | n_logits | us | TFLOPS | TB/s | err |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 25000 | 16384 | 4096 | 4608 | 20905 | 25000 | 25024 | 376053760 | 1138.31 | 5412.7 | 1.387 | 0 |
| 2 | 25000 | 16384 | 4097 | 4608 | 22945 | 25000 | 25024 | 392830720 | 1107.10 | 5813.5 | 1.489 | 0 |
| 4 | 25000 | 16384 | 4099 | 4608 | 23334 | 25000 | 25024 | 399873142 | 1162.23 | 5637.0 | 1.445 | 0 |

**Against #5332, and read the caveat with it.** Same shapes to the logit and the same harness,
but a different part measured on a different box, so this is a data point and not a speedup
claim:

| bs | n_logits | gfx1250 us | #5332 opus us (gfx950) | #5332 FlyDSL us (gfx950) | gfx1250 TFLOPS | #5332 opus TFLOPS |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 376053760 | 1138.31 | 1979.85 | 2150.75 | 5412.7 | 3112.0 |
| 2 | 392830720 | 1107.10 | 2073.18 | 2256.64 | 5813.5 | 3104.5 |
| 4 | 399873142 | 1162.23 | 2108.68 | 2301.03 | 5637.0 | 3106.9 |

### Decode — MTP

Windows are **compressed** column counts, not raw context: a long row scans 25000 of them
(≈ 100k raw tokens at ratio 4), a short row scans 100. `mtp` is the query rows per sequence, so
`rows = seqs * mtp`. `MTP = 1` carries the batch sweep, because at one row per sequence
`rows == seqs == tiles` and `seqs` is directly what the schedule has to spread over the part.
The `ragged` lines hold the tile count and move only how many sequences are long, which makes
the uniform line at the same `(mtp, seqs)` their anchor.

| uniform | 8 | 32 | 32 | `qlen4_kv64` | 256 | 88 | 768 | 6400000 | 29.33 | 3574.8 | 2.768 | 0 |
| ragged | 4 | 32 | 16 | `qlen4_kv64` | 128 | 56 | 768 | 1606400 | 10.67 | 2466.1 | 3.220 | 0 |
| ragged | 4 | 32 | 4 | `qlen4_kv64` | 128 | 56 | 768 | 411200 | 5.98 | 1126.4 | 1.550 | 0 |
| ragged | 4 | 32 | 28 | `qlen4_kv64` | 128 | 56 | 768 | 2801600 | 15.76 | 2913.0 | 3.774 | 0 |

**`MTP = 1` is why the second instance exists, and the cost of not asking for it grows with the
batch.** A four-wave CTA covering one row masks three waves off while still holding their
registers, and it is four times as wide, so the part holds a quarter as many. Both arms cut the
same tiles; the whole difference is the grid, 3072 CTAs against 768. Running the same shapes on
`qlen4_kv64` instead, same inputs and same harness, the uniform rows read **0.96x at one
sequence, 1.33x at 8, 1.87x at 32 and 2.56x at 128** (the ragged ones 1.27x and 1.60x) — at a
single tile the split fills the part either way, and above one resident round the narrower
budget is the bottleneck.

**Within `qlen4_kv64`, `mtp` 4 → 8 costs 1.72x** (17.08 → 29.33) for twice the logits, because a
sequence then needs two tiles and its window is read twice. The knee is at `Q_PER_BLOCK`.

**The batch sweep is the schedule doing its job**: 128 times the logits for 5.0x the time
(3.93 → 19.72 us), because below one resident round more sequences only fill CUs that were idle.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Kernel] Add packed FP4 logical transpose
body:
## Summary

- Add `transpose_packed_fp4` for bit-exact logical transpose of row-major FP4 data packed as two nibbles per byte.
- Keep the kernel, wrapper, tests, and benchmark in the existing `fast_transpose` files.
- Support arbitrary input strides, non-power-of-two tails, `torch.uint8`, and `torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2`.
- Reuse the existing 32 x 32 logical transpose tile and provide a kernel `repr` containing both tile parameters.

title: [FlyDSL] [KIMI-K3] Enable KDA per-channel decay gate in FlyDSL GDR decode
body:
## Summary

This PR extends the existing FlyDSL Gated Delta Rule (GDR) decode kernel with a compile-time per-channel decay-gate path for Kimi Delta Attention (KDA), a linear/recurrent attention mechanism that continuously compresses history into a fixed-size recurrent state and selectively forgets information through decay gates, avoiding a growing KV cache for efficient long-context decoding. The per-channel decay formulation allows each channel to learn its own forgetting rate, enabling finer-grained state retention than a single shared decay factor. This work addresses [SILOTIGER-847](https://amd.atlassian.net/browse/SILOTIGER-847).

- Decay `a` is per-channel `(B, Sq, H, K)` instead of per-head `(B, Sq, H)`.
- `dt_bias` is per-channel `(H, K)` instead of per-head `(H)`, and may be f32 while activations stay bf16/fp16.
- Gate math is `g = g_min * sigmoid(exp(A_log) * (a + dt_bias))` with `g_min = -5`.
- `gate_mode` is inferred from `a.dim()` (`"kda"` if 4-D, else `"gdr"`), so existing callers keep the same signature.
- Scalar GDR is untouched; the KDA tilings are new and reach only the KDA path.
- `flydsl_gdr_decode` is exported from `aiter.ops.flydsl`.



## Technical details

**Kernel** (`kernels/gdr_decode.py`): `gate_mode` is a factory argument, so `"gdr"` and `"kda"` compile to separate `lru_cache` binaries and `PER_CHANNEL` folds out under `const_expr`. Only a non-`gdr` mode is suffixed onto the kernel name, so existing GDR symbols are unchanged. The scalar arm's one edit is the `dt_bias` copy atom, which is the same 16-bit copy whenever `dt_bias` carries the activation dtype.

**Wrapper** (`linear_attention_kernels.py`): in KDA mode `a` is `(B, Sq, H_v, D_k)` and `dt_bias` is `(H_v, D_k)`, and both are checked against the shapes that `query` and `value` imply. The kernel bakes in a few layout assumptions, so the wrapper now rejects the inputs that would break them: `a` must be dense along `D_k`, `out` must be contiguous, and an unshuffled `state` must have unit stride in K. A caller-supplied `stream` must be on `query`'s device, and the staging copies are enqueued on that same stream so they complete before the launch reads them. A negative slot index marks a CUDA-graph padding row: the kernel zeroes that row of `out` and leaves the state pool untouched.

**Tuning**: `_KDA_DECODE_BY_PART` stores one `(NUM_BLOCKS_PER_V_DIM, NUM_WARPS, WARP_THREADS_K)` triple per batch size, measured at B ∈ {1, 4, 64, 256} for a single shape: 12 key and value heads, 128 wide, bf16 activations over an f32 state. Every other shape keeps main's `_decode_tiling()` heuristic. `NUM_BLOCKS_PER_V_DIM` splits the value dimension so that one decode launches more blocks, which is how a small batch fills the GPU, and the split that pays therefore depends on how many CUs the part has. An arch name does not pin that down — MI308X and MI300X are both gfx942, at 80 CUs and 304 — so the table is keyed on `(arch, CU count)`, and a part with no entry of its own uses `_decode_tiling()`, which reads the CU count at runtime.

**Tests and benchmark**: `op_tests/test_flydsl_gdr_decode.py` covers both gates and the per-part lookup; the torch oracle is test-only in `op_tests/kda_ref.py`. In `bench_gdr_decode_kda.py`, `--sweep` prints a table entry, and `--bench` needs a vLLM checkout passed with `--vllm` for its comparator, `fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode` from `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/third_party/kda/fused_recurrent.py`. That is the Triton packed decode, not the HIP fused KDA, and only device time is quoted because vLLM graphs this kernel with others.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest` on `op_tests/test_flydsl_gdr_decode.py` and `aiter/ops/flydsl/test_flydsl_linear_attention.py`, on both parts
- [x] Numerics vs the torch KDA oracle: elementwise `rtol`/`atol` 1e-3 in the tests, and the reference's own RMSE-ratio-or-absolute 1e-3 pair in the benchmark's parity check
- [x] bf16 activations, f32 `dt_bias`, f32 and bf16 state, padded non-contiguous state, strided state indices, both shuffle modes, slots from 1, negative-slot zeros
- [x] Scalar GDR unchanged: same `_decode_tiling()` dispatch as main, no restored CSV, still matching the Triton reference across the existing GQA shapes
- [x] Device-time A/B vs Triton packed decode at B ∈ {1, 4, 64, 256}, 12 heads, K=V=128, bf16, f32 state, on MI355X and MI308X



## Test result

Device time per call, host excluded, L2 flushed, 5 trials on fresh inputs, mean ± std; both kernels see the same data. The last column runs FlyDSL on the config `_decode_tiling()` picks, so it is what the tuned row buys.

MI355X, gfx950, 256 CUs:


| B   | Triton µs    | FlyDSL µs    | speedup      | FlyDSL untuned µs     |
| --- | ------------ | ------------ | ------------ | --------------------- |
| 1   | 7.34 ± 0.01  | 6.55 ± 0.10  | 1.12x ± 0.02 | 6.57 ± 0.03           |
| 4   | 8.01 ± 0.00  | 6.89 ± 0.01  | 1.16x ± 0.00 | 7.43 ± 0.00           |
| 64  | 22.35 ± 0.11 | 20.79 ± 0.03 | 1.08x ± 0.01 | 22.84 ± 0.15          |
| 256 | 79.63 ± 0.07 | 76.93 ± 0.07 | 1.04x ± 0.00 | 88.70 ± 0.05          |


MI308X, gfx942, 80 CUs:


| B   | Triton µs      | FlyDSL µs     | speedup      | FlyDSL untuned µs     |
| --- | -------------- | ------------- | ------------ | --------------------- |
| 1   | 13.38 ± 0.03   | 11.62 ± 0.04  | 1.15x ± 0.00 | 12.55 ± 0.06          |
| 4   | 18.56 ± 0.01   | 16.00 ± 0.04  | 1.16x ± 0.00 | 18.15 ± 0.09          |
| 64  | 77.22 ± 0.08   | 54.76 ± 0.19  | 1.41x ± 0.01 | 59.93 ± 0.21          |
| 256 | 248.33 ± 12.44 | 174.84 ± 0.09 | 1.42x ± 0.07 | 196.44 ± 0.17         |

title: [Triton/Gluon] Fix fp8 KV correctness reference in bench_unified_attention
body:
## Purpose
`op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_unified_attention.py -test` reports false correctness failures for **every** fp8 KV shape (bf16 passes). The `-test` path calls `ref_paged_attn` with the original, un-quantized `key_cache`/`value_cache` **and** the fp8 descale factors. `ref_paged_attn` then does `key_cache = key_cache * k_descale` on full-precision tensors, so the reference diverges structurally from the kernel (softmax is not scale-invariant in K). The kernel itself is correct; only the harness reference is wrong. Fixes #5661.

## Change
Pass the quantized tensors (`q_fp8`/`k_fp8`/`v_fp8`) to `ref_paged_attn` when fp8 is enabled, so the reference reconstructs K/V via `* descale`, matching what the kernel consumes. No kernel code touched.

## Test Plan / Result (MI325, gfx942)
```
python op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_unified_attention.py -b 1 -hq 32 -hk 8 -d 128 -sq 512 -sk 512 -equal_seqlens -fp8_kv -test
```
- Before: `FAIL ... max_diff=3.87` (19.9% mismatched).
- After: `PASS ... max_diff=0.0156`.
- Also verified PASS after the fix for head_size 512 (GQA 32/4) and head_size 256 (GQA 32/16), the Gemma-4 shapes.

## Notes
AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find and fix this. Not a duplicate — no open PR addresses the bench fp8 reference. This is a test-harness-only change; it unblocks using `-test` as a correctness gate when tuning fp8 configs.

title: [FlyDSL] [CI] [a16w4] Support MXFP4 weights on gfx942 (CDNA3)
body:
## Motivation

`moe_2stage_a16wmix` cannot run with MXFP4 weights on gfx942 (CDNA3) at all — it does not
even assemble. `make_b_loader`'s `upconvert_b` upconverts the weights with
`v_cvt_scalef32_pk_bf16_fp4`, which is CDNA4-only:

```
error: instruction not supported on this GPU (gfx942): v_cvt_scalef32_pk_bf16_fp4
        v_cvt_scalef32_pk_bf16_fp4 v47, v56, v90 op_sel:[1,0,0]
```

1792 occurrences, and it is the **only** unsupported instruction in the kernel. Everything
else in the pipeline is already arch-gated and fine on CDNA3 — the `use_k16` K=16 MFMA
path, the int4 dequant one line above the fp4 branch, the `dma_via_vgpr` A-tile staging.
So the weight upconvert is the single thing standing between this kernel and CDNA3.

This is architectural rather than SKU-specific: the instruction is absent from all of
CDNA3, so every gfx942 part is affected (MI300X, MI300A, MI308X, MI325X). CDNA3 also has
no fp4 MFMA, so the weights genuinely have to be decoded to bf16 before the MFMA rather
than fed in directly as on CDNA4.

The goal is to make the existing a16w4 MXFP4 path work on gfx942, with the gfx950 path
bit-unchanged. `op_tests/flydsl_tests/test_flydsl_moe_a16wfp4.py` is already gated for
`get_gfx() in ("gfx942", "gfx950")`, so no test gating changes here — that test is
supposed to run on CDNA3 already and only fails because the kernel will not build.

## Technical Details

`_fp4_nibble_to_bf16x8` in `moe_2stage_a16wmix/utils.py` is the CDNA3 counterpart of the
`_int4_nibble_to_bf16x8` already in that file, and `upconvert_b` selects it the same way
it selects the int4 one. It is a `v_perm_b32` byte lookup rather than per-element
arithmetic, because for E2M1 it can be:

- Every E2M1 magnitude is exactly representable in bf16, so the 16-entry table reduces to
  a byte permute over two constant pools — one for the bf16 high bytes, one for the low
  bytes — selected by `nibble & 7`.
- The sign is the nibble's bit 3, shifted into bf16 bit 15.
- The E8M0 scale is a power of two, so applying it leaves the result exactly
  representable and the f32 -> bf16 step is a truncation, not a round-to-nearest.
- E2M1 has no NaN encoding, so no NaN handling is needed.

The result is no reconstruction through f32, no compares or selects for the subnormal
cases, and no full `cvt`.

**Arch gating.** The selection is an `is_gfx942` flag, following the
`is_gfx942 = str(gpu_arch).startswith("gfx942")` / `const_expr(is_gfx942)` idiom already
used in `preshuffle_gemm.py`. It is computed inside `make_b_loader` because, as that
factory's docstring notes, FlyDSL hashes its source for the cache key and not nested
helpers.

The arch arrives as a new `rocm_arch` parameter rather than being derived from `use_k16`.
`use_k16` means "K=16 MFMA", which is only correlated with CDNA3 — forcing the K=16 path
on a gfx950 box to validate it must not also switch the weight decode. `rocm_arch` is
threaded explicitly alongside `use_k16` (`compile_gemm{1,2}_a16w4_port` -> the local
`_use_k16` alias -> `_gemm{1,2}_body_a16w4` -> `make_b_loader`) rather than resolved
inside the builder, so `compile_gemm{1,2}_a16w4_port`'s `functools.cache` stays keyed on
it and two targets cannot share a cached kernel. It has no default at the compile entry
point on purpose — a silently-wrong arch produces a kernel that does not assemble — so
both callers are updated: `moe_2stage_a16wmix/__init__.py` and `ops/flydsl/moe_kernels.py`.

gfx950 is unaffected: the new branch is `const_expr`, so there is no runtime check and the
emitted gfx950 ISA is unchanged.

`+100 / -0` across 5 files, no deletions.

Related: [ROCm/FlyDSL#424](https://github.com/ROCm/FlyDSL/pull/424) and
[#431](https://github.com/ROCm/FlyDSL/pull/431) introduced these kernels as gfx950 work;
[vllm-project/vllm#50319](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50319) asked for
exactly this gfx942 MXFP4-bf16 MoE capability and had to route around its absence.

## Test Plan

Environment: gfx942 (MI308X), ROCm 7.14, flydsl 0.3.2.

1. Assemble `compile_gemm1_a16w4_port` for the Kimi-K3 `3584x512 E896 topk16` geometry and
   count unsupported instructions, before and after, natively on gfx942 and with
   `ARCH=gfx950` to confirm the CDNA4 path is untouched.
2. Numerics: because this container's prebuilt `module_aiter_core.so` predates aiter main
   and raises `ActivationType has no attribute 'GeluTanh'` in `aiter/ops/quant.py`,
   `op_tests/flydsl_tests/test_flydsl_moe_a16wfp4.py` could not be run here. The decode
   was instead validated through `ROCm/FlyDSL`'s `tests/kernels/test_moe_gemm.py`
   (`test_a16w4_moe_e2e`, strict cosine gate against a torch reference), with the decode
   block lifted verbatim from this change — byte-identical, 3919 bytes, sha256 prefix
   `8cda818e15177887`.
3. The same FlyDSL selection with only the kernel change reverted, to confirm the tests
   are not passing vacuously.

## Test Result

| check | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| gfx942 assembly, unsupported instructions | 1792 | **0** |
| `ARCH=gfx950` assembly, unsupported instructions | 0 | 0 |
| FlyDSL `test_a16w4_moe_e2e` (a16w4 selection), gfx942 | 3 failed, 2 passed | **5 passed** |

The `before` column of row 3 is the load-bearing one: the three failures are exactly the
fp4 cases (`small-a16w4`, `kimi512-a16w4`, `native_layout[small]`), while the two that
still pass are the `a16w16` bf16-weight variants, which never reach the decode. So the
gate is neither vacuous nor over-broad.

Not claimed here: no gfx950 measurements or behavioural claims — this box is CDNA3 only.
Since the new path sits behind `const_expr(is_gfx942)` and the gfx950 ISA is unchanged,
gfx950 behaviour cannot move, but a gfx950 CI run to confirm that would be welcome. The
aiter-side e2e test is also still unrun for the environment reason above; it needs a
container whose `module_aiter_core` matches aiter main.

Out of scope, happy to file separately: `test_flydsl_moe_a16wfp4.py` covers
`inter_dim` 512 and 384, but FlyDSL's `test_moe_gemm.py` requires `inter_dim % 256 == 0`,
so the two suites do not cover the same shapes for this kernel.


## Submission Checklist

- [x] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#pull-requests.

title: [Build] prebuild: add the missing nmask/nlse bf16 mha_varlen_fwd variant
body:
`PREBUILD_KERNELS=1` prebuilds five of the six bf16 `mha_varlen_fwd` variants that the dense (non-sparse) attention path can ask for. `req_md_names` in `setup.py` hardcodes the list, and it covers mask/nmask crossed with lse/nlse except for one combination: no-mask **and** no-LSE. That is the plainest case of the six.

The consequence is not a missing feature but a startup hang. The variant is still perfectly buildable, so it gets JIT-compiled on first use instead — and in a tensor-parallel server every rank reaches it at the same moment. On an 8-GPU node, eight SGLang schedulers start compiling the same kernel concurrently and the engine's readiness probe times out before any of them finishes.

## How we found it

Bringing up GLM-5.2 744B LoRA RL on MI355X (8x gfx950) under SGLang. GLM-5.2's DSA indexer only goes sparse above `index_topk` (2048) tokens, so a short rollout runs dense attention through `mha_varlen_fwd` with no causal mask and no returned LSE — exactly the combination that is not prebuilt. Engine startup then hung, and the log names the module:

```
(CommandActor pid=59282) [aiter] [pid=63232] start build
    [mha_varlen_fwd_bf16_nlogits_nbias_nmask_nlse_ndropout_nskip_nqscale]
(CommandActor pid=59284) [aiter] [pid=63264] waiting for baton release at
    .../build/lock_mha_varlen_fwd_bf16_nlogits_nbias_nmask_nlse_ndropout_nskip_nqscale
(CommandActor pid=59285) [aiter] [pid=63258] waiting for baton release at
    .../build/lock_mha_varlen_fwd_bf16_nlogits_nbias_nmask_nlse_ndropout_nskip_nqscale
```

One rank builds it; the other ranks serialise behind that module's `FileBaton`, and the engine's readiness probe times out first. Prebuilding this one variant out-of-band (~27 s) and caching the `.so` made startup reliable, which is what pointed at the prebuild list rather than at the kernel.

## Evidence

On `rocm/sgl-dev` (`v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x`, and reproduced on `v0.5.15.post1`):

```
$ ls /sgl-workspace/aiter/aiter/jit/ | grep -c mha_varlen_fwd
5
```

The five present are exactly the five in `req_md_names`; the no-mask/no-LSE variant is the one absent.

`get_mha_varlen_prebuild_variants_by_names` already accepts the name and returns a well-formed recipe, identical in shape to a shipped one — so this is a list omission and not a missing recipe:

```
SHIPPED: 1 variant(s); blob_gen_cmd=True
MISSING: 1 variant(s); blob_gen_cmd=True
```

## Scope

One more variant in the prebuild set. No kernel, recipe or build-system change, and no effect on `PREBUILD_KERNELS=0`, `2` or `3`.

## What we did not verify

We did not run a full base-image rebuild to watch the `.so` land, because `PREBUILD_KERNELS=1 setup.py build_ext` rebuilds the whole module set (one module alone took 980 s in our timing) and that belongs in the image builder's CI rather than in our environment. What is verified is that the variant is absent from the shipped set, that aiter's own recipe lookup accepts the name and returns a valid build entry, and that the kernel builds — the runtime JIT builds it today, which is the behaviour this change moves to build time.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Perf] Add persistent CTA scheduling for paged FP8 MQA decode
body:
## Summary

Add a reusable, GPU-built persistent CTA schedule for paged FP8 MQA decode logits. `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_persistent_schedule` builds a `[CTA, 4]` work table once; passing it as `PersistentSchedule` makes the compute kernel read its tile from that table instead of deriving it from `pid`. Work is balanced across variable-length contexts, so one long sequence no longer strands the rest of the grid.

This PR targets **#5614's branch**, `zhiding512/fix-paged-mqa-block-paging-20260917`, based on `95e292923`.

## Motivation

The regular SplitKV path maps CTAs per (batch, query, head tile, split). With ragged or skewed contexts most CTAs finish early and idle behind the longest sequence. The schedule finds the smallest per-CTA chunk budget whose CTA count still fits the grid, gives empty sequences no slots, and balances chunks within each sequence so its last CTA is not a short straggler.

## Changes

- Add `_deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_persistent_schedule` and the `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_persistent_schedule` helper. The table can be rebuilt in place into an existing buffer, and stays valid while `context_lens` is unchanged.
- Add a `PERSISTENT` compile-time branch to both the plain and preshuffle Gluon compute kernels; tiles are read through `_load_persistent_mqa_tile`. The regular path is untouched.
- Specialize the persistent query count; cover MTP causal masks in every stage, output guards, zero contexts and large KV offsets.
- Persistent AOT binaries use a distinct `_persistent` name.

This PR carries the kernel and dispatch changes only. Tests and the benchmark harness are kept out to keep the diff reviewable; the validation they produced is summarized below.

## Performance

gfx950 / 256 CU; H=32, D=128, next_n=1, KVBlockSize=64, ChunkK=256, WavePerEU=2, output bound 131072. Six alternating-order rounds, median; CPU work and output initialization excluded. `schedule` is the table build measured on its own — the kernel column excludes it because the table is reusable across calls that share `context_lens`.

Uniform context 131072, plain layout, helper-default CTA counts:

| Batch | CTAs | baseline μs | persistent kernel μs | schedule μs | kernel change |
| ----: | ---: | ----------: | -------------------: | ----------: | ------------: |
| 1     | 512  | 6.774       | 6.396                | 1.823       | -5.58%        |
| 4     | 512  | 15.942      | 16.140               | 2.428       | +1.24%        |
| 16    | 512  | 46.084      | 45.907               | 2.417       | -0.38%        |
| 64    | 1024 | 232.865     | 227.337              | 2.401       | -2.37%        |
| 128   | 2048 | 398.570     | 395.846              | 1.886       | -0.68%        |

Variable-length contexts, where the schedule actually pays off. `ragged` is `ctx[0]=0`, `ctx[i]=(i+1)*131072//128`; `skewed` is one 131072-token sequence plus 257-token sequences:

| Workload         | Layout     | baseline μs | persistent kernel μs | kernel change |
| ---------------- | ---------- | ----------: | -------------------: | ------------: |
| B16 skewed       | plain      | 31.403      | 8.545                | -72.79%       |
| B16 skewed       | preshuffle | 21.441      | 6.257                | -70.82%       |
| B128 skewed      | plain      | 110.212     | 9.100                | -91.74%       |
| B128 skewed      | preshuffle | 72.325      | 6.655                | -90.80%       |
| B128 ragged      | plain      | 266.589     | 209.158              | -21.54%       |
| B128 ragged      | preshuffle | 270.079     | 228.483              | -15.40%       |
| B64 uniform 4096 | plain      | 10.957      | 11.385               | +3.90%        |
| B64 uniform 4096 | preshuffle | 8.438       | 8.748                | +3.68%        |

Two caveats for callers. Uniform long contexts gain at most about 2%, so the schedule is not worth it there. Rebuilding the table on every call costs a fixed 1.8–2.4 μs that does not scale with the workload, which dominates at small batch — B1 plain goes from 6.396 to 8.219 μs end to end. Build the table once per decode step and reuse it across layers while contexts are unchanged.

Measured on ROCm device 6 with unlocked clocks using a local harness that is not part of this PR; absolute values are not comparable with earlier reports on other devices, but all variants within a row were timed in one process on the same inputs in alternating order.

## Testing

No test files are touched by this PR. The existing suite is unaffected, and the new path was validated with a separate local suite that is not included here.

- [x] **62 passed** — `op_tests/test_pa_mqa_logits_offset.py` on gfx950, unmodified, confirming the regular SplitKV path is unchanged.
- [x] **47 passed** — local persistent suite: schedule reuse after changing contexts inside one CUDA Graph, random physical pages, per-token scales, compact and padded page tables, zero contexts, short tails, `KVBlockSize > ChunkK`, 2/4/8 GiB KV address boundaries, output row offsets across 2 GiB, output guards, and `next_n=65/129` cross-stage MTP.
- [x] AOT load verified for plain and preshuffle with `next_n=3`, including the distinct `_persistent` name.
- [x] Every benchmark variant above was checked against the full FP32 reference before timing: 0 mismatches.
- [x] Black, Ruff and `git diff --check` pass.
- [ ] gfx942 hardware validation (not available in this session).

Happy to bring the persistent tests and the benchmark in as a follow-up PR, or fold them back into this one if reviewers prefer them together.

## Dependencies

Depends on #5614. No new third-party dependencies.

## Breaking Changes

None intended. `PersistentSchedule` defaults to `None` and the regular SplitKV path is unchanged. The persistent entry point requires Triton >= 3.5 and gfx942/gfx950.

title: [FlyDSL][gfx950] Optimize FP4 MQA prefill and decode
body:
## Summary

- replace the original FP4 MQA prefill implementation with the validated 4-wave kernel in `pa_mqa_logits_fp4_prefill.py`
- group four same-batch query rows per prefill CTA, with one row per wave and one LDS-staged KV page shared by all four waves
- use one decode kernel for every `next_n`, with cooperative head waves and no decode-to-prefill routing
- specialize internally scheduled D128 H64/H128 decode with direct global KV/scale loads and grid-aware 32- or 64-token tiles
- retain the staged-LDS decode path for external/persistent schedules and unsupported layouts
- exclude benchmark scripts, raw measurements, and experimental kernel variants from the PR

## Dependency

Depends on #5518. This branch should be rebased onto the updated `main` after #5518 merges so it inherits the corresponding page-stride, 64-bit addressing, and page128 support without duplicating that dependency's history here.

## Implementation

### Prefill

- 4 waves per CTA, one query row per wave
- four waves cooperatively load four KV pages into a single LDS stage
- LDS-resident KV is reused across the four query rows
- `32x32x64` FP4 MFMA
- next-chunk global loads overlap with computation on the final page of the current chunk
- 17,408 bytes LDS and 126 VGPRs in the measured kernel

### Decode

The decode kernel now handles all `next_n` values directly:

- head waves cooperate on the head reduction within each CTA
- internally scheduled D128 H64/H128 layouts read KV and scales directly from global memory into registers
- a 32-token, 2-wave tile is selected when the complete direct grid is at most 1024 CTAs
- larger direct grids use 64-token tiles to control launch size
- the direct path uses a 2D launch and compile-time page/chunk addressing
- scalar weight loads are selected for the larger grids where they reduce contention
- external/persistent schedules and unsupported layouts retain the staged-LDS generic path
- callers can still override `block_k` and `num_warps`

For the ordinary `next_n=1/2` direct shapes, each CTA owns one token chunk. Extra LDS stages therefore do not form a cross-chunk pipeline, and `next_n` does not itself create additional waves. Their improvement comes from exposing more grid-level parallelism with 32/64-token tiles and bypassing KV LDS staging; head waves only parallelize the head reduction.

## Performance

Measured on MI355X using median GPU kernel time. Decode results use nine paired CUDA Graph rounds with identical inputs and randomized Old/New execution order. Unless noted otherwise, rows use H64, D128, page64, and ragged context lengths averaging approximately half of `max_ctx`.

### Prefill

| Shape (`B x Q x KV`) | Old (us) | New (us) | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| AgentX trace | 781.16 | 610.38 | 1.280x |
| 1 x 512 x 64K | 249.20 | 200.74 | 1.241x |
| 1 x 1K x 64K | 473.36 | 377.41 | 1.254x |
| 1 x 2K x 32K | 451.07 | 356.27 | 1.266x |
| 1 x 1K x 128K | 910.54 | 693.36 | 1.313x |
| 4 x 256 x 16K | 121.77 | 93.07 | 1.308x |
| 8 x 128 x 8K | 69.46 | 50.87 | 1.366x |
| 1 x 4K x 4K | 98.64 | 56.60 | 1.743x |
| 1 x 8K x 8K | 372.80 | 213.22 | 1.748x |
| 2 x 8K x 8K | 745.16 | 423.80 | 1.758x |
| 1 x 8K x 32K | 1519.69 | 1206.67 | 1.259x |

### Decode

Here, Old is the original 256-token/4-wave MXFP4 decode configuration and New is the production configuration selected by the current dispatcher.

| Shape (`B x next_n x max_ctx`) | Old MXFP4 (us) | New (us) | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 x 1 x 512 | 2.510 | 1.942 | 1.292x |
