title: feat(mori-ep): add the low-latency kernels and a cached handle set
body:
`MoriAll2AllManager` could only create the existing `IntraNode` and `InterNodeV1` EP kernels. Callers that needed `AsyncLL` or `InterNodeV1LL` had to construct `EpDispatchCombineOp` themselves, duplicating kernel selection and configuration outside the communicator.

This PR makes kernel selection depend on the requested latency mode and the topology measured from the process group:

- regular, intra-node: `IntraNode`
- regular, inter-node: `InterNodeV1`
- low latency, intra-node: `AsyncLL`
- low latency, inter-node: `InterNodeV1LL`

`low_latency` defaults to `False`, so existing callers retain their previous kernel, configuration, and cache identity. Low-latency launch geometry follows the WideEP reference values and remains configurable through `MORI_EP_WARP_PER_BLOCK`, `MORI_EP_BLOCK_NUM`, and `MORI_EP_RDMA_BLOCK_NUM`. `num_qp_per_pe=2` is added only for low-latency kernels.

The handle cache supports multiple reusable instances of one configuration through:

```python
get_handle(kwargs, index=0)
```

Index `0` preserves the existing shared-handle behavior. Callers with concurrent operations select another index for each additional in-flight slot. The index participates in the cache key but is not passed into the MoRI configuration. The same indexed-cache API is exposed by the FlyDSL manager for consistency, while `create_handle()` remains available for deliberately uncached FlyDSL ops.

ROCm/ATOM#2228 is the consumer integration. It passes the requested latency mode to the manager and requests two indexed handles when TBO is enabled, one per concurrent ubatch; otherwise it requests only index `0`.

Validation:

- Existing default kernel rows and geometry remain unchanged.
- Indexed-cache smoke coverage confirms that `(kwargs, index)` controls identity, index `0` preserves the old singleton behavior, and negative indexes are rejected.
- Verified against MoRI `1.2.3.dev20260824`: both low-latency kernel types exist, and split `dispatch_recv`/`combine_recv` is supported only by `AsyncLL`.
- Style, repository dependency, signal, wheel, and MI300X OPUS checks pass on the current PR head.

title: Size the MQA logits decode grid to the CU count, not the batch
body:
Stacked on #5614 (`zhiding512/fix-paged-mqa-block-paging-20260917`). One file, +14 -7.

## The problem

`deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` derives `SplitKV` from the batch and then rounds
**SplitKV** up to a multiple of five:

```python
TileQCount = batch_size * next_n
SplitKV = (max(1, TotalCuCount // TileQCount) + 4) // 5 * 5 * WavePerEU
grid = (batch_size * next_n * SplitKV, 1, 1)
```

But the thing that has to line up with the CU count is the **grid**, and the two
differ by a factor of `TileQCount`. So where the grid lands is decided by that
factor rather than by the machine:

| batch | SplitKV | grid | workgroups per CU (256 CU) |
| ----: | ------: | ---: | -------------------------: |
| 1 | 520 | 520 | 2.03 |
| 4 | 130 | 520 | 2.03 |
| 16 | 40 | 640 | **2.50** |
| 32 | 20 | 640 | **2.50** |
| 64 | 10 | 640 | **2.50** |
| 128 | 10 | 1280 | 5.00 |

At 2.5 per CU half the CUs run three workgroups and half run two, and the kernel
waits for the deeper half. Batch 128 happens to land on an exact 5, which is why
it was never paying this and why it barely moves here.

## The change

Size the grid, not SplitKV:

```python
SplitKV = max(1, ceil(2 * TotalCuCount / TileQCount))
SplitKV = min(SplitKV, max(1, ceil(max_model_len / ChunkK)))
```

The second line is an upper clamp only: a split whose start is already past the
end of the context returns immediately, so there is no reason to launch it.
`max_model_len` is the width of the logits buffer and is always >= the real
context, so the clamp is monotonically safe -- when it is loose it simply stops
binding and the first line stands.

`gfx1250` keeps the old formula; no such part was available to re-tune on.

The new optional `SplitKV` argument is an override in the same spirit as the
existing `TotalCuCount`. It is what lets both arms of every measurement below
come from a single binary, and what makes the sweep reproducible.

## Why two workgroups per CU

Sweeping SplitKV directly over 36 shapes -- batch 1/4/16/32/64/128 x context
8k/32k/128k x both layouts -- and scoring each candidate formula by how far its
pick sits from the best SplitKV measured at that shape:

| formula | mean regret | worst regret |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| current | 8.34% | 23.78% |
| grid = 1 x CU | 9.53% | 37.63% |
| grid = 1.5 x CU | 10.79% | 37.69% |
| **grid = 2 x CU** | **0.86%** | **5.04%** |
| grid = 2.5 x CU | 9.33% | 23.78% |
| grid = 3 x CU | 6.40% | 19.33% |
| grid = 4 x CU | 3.76% | 14.41% |
| grid = 8 x CU | 6.64% | 25.53% |

It is a sharp optimum, and the cliff is visible in the raw curve. Batch 64,
context 128k:

| SplitKV | grid | per CU | us | regret |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8 | 512 | 2.00 | 236.54 | 1.6% |
| **10 (current)** | **640** | **2.50** | **273.95** | **17.6%** |
| 11 | 704 | 2.75 | 257.32 | 10.5% |
| 16 | 1024 | 4.00 | 232.86 | 0.0% |
| 32 | 2048 | 8.00 | 241.31 | 3.6% |

The varctx path in this same file already sizes its grid as
`TotalCuCount * WavePerEU`, so this brings the two into agreement.

### A better variant that was deliberately not taken

Adding a second term that also caps chunks per workgroup at 32 brings mean
regret to 0.50% and buys a further -2.9% (plain) / -3.8% (preshuffle) at batch
128 with a 128k context. It needs the context length, and the only bound the
host has is `max_model_len` -- the real lengths live in a GPU tensor and reading
them would mean a device sync on the decode critical path. Mean regret when that
bound over-estimates:

| rule | exact | 2x | 4x | 8x | 16x | 64x |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| grid = 2 x CU (context-free) | 0.86% | 0.92% | 0.88% | 0.88% | 0.91% | 0.91% |
| + cap 32 chunks/WG | 0.50% | 1.35% | 1.61% | 3.39% | 6.94% | 18.55% |
| + cap 32, at most 2x | 0.57% | 1.16% | 1.34% | 1.71% | 3.06% | 4.46% |
| current (context-free) | 8.34% | 8.34% | 8.34% | 8.34% | 8.34% | 8.34% |

`op_tests/test_pa_mqa_logits_offset.py` in this repo already exercises
`max_model_len = 1<<20`, which is a hundredfold over-estimate. Giving up 0.36
points of mean regret to be insensitive to how a caller sizes that buffer seemed
the better trade.

## Measurements

gfx950 (MI355X), 256 CU, ROCm 7.2.4 / HIP 7.2.53211, PyTorch
2.10.0+rocm7.2.4.git3d3aa833, Triton 3.7.0, bare host, clocks not locked, an
otherwise idle GPU confirmed with `rocm-smi` before each round.
`KVBlockSize=64`, `ChunkK=256`, `WavePerEU=2`, H=32, D=128.

One process per point, `num_iters=101`, mismatches counted over the **whole**
output against an fp32 reference. **Both arms come from the same binary** -- the
new `SplitKV` override reproduces the old formula's value exactly -- and the two
are run back to back, order reversed on even rounds, median of three. Raw
per-round values are in the report linked at the end.

42 shapes over batch 1..128, context 8k/32k/128k, `next_n` 1 and 2, both
layouts. **Median -2.99%, 19 shapes better by more than 5%, best -19.06%, and
exactly one shape worse by more than 1%. Zero mismatches everywhere.**

| layout | batch | next_n | context | SplitKV | grid | before us | after us | change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | :---: | :---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| plain | 16 | 1 | 131072 | 40->32 | 640->512 | 58.74 | **47.55** | **-19.06%** |
| plain | 64 | 1 | 32768 | 10->8 | 640->512 | 58.50 | **47.51** | **-18.79%** |
| plain | 32 | 1 | 32768 | 20->16 | 640->512 | 32.69 | **26.64** | **-18.51%** |
| plain | 32 | 1 | 131072 | 20->16 | 640->512 | 138.69 | **113.26** | **-18.34%** |

The gains land exactly where the old grid was 640. The +1.17% at plain /
batch 128 / 128k is the only shape worse by more than a percent; its grid was
already an exact 5 per CU, so it had nothing to gain and the change costs it the
5-workgroup-deep schedule it happened to like. Preshuffle at batch 4 gaining
14.34% off 520 -> 512 says the cliff is steeper than the table suggests.

## Correctness

- `op_tests/test_pa_mqa_logits_offset.py`: **62 passed**.
- A scan aimed at the split seams, since a grid change moves where each
  workgroup's token range begins: the chunk counts where the split arithmetic is
  awkward, non-uniform context lengths including `(8192, 8191, 1, 256, 257, 255,
  65536, 3)` and `(20000, 3001, 513, 131072)`, contexts of length 1 and 2, exact
  multiples of `ChunkK` and one less, and `KVBlockSize` 1/16/64/256, on both
  layouts. Zero mismatches against an fp32 reference over the whole output,
  masked region included.
- Every one of the 42 performance processes also checked its full output; zero
  mismatches.

## Not in this PR

- The same `SplitKV` formula appears in `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1`,
  a different entry point. Not touched and not measured.
- The plain kernel splits with `cdiv`, so trailing splits can start past the end
  of the context and return having done nothing -- at batch <= 16 that strands up
  to half the grid for roughly half of all context lengths. Switching it to the
  even split the preshuffle kernel already uses is worth up to -18% on the
  affected shapes but costs a flat ~+1% where the old form already used the whole
  grid, by a mechanism I could not pin down (identical VGPR/SGPR/spill, five more
  instructions). Left out deliberately; the data is in section 6.2 of the report.
- `gfx1250` and `gfx942` are unmeasured. gfx1250 keeps its existing formula.
- Performance was measured with uniform context lengths only. Variable contexts
  were covered for correctness; that case is what the varctx path exists for and
  it is untouched here.
- Batch 1, and plain at batch 4 with a 32k context, are bimodal on this host
  (two clusters ~9% apart, present in the unmodified baseline as well). No
  conclusion is drawn from those points.

Full report, including all raw per-round values, the 36-shape sweep, and the
measurements that were discarded for contamination:
`mqa_logits_splitkv_grid_20260920.md`.

title: [Config] configs: GLM-5.3 routed MoE rows for gfx950
body:
## Why

GLM-5.3-Flash routed experts dispatch AITER's one-stage block-FP8 fused-MoE operator with this TP4 runtime signature:

- model/local dimensions: `(4096,512)`
- experts/top-k: `(288,8)`
- BF16 output with FP8 activations and weights
- `QuantType.per_1x128`, G1U1, `doweight_stage1=0`

The single kernel performs the gate/up GEMM, `SiLU(gate) * up`, down GEMM, and top-8 routed-weight accumulation.

The existing model-config set does not cover this dispatch signature. Without exact entries, these shapes use AITER's fallback kernels instead of kernels tuned for the dispatched token buckets.

## What this adds

Six gfx950/cu256 rows are added in a dedicated, architecture-specific GLM-5.3 table:

- `M={4,8}`: one-stage `16x128`
- `M={2048,4096,8192,16384}`: one-stage `64x256`

The matching untuned table records the complete 15-shape power-of-two ladder from `M=1` through `M=16384`.

All fifteen buckets were tuned with the standard fused-MoE tuner over the compatible one-stage ASM block-FP8 family. Only rows improving AITER's production operator by at least 3% were retained. Nine candidates were neutral or slower and are intentionally excluded.

The gfx950-specific filenames avoid the add/add path conflict with #5500's shared gfx942/fnuz tables; both PRs can merge independently, and their full dispatch keys remain disjoint.

## Validation

- All six retained rows have `err1=0.0%`, `run_1stage=1`, `kernelName2` empty, and `us2=0`.
- Production operator validation passed for every retained shape.
- `M=4` improves 7.39-7.98% across two repeated runs.
- `M=8` improves 3.08-3.15% across two repeated runs.
- `M=2048/4096/8192/16384` improve 35.20% / 50.21% / 32.01% / 21.14% in the tuner comparison.
- Nine rejected buckets remain on their existing fallback: `M={1,2,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024}`.
- `test_csv_validation.py` and `test_config_shape_collision.py`: 32 passed, 37 subtests passed.
- Every new dispatch key occurs exactly once across the complete current-main fused-MoE config set.
- No open AITER PR contains any new dispatch key.
- No changed file path overlaps open PR #5500.

Hardware: MI355X (`gfx950`, 256 CUs).  
Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.19-rocm724-mi35x-20260910`.  
Tuning branch base: upstream `ROCm/aiter` `main` at commit `d9f0c0b2efb53c62c5d3f1dc623c08ea8d2656fb`.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [QSA] Add paged sparse attention kernels
body:
## Summary

Add portable Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA scoring, radix selection, index expansion, and sparse GQA operators with gfx950 parity coverage.

- Add portable Triton paged MQA scoring and sparse paged GQA kernels.
- Add gfx950 Gluon implementations with guarded dispatch and portable Triton fallback.
- Keep radix top-k and index expansion on their existing paths.
- Enable automatic Gluon dispatch only for validated gfx950 Qwen3.8 geometries; explicit Triton and Gluon overrides remain available.
- Reject non-contiguous 1D metadata consumed as contiguous by kernels, and validate positive integer selection parameters before arithmetic.

## Released Qwen3.8 geometry

The released BF16 and FP8 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next checkpoints use:

```text
indexer_n_heads=4
indexer_kv_heads=1
indexer_head_dim=128
indexer_budget=2048
indexer_compress_ratio=4
```

The gfx950 Gluon scorer supports both this four-head production shape and the earlier eight-head development shape. On AMD Instinct MI350X (`gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-`), ROCm 7.2, PyTorch 2.9.1, and Triton 3.7.0, seven alternating-backend runs for `rows=32`, `heads=4`, `head_dim=128`, `page_size=8`, and `pages=512` measured:

- Triton mean p50: **0.018383 ms**, p50 CV **1.736%**.
- Gluon mean p50: **0.017566 ms**, p50 CV **0.080%**.
- Speedup: **1.047x**.

The complete QSA test file passed on the same MI350X environment: **17 passed**.

## gfx950 sparse GQA performance

Shape: `num_tokens=16`, `num_query_heads=10`, `head_dim=128`, `selection_width=2051`.

The following exact-head results were measured from runtime commit `2462d5b64` on AMD Instinct MI350X (`gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-`), ROCm 7.2, PyTorch 2.9.1, and Triton 3.7.0. Current PR head `150c7bc12` adds only the corresponding documentation refresh. Each result is the mean p50 from seven alternating-backend runs with 100 warmup iterations and 500 measured iterations per backend.

- Ordered indices: Triton **0.115509 ms**, Gluon **0.092252 ms** — **20.1% lower latency (1.252x)**; p50 CV **2.353% / 0.124%**.
- Randomized indices: Triton **0.118881 ms**, Gluon **0.094143 ms** — **20.8% lower latency (1.263x)**; p50 CV **1.690% / 0.549%**.

The benchmark reports every run's p20/p50/p80, aggregate p20/p50/p80, p50 standard deviation/CV, backend order, and full environment/config metadata. Unsupported shapes and failures retain the Triton fallback.


title: Add relu2 (Squared ReLU) activation support to CK-Tile fused MoE GEMM
body:
## Motivation

- NemotronH's MoE layers use Squared ReLU (`relu(x)^2`) as their activation function. Tier 1 (#5689) added a standalone `relu2` kernel so aiter could compute this activation directly instead of falling back to eager PyTorch, but that PR only covered the simple elementwise case, not the fused MoE GEMM path.

- The fused MoE GEMM path (`csrc/ck_tile_gemm_moe_2stages/`) didn't support relu2 at all. 

- This PR adds real relu2 support to the fused MoE GEMM path, so NemotronH's MoE layers can run through aiter's fast CK-Tile kernels instead of falling back to a legacy path that doesn't support relu2 at all.

This is Tier 2 of a 3-PR series adding end-to-end relu2 support:

1. #5689 -- standalone aiter elementwise kernel (no dependencies)
2. This PR -- aiter CK-Tile fused MoE GEMM support for relu2 (depends
   on Tier 1)
3. vLLM AITER backend integration (depends on this PR)


## Technical Details

Root cause: `moe_dispatch` (the CK-Tile MoE GEMM's kernel-selection function) had no case for relu2's internal activation id, so relu2 calls fell through the if/else chain with no matching branch and no `return` -- genuine undefined behavior, not a crash or NaN. 

This PR adds the missing dispatch branch, along with the supporting relu2 activation functor, codegen routing, and Python-side wiring needed to reach it (`aiter.fused_moe`'s `get_2stage_cfgs` now selects the CK-Tile relu2 path instead of falling back to a legacy codegen path that has no relu2 support at all).

## Test Plan

Model: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-BF16`, 8x AMD Instinct MI350 (gfx950), TP=8.

- Kernel-level: `test_fmoe` (isolated CK-Tile GEMM, vs. torch-eager reference) at E=8/topk=2 across token counts {16,32,64,128,256}, and at E=512/topk=22 (NemotronH's production MoE scale).
- End-to-end: NemotronH's real checkpoint is unquantized bf16 and only reaches this fused-GEMM dispatch path when weights are quantized to fp4x2/per_1x32 at load time, so this was validated via  `--quantization mxfp4` online quantization in vLLM. Ran `vllm bench serve` (1024/1024 and 8192/1024, concurrency 128, 256 prompts) and `lm_eval` GSM8K (5-shot, n=1319) as an A/B test toggling only the `moe_dispatch` fix (identical mxfp4 quantization and hardware otherwise, fix reverted vs. applied).

## Test Result

- Kernel-level: all PASS. logits_diff 2.67e-05 to 7.56e-05 at E=8/topk=2, and 6.06e-05 at E=512/topk=22, vs. torch-eager reference.

* [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
* [] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
* [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. (N/A -- no user-facing docs/config affected by this internal dispatch fix)

title: [Perf] Tune DeepSeek V4.1 mHC large-M split-K on gfx950
body:
## Purpose

`get_mhc_pre_splitk_large_m` currently selects `(split_k=8, tile_k=64)` from
M=8192 for every eligible gfx950 shape. For the unpacked DeepSeek-V4.1
four-stream H=5120 projection, that policy regresses the lower and upper
large-M buckets; it wins only after the generic policy falls to two-way
split-K and before eight-way split overhead takes over.

This change keeps `(8, 64)` only for M=13312–14592 for that exact geometry.
Packed BF16 weights, other hidden sizes, other architectures, and every shape
outside the measured interval retain the existing policy.

## MI355X results

wrapper with identical inputs, warmup, output allocation, stream, and JIT
cache:

- M=14336: 1.0355x device-mean and 1.0344x wall-mean speedup.

The gfx950 mHC pre/post/post-pre boundary suite completed at M=8192, 13312,

title: [Triton/Gluon] [FlyDSL] [Perf] argmax: take the split count as an argument, not a build parameter
body:
## What

`build_topk_per_row_argmax_module` is keyed on `splits`, and `splits` follows the
**row count**, so a build per split is a build per batch size. Over a 129280-wide
vocabulary that is **31 distinct builds at bf16 and 63 at fp32**, with buckets one
row wide near the bottom — rows 35, 36, 37 and 40 each get their own.

This makes the split count a runtime argument and keys the build on a bool
(`single`: is the row held by one workgroup?), so **two builds per dtype serve
every shape**.

While the sweep was cheap, it also showed the split rule picking 2 or 4 for rows
too short for any split to pay, so this adds `_SPLITTABLE_ROW_COLUMNS`.

## Why it matters

On a serving trace (8.3 s window, one rank):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| distinct argmax kernels | **28** | **2** |
| device idle before a first launch | **195.6 ms** | **0** |
| device idle before any later launch | 0 | 0 |

The 195.6 ms is 79% of all device idle in that region, in stalls of **16–27 ms**
each, against a largest non-argmax gap of 0.97 ms. Each stall is one first launch
of a new `splits`; all 114 later launches have a gap of exactly 0. Inside a stall
the only traced host call is `hipModuleLoadData`.

## How `splits` stops being compile-time

Only one use ever needed it: the fold's `range_constexpr(ceil(splits /
block_threads))`. A runtime `range(tid, splits, block_threads)` covers it and
drops the masking the constexpr form needed. Note this **must** be a runtime
loop — over vocabulary widths the trip count is always 1, but the rule reaches
1024 splits on 4M-wide rows, where it is 4.

`grid=(splits, rows, 1)` already carried a runtime `rows` beside the constant
`splits`, so the launch side needed nothing new.

## The rule gate

At 8192 columns a row is four block-iterations at bf16 and eight at fp32; a
split trades two of them for a second kernel launch. The existing
`_MIN_SLICE_VECTORS` caps how **far** a row may be split rather than deciding
**whether** to, which is how 2 and 4 got through.

The threshold is in **columns, not vectors**: at these widths the two dtypes
agree cell for cell while their vector counts differ by two. (It is deliberately
not the same quantity as `_LONG_ROW_VECTORS` despite the equal number.)

## Measurements

flydsl 0.3.4.1, gfx950, 166 cells — rows 1..16384 × widths 2048..1M, both
dtypes — every split count timed twice in opposite orders:

| split rule | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| worst cell vs per-cell oracle | 2.362x | **1.582x** |
| cells over 1.10x | 61/166 | **33/166** |
| mean | 1.1573 | **1.0565** |
| total time given up | 196.0 µs | **117.1 µs** |

Threshold swept at 8192 / 16384 / 32768 columns; 16384 wins on all four figures,
under flydsl 0.3.4.1 and again under 0.3.2.

**The runtime split count itself costs nothing measurable.** 18 shapes, arms
alternated A/B/A/B: geometric mean 1.0019, worst cell 1.017, and every cell's
difference is inside that cell's own round-to-round spread, which runs to 4.4%.

**Scope of behaviour change:** the rule value differs only for widths
**8185..16384 at bf16** and **4093..16384 at fp32**. Every other shape selects
exactly what it selected before.

## Correctness

- Bit-identical to `torch.argmax` across the sweep's row counts at both dtypes,
  ragged `row_lens` included.
- `op_tests/test_topk_select.py` passes: table clean, `test_topk_argmax_half`
  over 48 cells, and the tie / NaN invariants at the widths this touches.
- The parity check is armed: reverting the fold's loop bound by one fails it on
  35 of 170 rows.

## Notes

- Honest limit on the ratios: the cells with the largest *ratios* are the ones
  where the whole kernel is 4–9 µs of launch overhead, so the absolute stakes in
  the rule are small — the largest absolute loss anywhere in the domain is
  15.6 µs on a 440 µs kernel. The per-shape compiles are the part worth having.
- The remaining tail (1.42–1.58x) is low-row cells where the slice floor blocks a
  large split. Mechanism understood, absolute loss 3–4 µs, and those cells are
  launch-bound in a microbenchmark — left alone rather than refit four coupled
  constants against that.
- The sweep and scoring scripts live outside this repo; happy to add them under
  `op_tests/` if that is wanted, since the in-tree comments already reference an
  `argmax_rule_fit.py` that is not present.

title: [tuning] Add DSv4 EP16 a4w4 fused-MoE tables + fix MXFP4 aux whitelist for EP shapes
body:
补上 DSv4 **EP16 + a4w4** 的 fused-MoE 调优表，并修复挡住它的 MXFP4 aux 白名单。
现有 `dsv4_fp8fp4_*` 描述的是 TP 配置（inter_dim 是 3072 被 TP 切后的值、expert 是全局 385、topk 7），
**EP 部署下命中 0 次**，MoE 全程跑启发式 kernel。

### ① 白名单修复
`gen_instances.py::SHAPES` 里 `(48, 7168, 3072, 6)  # dsv4_ep8` 的 topk 按 routed 值填成 6，
未计入 EP 下 `fused_moe.py` 的 `topk -= int(is_ep)`（EP 约定 caller 追加一个恒被 mask 的槽），
**这条在 EP 下恒不命中**；EP16 的 `expert=24` 则完全没有条目。症状：
```
discarding MXMOE config: generated MXFP4 auxiliary kernels do not cover
(expert=24, model_dim=7168, inter_dim=3072, topk=5)
```
补两条（原条目保留不动），两处同步（`moe_mxfp4_aux.py` 注释要求 Keep synchronized）：
`(48, 7168, 3072, 5)` / `(24, 7168, 3072, 5)`。codegen 重新生成 289 个实例，编译 12.7s。

### ② key 来自运行中服务的实测
单节点 EP8 起 DSv4-Pro 抓 `fused_moe` 查表 key（176 次采样，只有一个 shape）：
```
('gfx950', 256, <token>, 7168, 3072, 48, 5, Silu, bf16, fp4x2, fp4x2, per_1x32, True, False)
```
- `inter_dim=3072`（EP 不切）；`expert=48` = 384/ep_size，**不含 shared**（V4-Pro shared 是 FP8、routed 是 FP4，dtype 检查不过）
- `topk=5`：routed 6 被 EP 剥掉一列 —— 与 ① 的根因同源
- EP16 即 `expert=24`；token 档 `M = max_num_batched_tokens × dp_size`，EP8 实测上限 131072=16384×8 ⇒ EP16 为 **262144**

### ③ ⚠ a4w4 的启用配方（两个 env 必须同进同出）
```bash
ATOM_MOE_GU_ITLV=0        # gate_mode=SEPARATED + Silu → GEMM 的 A 操作数 = fp4x2
ATOM_MORI_FP4_DISPATCH=1  # MoRI dispatch wire format 也发 fp4
AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0
```
`ATOM_MOE_GU_ITLV=1`（CI 现有配方）把 A 钉成 fp8，即 a8w4。
**只开 `ATOM_MORI_FP4_DISPATCH` 会 SIGABRT**：dispatch 发 fp4 而 GEMM 要 fp8，row-width 不匹配。

### ④ 实测收益（`--run_config` E2E，16 档全部命中、0 回退、0 丢弃）
| 对比 | 收益 |
|---|---|
| 标准 tuner 表 vs 不写表（启发式） | **+11.3%**（token 512/1024 为 +33.1%/+42.1%）|
| MXMOE vs 标准 tuner（白名单补齐后） | **再 +4.3%**，赢 15/16 档（token=1024 最大 −7.6%）|
| gsm8k a4w4 vs a8w4 对照 | 0.9522 vs 0.9538，差 0.16pp 在噪声内，均过 threshold 0.94 |

最终表 = 逐点择优：MXMOE 15 行 + 标准 1 行（512 档）。
**判据是实测 E2E 而非 tuner 自报的 kernel us**（inline-quant 把 quant 算进 kernel 时间、
外部 quant 不算，比 us 会系统性偏袒后者），故表中 `us` 列在行间不可横向比较。

### 不在范围内
只覆盖 gfx950 + EP16（EP8 的 shape 已进白名单但未调优）；未改任何运行时逻辑。

title: [FlyDSL] [gfx1250] TDM dispatch for mega-moe EP
body:
The vector dispatch spends a whole wave per (token, expert-slot) route and copies the payload with per-lane 16-byte stores, which leaves gfx1250's Tensor Data Mover unused. Add a second dispatch that moves the payload by TDM, which in turn makes the per-route remote atomic and the scattered 4-byte metadata stores -- previously hidden under the copy -- worth restructuring: routes map one per lane and dedup via ballot + mbcnt_lo, recv slots are reserved one remote atomic per (block, peer) off an LDS histogram, and idx/weights/srcmap are staged into a destTokId-ordered SoA so the metadata leaves as bulk TDM runs.

Selected with dispatch_backend="tdm" (MEGA_DISPATCH=tdm); the default stays "flydsl", so existing callers are untouched. The arena state it leaves is interchangeable with the vector kernel, so gemm1, the gemm2 P2P scatter and the fused combine are unchanged.

The kernel needs its own launch schedule rather than the vector table: 32 warps of a 7168-wide bf16 payload tile want 448 KB against a 320 KB LDS budget and fail to build. tdm_max_warps clamps any spec that still names too many warps, keeping the tuned block count that paces the grid barrier.

Measured on 4x gfx1250, hidden 7168 topk 6, dispatch kernel self device time, vector -> TDM: 512 tokens/rank 109 -> 76 us, 4096 tokens/rank 1344 -> 186 us (7.2x), which is 1.72x on the whole dispatch->gemm->combine layer. That lands on par with mori's C++ TDM dispatch (82 us and 190 us at the same two points).

test_dispatch_tdm_gfx1250.py A/Bs the three implementations under the existing MegaMoE end-to-end harness, gating each on its fp32 reference check.

title: Declare fused_moe/tuned_gemm preshuffled weight layout
body:
## Motivation
reported in this issue https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/2194
`shuffle_weight()` records the preshuffled MFMA layout by setting an `is_shuffled`
attribute on the tensor it returns. A plain Python attribute is not tensor metadata,
so it does not survive tensor operations. `fused_moe` and `gemm_a16w16` then infer
"not preshuffled", select the `preshuffle_off` kernel and read preshuffled data with
the wrong layout — silently, with no error and no warning.
Measured on torch 2.10 / gfx950, the tag is lost by 8 of the 10 operations probed:
| operation | tag survives |
| --- | --- |
| `clone()`, `to(device, copy=True)`, `detach()`, `t[:]`, `view(dtype)` | no |
| `nn.Parameter(t)` | no |
| `copy.deepcopy(t)` | yes |
| `copy.deepcopy(nn.Parameter(t))` | no |
| `contiguous()` | yes, but only because it returns `self` when already contiguous |
Impact, identical config on each side:
- `fused_moe` with FP4 weights: the run-to-run noise floor is 1280 (stage2 reduces
  with atomics), while a cloned weight gives a max diff of **290816**
- `gemm_a16w16`, bf16 128x1024x512: a cloned weight gives a max diff of **139.0**,
  where the output magnitude is only ~22

## Technical Details

Add an optional `is_shuffled` argument so a caller can state the layout when the
tensor can no longer carry it:
```python
w = shuffle_weight(w_q, layout=(16, 16))
out = fused_moe(hidden, w.clone(), w2.clone(), ..., is_shuffled=True)
```
It defaults to `None`, which keeps inferring from the attribute, so no existing
caller is affected. Threaded through `fused_moe`, `fused_moe_`, `_fused_moe_impl`,
`fused_moe_2stages`, `fhmoe` and `gemm_a16w16`, with the matching `*_fake`
signatures updated so the `torch_compile_guard` schemas still line up.
`op_tests/test_moe_2stage.py` now passes the flag explicitly. Its i4x2 and int4
branches feed `shuffle_weight()`'s result through `pack_int8_to_packed_int4()` and
`.view()`, both of which return fresh tensors, so the tag was already gone before
the kernel saw it.

**Alternative considered**

Making the layout propagate on its own — a tensor subclass — is the better long-term
answer, and torchao's `AffineQuantizedTensor` shows the shape it should take: each
layout is its own type with a `Layout` / `TensorImpl` pair, `__torch_dispatch__`
intercepts every op, and `__tensor_flatten__` lets `torch.compile` see through it.

It is out of scope here for two reasons specific to a kernel library. First, a
subclass without dispatch interception is worse than none: probing one showed the tag
surviving `t[:]` and `view()`, and a slice of a preshuffled tensor is not a valid
preshuffled tensor, so the tag would keep propagating after it stopped being true.
Second, doing it properly does not close the loop from aiter alone. torchao owns the
module transform, so its subclass is what `load_state_dict` copies into; aiter does
not own module construction, and weights would still arrive as plain `nn.Parameter`
from the serving stack.

The explicit argument is needed regardless of that work: weights that arrive already
shuffled in a checkpoint, the tuner calling `ck_moe_stage*_fwd` directly, and the C++
op boundary all have no tensor able to carry a tag. `is_shuffled: bool | None` can
widen to accept a `Layout` later without breaking callers, so this is a step toward
that design rather than a competing one.


## Test Plan

`op_tests/test_is_shuffled.py` is new and covers both ops. It compares against the
untouched tensors instead of a fixed tolerance, and includes a negative control —
declaring `is_shuffled=False` for genuinely preshuffled weights must diverge — so
the test fails if the argument is ever ignored rather than passing by accident.
- `python op_tests/test_is_shuffled.py` passes
- `python op_tests/test_moe_2stage.py --no-flydsl-csv --quant 4`: 12/12 cases,
  `logits_diff` between 3.4e-06 and 1.2e-03, and the selected stage1 kernel is
  `..._MulABScaleShuffled_v3_...`, confirming the `preshuffle_on` variant is used

## Test Result

title: [HIP] Add register-resident grouped topk for single-group MoE.
body:
## Motivation

When `biased_grouped_topk` / `grouped_topk` run with no group filter (`topk_group == num_expert_group`, typically G=1), expert counts are in the hundreds to thousands and topk is in the teens to 32. Decode and small prefill launch one row per token. The existing HIP kernel stores scores in LDS and then runs sequential argmax for `topk` rounds, rescanning the full row each time, so latency grows with topk.

This PR keeps the same APIs but takes a register path: scores stay in VGPRs, and a lane-max pivot plus warp compact picks the topk, skipping the repeated LDS argmax.

## Technical Details

Only `csrc/kernels/topk_softmax_kernels_group.cu` changes:

- New kernel `topk_reg_kernel`: 1 token = 1 wave64; each lane owns `E/64` experts. Comparison scores live in VGPRs; output weights (sigmoid or softmax) are written to LDS and gathered.
- Lane-max pivot + warp compact selects topk; falls back to sequential argmax if there are too many candidates. Numerics match the original LDS kernel.
- `biased_grouped_topk` (sigmoid+bias) and `grouped_topk` (softmax or unbiased sigmoid) share `LAUNCHER_TOPK_REG`; a missed gate falls back to LDS. Biased remains sigmoid-only, matching the existing API.
- Even row stride uses vec2 loads. Odd stride misaligns the row pointer for vec2, so the same `(2L, 2L+1)` pair is loaded as scalars.

Host gates (all must hold):

- `topk_grp == num_expert_group` (no group filter)
- wave64 only (wave32 untested)
- `num_experts % 64 == 0`,  max: 2048， now ues whitelist {128, 192, 256, 384, 512, 896, 1024, 2048}
- topk in [4, 32]

dtypes: fp32 / fp16 / bf16. `gating_output` / `correction_bias` share a dtype; `topk_weights` stay fp32.

## Test Plan

No new test file. Reuse `op_tests/test_moeTopkSoftmax.py`: G=1 hits the register path; a group filter still hits LDS.

title: [FlyDSL] [Feature] Support FP8 output in gather_kv_b_proj
body:
Adds FP8 (E4M3) output support to FlyDSL `gather_kv_b_proj`, including K's RoPE columns. The kernel uses caller-supplied device descales to write FP8 K/V directly from its FP32 epilogue, eliminating intermediate BF16 buffers and separate K/V quantization launches.

Measured on gfx950 with 12 heads, latent dimension 512, K dimension 192 and V dimension 128. Both paths use the same precomputed scales; calibration is excluded from timing.

| Cached tokens | BF16 FlyDSL gather + HIP quantization | Direct FP8 gather | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2,048 | 26.52 µs | 12.55 µs | 2.11× |
| 8,192 | 47.41 µs | 32.74 µs | 1.45× |
| 16,384 | 83.34 µs | 56.65 µs | 1.47× |

Accuracy validation passed: **91 GPU tests** in `op_tests/test_flydsl_gather_kv_b_proj.py`. Existing UTs cover BF16/FP8 outputs, both weight layouts and scale modes, 12/16 heads, 128+128 and 192+256 projection dimensions, RoPE and tail handling. FP8-specific checks cover rounding boundaries, saturation, scale validation and graph replay.

title: [FlyDSL] Enable FP8 FMHA split-K for short cached-prefix queries

Measured on gfx950: B=1, Q=70, H=12, Dq=Dk=192, Dv=128, `return_lse=True`. Both versions use automatic split selection.

| KV tokens | Base (`246efe910`) | PR (`38f239361`) | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

Median of 7 rounds × 100 CUDA graph replays per mode, after 5 warmups. Includes attention and split combine; excludes quantization and JIT compilation. PyTorch 2.10.0 / ROCm 7.2.4, FlyDSL 0.3.2.

Accuracy validation: **27 targeted GPU tests passed** in `op_tests/test_flydsl_fmha.py`, covering short-query splits, output/LSE references, variable-length inputs, custom softmax scales, graph replay, and rejection of causal short-query split-K. Black and Ruff passed.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Config] gfx1151 gemma4 attn prefill tuning
body:
Tuning for large head_size=512 attn_2d tuning for Strix Halo, of fp8/bf16 KV cache.

## Motivation
vLLM's default `TRITON_ATTN` backend doesn't offer optimal tuning config for gfx1151, and there isn't per-arch tunning opportunity.

## Test Result

### Kernel-level, bf16 KV / bf16 Q

| kv_len | q_len | block | TRITON_ATTN (ms) | AITER before (ms) | AITER tuned (ms) | tuned vs before (improvement) | tuned vs TRITON_ATTN (improvement) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32,768 | 32,768 | 16 | 12830.31 | 4215.41 | 2211.04 | 1.91× | 5.80× |
| 32,768 | 32,768 | 64 | 11119.52 | 4050.21 | 2265.70 | 1.79× | 4.91× |
| 32,768 | 2,048 | 16 | 1390.79 | 425.65 | 205.97 | 2.07× | 6.75× |
| 32,768 | 2,048 | 64 | 1296.01 | 432.48 | 200.48 | 2.16× | 6.46× |

### Kernel-level, fp8 KV / bf16 Q

| kv_len | TRITON_ATTN (ms) | AITER before (ms) | AITER tuned (ms) | tuned vs before (improvement) | tuned vs TRITON_ATTN (improvement) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32,768 | 1452.3 | 971.8 | 615.1 | 1.58× | 2.36× |
| 60,000 | 2723.7 | 1789.8 | 1193.2 | 1.50× | 2.28× |

### Model-level, `vllm bench serve`

32768-in / 32-out, `--max-num-seqs 1`, `--max-concurrency 1`, `--num-prompts 4`

| backend | KV | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| TRITON_ATTN | bf16 | 146005.21 | 73.58 |
| ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN | bf16 | 20117.60 | 50.59 |
| TRITON_ATTN | fp8 | 164764.79 | 85.09 |
| ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN | fp8 | 63824.95 | 70.63 |

| comparison | Median TTFT improvement | Median TPOT improvement|
|---|---:|---:|
| tuned vs TRITON_ATTN, bf16 KV | 7.26× | 1.45× |
| tuned vs TRITON_ATTN, fp8 KV | 2.58× | 1.20× |

## Potential problem
Using TRITON=`3.8.0+git4cff872c.rocm10.1.0a20260811`, the compiler has an **uneven** cost upcasting fp8 to bf16/fp16, and the following local patch is required in vLLM to always pass in bf16 Q into the kernel.
`vllm/v1/attention/backends/rocm_aiter_unified_attn.py`, in `RocmAiterUnifiedAttentionImpl.__init__`:

```python
from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx11
self.supports_quant_query_input = not on_gfx11()
```

Without it, `Attention.__init__` builds a `query_quant` whenever the KV cache is fp8 (`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py:464-470`) and the query is quantized alongside the KV cache to fp8. 

### REASON
As gfx1151 has no fp8 WMMA, passing in fp8 Q is not only a pure precision loss, but also causes the kernel to regress up to 4 times. The Triton compiler's current default WMMA upcasting dtype is fp16, not bf16. Fp16 uses a lot more cmp instructions and causes the kernel to regress badly. Leaving Q in bf16, then inside kernel do `K_load.to(Q.dtype)`, `V_load.to(Q.dtype)` explicitly uses bf16 and bypasses the compiler problem. This is what the above table measurements are based on.

For conclusion, this is a pure use case problem, and this PR stays valid. Investigation into Triton compiler's RDNA3 fp8 upcasting dtype (fp16/bf16) is ongoing.

title: [Config] Add Qwen3.8-27B TP1 a8w8 blockscale GEMM tunings for gfx942
body:
## What this adds

**641 tuned `a8w8_blockscale` rows in one file** — 249 decode (M ≤ 512) and 392 prefill (M 907…65536) — covering the five GEMM widths Qwen3.8-27B drives at **TP1** on gfx942 / `cu_num=304`: `down` 5120×17408, `out_proj` 5120×6144, `in_proj` 16384×5120, `qkv` 14336×5120, `gate_up` 34816×5120.

The accompanying untuned CSV is the shape list these were tuned from. It was extracted from real vLLM server logs rather than generated as an M ladder, so the M grid is what the scheduler actually requests.

#3324 tuned this model family at TP=2/4/8 only, so the TP1 widths were never covered and every call fell back to the default — **275 `not found tuned config` messages per profile run, now 4.**

## Results — decode

This config against AITER's own default, measured in a real vLLM serving run — Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, 128K context, max-concurrency 1, one MI325X — with byte-identical images and the config bind-mount as the only variable, three interleaved repeats per arm on an idle node.

| | AITER default | this PR | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| decode step | 15.444 ms | **12.449 ms** | **1.24×** |

Per-shape decode GEMM against the default, µs/call: `down` 2.33×, `out_proj` 1.51×, `in_proj` 1.12×, `qkv` 1.00×, `gate_up` 1.00×. Decode-step spread across repeats was 0.037 ms (default) and 0.012 ms (this PR). **No decode shape regresses.**



## Method and validation

- Tuned with `csrc/ck_gemm_a8w8_blockscale/gemm_a8w8_blockscale_tune.py --libtype ck --splitK`. Decode rows were re-timed with an interleaved sweep-then-verify pass, because the tuner's `min()` over short samples is noisy on near-ties. Only rows beating the default by ≥3% were kept, following #5421.
- `op_tests/tuning_tests/test_csv_validation.py` (15 tests) and `test_config_shape_collision.py` (17 tests) both pass.
- **Zero duplicate `(gfx, cu_num, M, N, K)` keys** — against all 12 other sources in the runtime merge set on `main` (40,892 rows), and against the three open PRs that touch those same files (#5602, #5278, #5186), none of which adds a gfx942/304 row at these widths. No pre-existing rows for these five `(N, K)` pairs. `update_config_files` raises on duplicates. Nearest related open work is #5586, which routes *untuned* blockscale shapes to triton; these rows make the same shapes tuned, so the two do not collide.
- **Kernel parity**, not a model evaluation: max relative Frobenius error against an fp32 reference is 4.11e-3, against bf16's `2^-8` = 3.9e-3 rounding floor. Every row has tuner `errRatio` ≤ 0.0002.

## Scope and caveats

- **Only the decode rows have in-situ evidence.** The prefill rows carry tuner measurements only, for the reason above.
- **MI300X is also gfx942 / 304 CUs**, so these rows are selected there too and cannot be scoped out without changing the lookup key. Measurement here is MI325X only. #3324's own environment section records its configs as measured on MI300X, so gfx942/304 rows already move in both directions.
- **Two rows pin AITER's default kernel** (`qkv` and `gate_up` at M=1), after the serving trace measured the tuned picks at 0.94× and 0.98× in situ — the 1.00× entries above. Pinned rather than deleted: `getPaddedM(1, N, K, 0) == 16`, so a deleted M=1 row lands on the M=16 row, not the default.
- **Six decode shapes ship no row** — `qkv` and `in_proj` at M=24 and M=32, `out_proj` at M=104 and M=112 — near-ties that did not clear the 3% bar and fall back.
- **`gate_up` ships 72 prefill rows, not 80.** The 8 missing ones are shapes where `M*N > INT32_MAX` and the CK kernel faults during tuning. At runtime `getPaddedM` collapses M > 8192 to 8192 at these widths, so they inherit the tuned M=8192 row rather than going untuned.
- One model, one context length, one concurrency point, one node.

## Summary

_auto_num_splits targets 4x CU worth of blocks, which underfills the device on the shapes vLLM issues for DeepSeek-V4 indexer prefill. Raising the target to 16x fills it.

At seq_len 1024 / seq_len_kv 131072 the 4x target picks 3 splits: 1536 blocks over 304 CUs, six launched waves at 84.2% occupancy, the last holding 16 blocks. At 16x it picks 10 splits — 5120 blocks, 17 waves, 99.1%.

title: [HIP] [OPUS] [JIT] fix(jit): baton liveness is undecidable from pid+host under --network host
body:
Fixes #5266.

## The bug

`FileBaton` records its holder as **pid + hostname**. A container started with `docker run --network host` — the normal way to run a tuner — reports the **host's** hostname while keeping its **own PID namespace**, and every container has a pid 1 and low worker pids (100-104).

So when a tuner container is killed mid-build, the next container reads the leaked lock, sees a matching hostname, checks `os.kill(103, 0)`, finds **its own worker** at pid 103, and concludes the dead holder is alive. Its workers then wait forever:

```
[pid=101 pname=SpawnPoolWorker-1] waiting for baton release at
    .../lock_module_gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle_cktile_tune
```

With a host-mounted build cache the leak survives container restarts, so the wedge is **permanent** until someone deletes the file by hand. "Delete the lock files first" became a required step in our tuning runbook.

## The fix

Record the **PID namespace** (`/proc/self/ns/pid`) and the holder's **start time** (`/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22) alongside pid and host:

| holder | decision |
|---|---|
| same namespace | pid alive **and** start time matches → live. This also closes the pid-reuse hole on any host. |
| other namespace | the pid is meaningless here, so decide on a **heartbeat**: the holder touches the lock every `heartbeat_seconds` while it works; a lock untouched for `heartbeat_stale_seconds` (default 60 s) is stale. |
| different host | unchanged — never steal. |

Locks written by an older AITER carry two lines; they parse with empty ns/start-time and keep exactly the previous behaviour.

## Checked

Self-held lock never looks stale · foreign-namespace holder with a live local pid is respected **while heartbeating** and goes stale when it stops · recycled pid caught via start time · dead pid · legacy 2-line locks (live and dead) · 0-byte orphan grace unchanged · `wait()` returns False after breaking a stale lock · heartbeat observed touching the file.

Same campaign as #5262 / #5268 / #5263–#5265.

title: [feat] add no_combine flag in 2-stage MoE backend
body:
## Motivation

Adds an opt-in NoCombine template flag that returns CK MoE's per-route [NumTokens, TopK, model_dim]
output (unweighted, no atomic combine) so callers can apply their own post-expert op.

## Technical Details

Adds `no_combine: bool = False` to `aiter.fused_moe`. When `no_combine=True`, the function returns the per-route, *unweighted* output of shape `(M, topk, model_dim)` instead of the default combined `(M, model_dim)`. Downstream callers (e.g. GPT-OSS-style pipelines) apply their own topk weighting / mixing.

### Scope

- Backend: CK 2-stage only (rejects FlyDSL, CK-Tile, ASM stage1; rejects `metadata.run_1stage`; rejects non-CK stage2).
- Quant:   `QuantType.No` only (rejects per_Tensor / per_Token / per_1x128 / per_1x32).
- Dtype:   bf16 inputs, bf16 weights, bf16 output (rejects `dtype=` override).
- Stage1 weighting: rejects `doweight_stage1=True`.

### CK template (submodule bump)

`3rdparty/composable_kernel` needs a separate upstream PR (https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-libraries/pull/7773)

### Aiter wrapper

`csrc/ck_gemm_moe_2stages_codegen/gemm_moe_ck2stages_common.cuh` forwards the new template parameter to `DeviceMoeGemm` only when `AITER_CK_HAS_NO_COMBINE_TEMPLATE` is defined; otherwise a `static_assert(!NoCombine, ...)` fails the build for any `NoCombine=true` instantiation. `aiter/jit/core.py` threads the env var of the same name into hipcc `-D` flags.

### Codegen

`csrc/ck_gemm_moe_2stages_codegen/gen_instances.py` adds a `NoCombine: bool = False` field to `kernelInstanceGEMM2`; the `.name` property carries `NoCombine0` / `NoCombine1` after the existing `MulRoutedWeight{0,1}` suffix. The 8 per-dtype `gemm2_heuristic_dispatch` templates branch on `{NoCombine} == no_combine`, and every stage2 `ck_moe_stage2_gemm<...>` template call now appends the `NoCombine` bool. A new `--no_combine` CLI flag emits the `(QuantType.No × b16)` stage2 instances and `parser.error()`s for any combination outside v1 scope.

### Python plumbing

`ck_moe_stage2` / `ck_moe_stage2_fwd` / `cmdGenFunc_ck_moe_stage2` / `get_moe_stage_module` (`aiter/ops/moe_op.py`), the C++ binding (`csrc/include/moe_ck.h`), the dispatcher
(`csrc/ck_gemm_moe_2stages_codegen/gemm_moe_ck2stages.cu`), and the pybind macro (`csrc/include/rocm_ops.hpp`) all expose `no_combine: bool = False` end-to-end. `get_moe_stage_module` appends `--no_combine` to the JIT `blob_gen_cmd` and tags the module name with `_no_combine`. The C++ dispatcher force-empties `kernelName2` when `no_combine=true` so the heuristic dispatch is used instead of the tuned table (which only has `NoCombine0` entries today).

`fused_moe_2stages`'s `no_combine` branch pre-zeros a `(token_num, topk, model_dim)` buffer, calls
`metadata.stage2(..., per_route_out, sorted_weights=None, no_combine=True)`, and zeros `per_route_out[k_local:]` when the caller passed `num_local_tokens`. The pre-zero is required by the EP zero-fill contract (non-local routes and `num_local_tokens` tails must be exactly zero in the per-route output).

## Test Plan

40passes in op_tests/test_moe_no_combine.py

## Test Result

Performance (MI350X, gfx950, `AITER_CK_HAS_NO_COMBINE_TEMPLATE=1`)

50-iter trim-10/10/10 mean:

| Shape                                | combined | no_combine | ratio |
|--------------------------------------|----------|------------|-------|
| M=256,  topk=2, D=4096, E=8          | 0.192 ms | 0.193 ms   | 1.006×|
| M=2048, topk=8, D=4096, E=8          | 1.906 ms | 2.073 ms   | 1.088×|

title: fix(tuned_gemm): honour otype instead of casting a BF16 result to it
body:
## What

`otype` says what dtype to produce. Two dispatch paths implemented it as
"compute, then cast", so a caller asking a BF16 GEMM for an FP32 output got
the accumulator rounded to BF16 and widened again — every value on the BF16
grid, which is exactly the precision it asked not to have.

**torch path.** `F.linear` returns the input dtype, so widening its result
afterwards preserves nothing. `torch.mm`'s `out_dtype` writes the accumulator
instead.

**skinny path.** `wvSpltK` / `LLMM1` / `wv_splitk_small_fp16_bf16` all allocate
their output at the input dtype and have no FP32 variant, so a shape asking for
a wider output must not select one. Those shapes fall to torch, which now
writes the accumulator.

Both now agree with the tuned ASM (`bf16gemm_fp32bf16_*`) and OPUS kernels,
which have always written the accumulator out.

Also adds a tuned config for `N=1024 K=5120` BF16→FP32 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's
fused compressor projection).

## Evidence

Output is on the BF16 grid iff it was rounded, so
`torch.equal(y, y.bfloat16().float())` separates the two cases:

| path | `\|y − exact fp32\|` | on BF16 grid |
|---|---|---|
| torch, before | 9.3e-4 | yes |
| torch, after | 3e-8 | no |
| ASM `bf16gemm_fp32bf16_*` | 3e-6 | no |
| OPUS | 1e-5 | no |

BF16 output is untouched: bit-identical to `F.linear` with and without bias,
and skinny is still selected when `otype == dtype`.

## Note on the tuned rows

Rows are ASM at or below M=1536 and OPUS above. `get_padded_m` lets a shape
reach a nearby row, and an OPUS row is revalidated against the original M
rather than the padded one, so a padded hit on it is discarded — M=17..31 and
M=49..63 silently fell back until those two rows became ASM.

Swept 503 values of M in [1, 16384]: none land on the BF16 grid, worst
`|y − exact fp32|` = 1.4e-5.

FlyDSL is excluded from these rows on purpose. Its `abf16_wbf16_fp32` kernels
round the accumulator to BF16 before storing, so the FP32 in the name is the
container, not the precision; the tuner ranks by time and its accuracy gate for
an FP32 output is `rtol = atol = 1e-2`, which a BF16-rounded result of this
magnitude passes.

## Test plan

- [x] BF16 output path bit-identical to `F.linear`, with and without bias
- [x] skinny still selected for `otype == dtype`, bypassed when wider
- [x] 503 values of M swept for the new tuned shape
- [ ] CI

title: [Triton/Gluon] Add scattered-pointer Q4_K_M MoE matvec kernel for streaming inference
body:
## Motivation

This kernel is the AITER-side primitive for a license-clean llama.cpp fork at https://github.com/ssubbotin/llama.cpp/tree/feature/moe-expert-gpu-cache, which adds a `--moe-stream-dir` flag for streaming-MoE inference: active experts live in a per-(layer, projection) VRAM LRU cache and cold experts page in from NVMe SSD on demand. Each cache slot holds one expert at an arbitrary device address; top-k routing picks K slots per token. This kernel consumes that scattered-pointer layout directly, so the engine never has to gather the K active experts into a contiguous slab before dispatch.

End-to-end this lets large MoE models run on GPUs that can't fit the full expert set in VRAM. Measured on the same fork unchanged: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Q4_K_M (17 GiB of weights) streams on a 16 GB RX 9070 XT at **21.72 tg64 tok/s**, with the OS page cache absorbing nearly all the streaming I/O after the first forward pass (cold/warm gap ≈ 13%). The same engine and the same kernel source compile and run unchanged on MI300X (gfx942), RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120), RX 9070 XT (gfx1201), and Strix Halo APU (gfx1151) — see the cross-architecture table under [Numbers](#numbers).

## Summary

Adds a Triton MoE matvec kernel that consumes K active experts from K **separate device buffers**, indexed by an array of per-expert device pointers plus a `(token, slot) -> unique-expert` remap. This is the core primitive needed for **streaming-MoE inference**, where expert weights are too large to fit fully in VRAM and live as slots in a per-(layer, projection) LRU cache fed from NVMe SSD on demand.

Existing AITER MoE kernels assume a contiguous `(E, N, K)` expert tensor; the streaming case has the K active experts scattered across K cache slots whose absolute device addresses are only known at dispatch time. This kernel consumes those addresses directly, avoiding the per-dispatch device-to-device slab copy that a contiguous-tensor wrapper would require.

**Format**: GGUF Q4_K_M, the dominant on-disk MoE quantization (super-block of 256 elements, 144 bytes/block: 4-byte `dm` + 12-byte packed scales/mins + 128 bytes of nibbles). The kernel decodes the layout in registers — no host-side repack needed.

**Kernel design**: each program tiles `BLOCK_SIZE_N` output rows for one (token, slot). The Q4_K_M block-loop unrolls the 8 sub-blocks (4 il-groups × low+high nibble), avoiding both 2D gather operations and runtime nibble-position arithmetic. `BLOCK_SIZE_N` is autotuned over `{4, 8, 16, 32}`.

## Files

- ` aiter/ops/triton/_triton_kernels/moe/moe_op_q4k_streaming.py` — Triton kernel
- ` aiter/ops/triton/moe/moe_op_q4k_streaming.py` — Python wrapper
- ` op_tests/triton_tests/moe/q4k_pack_reference.py` — pure-numpy Q4_K_M packer + reference dequant
- ` op_tests/triton_tests/moe/test_moe_q4k_streaming.py` — pytest correctness against the reference
- ` op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_moe_q4k_streaming.py` — microbenchmark over realistic MoE shapes

## Validation

The pure-numpy reference dequant is **byte-exact** against `dequantize_row_q4_K` in `libggml.so` (separate cross-validation, 23 random + edge-case blocks). The Triton kernel matches the numpy reference across 8 shapes, from synthetic edge cases to a production Qwen3-A17B-shaped expert (`n_dim_in=2048, n_dim_out=1408, K=8, n_used_per_token=8`).

## Numbers

MI300X (gfx942, ROCm 7.0.0, Triton 3.4), autotuned, fp32 in / fp32 out:

| workload                   |  ms   | GB/s | GFLOPS |
| -------------------------- | ----- | ---- | ------ |
| mixtral8x7b_gate_up_decode | 0.104 | 632  | 2248   |
| mixtral8x7b_down_decode    | 0.127 | 520  | 1847   |
| dsv3_gate_up_decode        | 0.107 | 618  | 2196   |
| dsv3_down_decode           | 0.096 | 689  | 2449   |
| qwen35_397b_gate_up_decode | 0.030 | 477  | 1697   |
| qwen35_397b_down_decode    | 0.025 | 564  | 2006   |
| mixtral8x7b_gate_up_b8     | 0.707 | 374  | 2656   |

### Cross-architecture portability

Same kernel source, same bench script, no per-arch code paths or `#ifdef`s. Triton compiles the kernel for each backend; AITER's autotuner picks `BLOCK_SIZE_N` per device. All 8 pytest correctness cases pass on each architecture.

| Workload                     | MI300X GB/s | Blackwell GB/s | RX 9070 XT GB/s | Strix Halo GB/s |
|------------------------------|------------:|---------------:|----------------:|----------------:|
| mixtral8x7b_gate_up_decode   |         646 |            498 |             262 |             118 |
| mixtral8x7b_down_decode      |         519 |            436 |             240 |             106 |
| dsv3_gate_up_decode          |         627 |            520 |             270 |             118 |
| dsv3_down_decode             |         695 |            529 |             262 |             121 |
| qwen35_397b_gate_up_decode   |         484 |            364 |             240 |             110 |
| qwen35_397b_down_decode      |         566 |            460 |             223 |             109 |
| mixtral8x7b_gate_up_b8       |         375 |            295 |             130 |              70 |

Peaks: 695 / 529 / 270 / 121 GB/s. Backends, in order: ROCm 7.0.0 + Triton 3.4 (MI300X), CUDA 13.0 + Triton 3.6 (Blackwell), ROCm 7.2.2 + Triton 3.6 (RX 9070 XT), TheRock ROCm 7.13.0a + Triton 3.6 (Strix Halo).

The kernel is decode-style memory-bound. Further gains (toward HBM3 peak) would come from wider weight loads (uint32-packed nibbles) and wave-level reduction; left as a follow-up so this change stays focused on the scattered-pointer primitive.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [CI] [GFX950] Fix mha_varlen_with_pe miscompile and optimize perf
body:
This PR aims to fix the backend compiler mis-compile error on `op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_mha_with_pe.py::test_mha_varlen_with_pe[True-0.17-96-64-8-1-64-128]`

**CORE Changes**:

* Hoist the `p = tl.where(dropout_mask, p, 0.0)` just before `sd_mask` store to reduce the live range of sgpr for `dropout` cmp.
* Remove the `dropout_mask` from passing as a param and keep it kernel local, since it's never used outside the kernel + tune the config
* Use i32 offset if i64 is not necessary.

The changes reduce the GPR pressure a lot. vgpr: 914 -> 83, sgpr: 248 -> 42, no sgpr->vgpr spill in loop body.


**Root Cause** of the failure is similar to [#5463](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5463):

```asm
; Buggy code piece
8886: v_readlane_b32 s0, v253, 4     ; K address low
8887: v_readlane_b32 s1, v253, 5     ; K address high
8888: v_readlane_b32 s2, v253, 6
8889: v_readlane_b32 s3, v253, 7

8890: s_and_b32 s1, s1, 0xffff       ; format address high word
8891: s_mov_b32 s3, 0x27000          ; descriptor configuration
8892: s_mov_b32 s2, 0x7ffffffe       ; descriptor range

8893: v_writelane_b32 v253, s0, 4
8898: v_writelane_b32 v253, s1, 5
8899: v_writelane_b32 v253, s2, 6
8900: v_writelane_b32 v253, s3, 7

      ; ...other initialization...

9020: .LBB0_12:                     ; loop starts HERE

9023: v_readlane_b32 s8,  v253, 4    ; s8  = K_low
9027: v_readlane_b32 s9,  v253, 5    ; s9  = K_high
9028: v_readlane_b32 s10, v253, 6    ; s10 = range
9029: v_readlane_b32 s11, v253, 7    ; s11 = configuration

      ; ...calculate this tile's offsets...

9088: buffer_load_dwordx4 v[34:37], v32, s[8:11], 0 offen   ; Load K using the descriptor in s[8:11].
9093: buffer_load_dwordx2 v[38:39], v32, s[8:11], 0 offen   ; Load K's positional-encoding portion.

13559: v_writelane_b32 v253, s12, 4   ; slot 4 = dropout-output address low
13580: v_writelane_b32 v253, s13, 5   ; slot 5 = dropout-output address high
13600: v_writelane_b32 v253, s14, 6
13607: v_writelane_b32 v253, s15, 7
13671: buffer_store_dword v43, v42, s[12:15], 0 offen

       ; ...other pointer/offset updates...

15884: s_cbranch_scc1 .LBB0_12       ; if SCC == 1, repeat the loop
```

From the asm code piece we can see that the descriptor spill slot 4-7 of v253 is polluted by `sd_mask` in the first iter of the loop,  and the s[8:11] for K is incorrect when read back with `v_readlane` in the second iter.

By proper reordering + removing the sgpr spill in-loop , this error case cannot be encountered.

cc: @Dewei-Wang-sh

title: [CI] Use PR aiter when installing Flash Attention Triton
body:
## Motivation

Flash Attention Triton integration currently installs Dao-AILab/flash-attention before overlaying the PR checkout of AITER. Flash Attention's setup.py initializes and installs its pinned third_party/aiter submodule first, which can point at an older AITER commit with stale dependencies. This currently fails during Docker build because the pinned submodule requires flydsl==0.1.9.dev599, which is not available on the index.

## Changes

- Copy the PR AITER checkout into the Docker image before installing Flash Attention.
- Replace /flash-attention/third_party/aiter with the PR checkout before running pip install for Flash Attention v2.
- Apply the same replacement order to the v3 Dockerfile.
- Remove /flash-attention/.git before install so Flash Attention setup.py does not reset third_party/aiter back to the pinned submodule commit.
- Keep the final editable install from /aiter so the installed amd-aiter points at the PR checkout.

## Validation

- Ran git diff --check.
- Parsed .github/workflows/flash_attention_integration.yaml with PyYAML.

Fixes #5611

title: [Config] [tuning] Add DSv4 a4w4 fused-MoE tuning tables for gfx950
body:
补上 DSv4 的 a4w4（activation + weight 均为 mxfp4，per_1x32）fused-MoE 调优表。
`model_configs` 下 DSv4 此前只有 a8w4 的 `dsv4_fp8fp4_*`，没有纯 fp4 activation 的表。

### 内容
- `dsv4_a4w4_untuned_fmoe.csv` — 沿用 `dsv4_fp8fp4_untuned_fmoe.csv` 的 6 组 shape × 16 档 token(1..32768)，只把 `q_dtype_a` 改为 `torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2`
- `dsv4_a4w4_tuned_fmoe.csv` — MI355X (gfx950, 256 CU) 上的调优结果，96 行

### 怎么调的
两条 tuner 路径各自全量调优后**逐点择优合并**：
- 标准 fmoe tuner → g1 = `flydsl_moe1_afp4_wfp4_*`（外部 quant），24 行胜出
- `--mxfp4-flydsl` 耦合 tuner → g1 = `flydsl_mxmoe_g1_a4w4_*`（inline quant），72 行胜出

两套各 96 shape 全部调优成功，cosine_diff 0.9~1.2%。

### ⚠ 择优口径是 E2E，不是表里的 us 列
两条路径对 quant 的计量方式不同：inline-quant 把 quant 算进 kernel 时间，外部 quant 不算。
直接比 `us` 会系统性偏向后者。实测对比：

| 判据 | flydsl : 标准 | 合并结果 |
|---|---|---|
| kernel `us`（各 tuner 自报） | 55 : 41 | 38/96 条劣于逐点最优 |
| **E2E（`--run_config` 实测）** | **72 : 24** | 达到逐点最优 |

**因此表中 `us` 列在行间不可横向比较**——它是各 tuner 在自己口径下量的 kernel 时间。
后续 retune 若只看 `us` 会得到不同的择优结果。

### 验收
`--run_config` 实测 E2E：
- 96/96 状态 OK，**无一行回退到启发式配置**
- 相对全取标准路径平均快 **8.61%**，81/96 个点更快
- 相对逐点最优偏离 -0.57%

### 不在范围内
- 只在 gfx950 上调的，没有其他 arch 的数据
- 没有改任何代码，纯配置表

title: [Perf] Route untuned a8w8 blockscale GEMMs to triton above a per-arch M
body:
`gemm_a8w8_blockscale` picks its CK instance from a table keyed on `(gfx, cu_num, M, N, K)`. When a shape is absent, `get_CKGEMM_config` returns `None` and the dispatcher calls `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_ck` with no `kernelName` and no `splitK` — one fixed tile shape at every M. That instance cannot fill the MFMA pipeline at prefill-sized M: on gfx950 it holds 385–421 TFLOP/s from M=512 all the way to M=16384, while the triton kernel, which buckets its config by M, reaches 1041.

Untuned is the common case rather than a corner. On `gfx950/cu_num=256` the shipped table has no row for any of Qwen3-14B-FP8's four linear shapes, and of the 115 distinct `(N, K)` that one host's fp8 `weight_block_size [128,128]` checkpoints ask for across TP ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8}, 88 have no tuned row. Per-model tuning closes shapes one checkpoint at a time — #5485, #5343, #5585, #4816 and #5219 are all that — but the set is not bounded by anything aiter controls. On this entry point a tuned row cannot select triton at all: the `libtype` dispatch here accepts `ck` and `cktile` and asserts otherwise, unlike `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle`, which honours `libtype == "triton"`.

So when no tuned config exists and M is at or above a per-arch threshold, dispatch to the triton kernel rather than the default CK instance. Triton loses at decode-sized M, so the threshold is measured rather than derived: 384 on gfx950 (MI355X, cu_num=256) and 2048 on gfx942 (MI325X, cu_num=304). An arch absent from the table keeps the CK fallback at every M, so gfx1250, gfx1201 (#4322) and anything new are unchanged by construction.

The triton call that the unsupported-arch fallback already made is factored out and reused; it takes CK's inputs as they are apart from the `uint8` → `fp8` view.

Scope: the non-preshuffled entry point only. `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle`, the asm and FlyDSL paths are untouched, a tuned shape takes the branch it took before, and `get_CKGEMM_config` was already on this path and is cached, so no lookup is added. This composes with per-shape tuning rather than competing with it — the predicate stops firing for a shape the moment that shape gets a row.

`op_tests/test_gemm_a8w8_blockscale_fallback.py` pins the dispatch rather than the speed: untuned takes triton at and above the threshold and CK below it, a tuned shape takes CK at every M, and an arch with no threshold never routes. The tuned config and the arch are injected rather than read from the shipped CSV, so tuning one of these shapes cannot make a case vacuous, and the arch gate is covered for gfx940/941/1250 without that hardware.

Measurements for both arches are in a comment below.

---

Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom); reviewed and measured by hand.

title: [Triton/Gluon] Create benchmark for `fused_add_rmsnorm_pad.py`
body:
## Motivation

`fused_add_rmsnorm_pad` ships a gfx942/gfx950 Triton kernel and a gfx1250 Gluon kernel but has no benchmark, so there is no way to put a metric on the numbers without a driver. Therefore, a benchmark file must be made.

The op is also not covered by the model benchmarking tool because it is absent from `model_shapes.json` and `KERNEL_DICT` (commented out in `bench_models.py`), so it cannot be reached through `bench_models.py`.

## Technical Details

Shape-driven benchmark following a neighbouring kernels `bench_rmsnorm.py` layout:
- same `get_x_vals`/`run_benchmark`/`parse_args`/`main` structure, 
- same `triton.testing.Benchmark` + `perf_report` + `do_bench(warmup=25, rep=100)`, and, 
- it reuses the tester's `generate_inputs` rather than duplicating input construction.

Organized around what the kernel actually specializes on. The Triton kernel has exactly two constexprs, `HAS_RES` and `BLOCK_SIZE_N`, and launches one program per row, so the sweep varies `M`, `N`, `--add-residual` and `--pad-to-multiple`, where,

```
N_out        = cdiv(N, pad_to_multiple) * pad_to_multiple   (else N)
BLOCK_SIZE_N = next_power_of_2(N_out)
```

15 default shapes, each grouped differently:

| category | shapes | source |
|---|---|---|
| M scaling at a fixed compiled variant | (1 … 16384, 2880) | `BLOCK_SIZE_N` held constant |
| tester widths, different `BLOCK_SIZE_N` buckets | (8192, 4/16/320/640) | `test_fused_add_rmsnorm_pad.py::parametrize("N", …)` |
| production width | N = 2880 | in tester list, but also GPT-OSS 120B's hidden size in `model_shapes.json` |
| aligned powers of two (without padding) | (8192, 512/1024/2048/4096) | isolates the norm from the pad |

#### Memory accounting
reflects the padding asymmetry. Reads are `N` wide, the write is `N_out` wide; `HAS_RES` adds one read and one write. `n_out` is computed exactly as the wrapper computes it. FLOPs are computed as: `flops = 4 * M * N + (M * N if add_residual else 0)`

#### Backend pinned to Triton
The wrapper defaults to Gluon on gfx1250 and Triton elsewhere, so an unpinned benchmark would measure a different kernel per architecture. Pinning is a **no-op** on **gfx950/gfx942** which I verified by kernel trace, `backend=None` and `backend="triton"` dispatch the identical kernel and takes effect only on gfx1250, where it keeps the numbers comparable with every other target.

No model mode: `--model`/`-M`/`--model-configs` are deliberately absent rather than inherited, since nothing associates this op with a model. A `model_benchmarking_shapes` stub is left as a TODO for if there requires future support for this kernel.

## Test Plan

- Every CLI path exercised: default sweep, `--shape`, all metrics and dtypes, `--add-residual`, `--pad-to-multiple`, `-o`
- Kernel trace to confirm the pinned backend dispatches `_fused_add_rmsnorm_pad` and never the Gluon kernel
- `rocprofv3 --kernel-trace` kernel time
- `black` and `ruff` checks, as well as `pytest` check

## Test Result

Default sweep, bandwidth, gfx950:

```
       M       N   GB/s              M       N   GB/s
       1    2880    2.6           8192       4   14.0
      32    2880   56.9           8192      16   57.7
     256    2880  445.7           8192     320 1056.2
    1024    2880 1677.0           8192     640 1902.7
    4096    2880 3712.9           8192     512 1612.6
    8192    2880 4590.6           8192    1024 2755.4
   16384    2880 5174.2           8192    2048 4199.9
                                  8192    4096 5101.1
```

Cross-check against `rocprofv3` kernel timing at `M=8192 N=2880`: benchmark 21.6 µs vs kernel 18.9 µs. The *2.7* µs gap is the wrapper's per-call `torch.empty` allocations, which `do_bench` includes and a kernel trace does not.
**note**: This is no longer the case. This happens with triton's default `do_bench` which clears L2 cache before starting the kernel event. Every event starts with a cleared cache, and this runtime entry is what causes the slight gap we see.



A larger gap (6.5 µs) with `--add-residual`, which allocates two tensors.

Backend pin verified as a no-op on gfx950: `backend=None` and `backend="triton"` both dispatch `_fused_add_rmsnorm_pad`, 3 dispatches each.

### Regression this makes measurable

Not addressed by this PR. This will be filed separately as a compiler issue with ATT traces.

| shape | Triton 3.4 | Triton 3.8 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| M=8192 N=2880 | 17.559 µs | 18.863 µs | **+7.4 %** |
| M=8192 N=2880, pad=256 | 18.889 µs | 19.389 µs | **+2.6 %** |

`rocprofv3 --kernel-trace`, 250 iters + 25 warmup, with single-average number (10% off head and 10% off tail, average the middle 80%). This is not reachable by any launch parameter - `num_warps`, `waves_per_eu` and `BLOCK_SIZE_N` were all tested and every candidate was worse; `num_stages` is a no-op on this kernel.

#### Correction test
pytest - `840 passed, 420 skipped, 109 warnings in 8.82s`

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#pull-requests.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [GFX12] Gluon BF16 GEMM config
[HIP] perf(biased_grouped_topk): batch router loads, cheapen the argmax, drop the sig_scores LDS cache
body:
## Motivation

`grouped_topk_kernel` runs once per MoE layer, so it sits on the critical path of every decode step. On the wide ungrouped routers it spends most of its time waiting rather than computing, and profiling on MI355X shows the waits are latency, not bandwidth: the memory system is never close to saturated. This PR addresses three sources of that latency and gives 1.21x on Kimi-K2.5 (E=384) and 1.23x on Kimi-K3 (E=896), geomean over token counts 1 to 163840 on MI355X.

## Technical Details

**1. Stride the kernel's loops by a `WARP_SIZE` constant instead of `blockDim.x`.** The build passes `-fno-offload-uniform-block`, so the compiler must assume a partial workgroup and turns every `blockDim.x` use into a kernarg load, a compare and a select behind a `vmcnt` wait. It stays a named constant inside the kernel rather than a template parameter, because `WARP_SIZE` constant-evaluates to 64 on the host and would silently bake in 64 on a wave32 target.

**2. Batch the prologue's global loads.** Load and consume are split into two unrolled phases, so a lane's loads issue behind two `vmcnt` waits instead of one per vector. The slot count is templated and dispatched on how many vectors a lane owns (four cases), not on the expert count, so it covers every expert count without a per-model dispatch list and without reserving registers for slots that are dynamically dead.

**3. Replace the key/value `wave_reduce` argmax with a DPP max plus a ballot.** `SQ_INSTS_VALU` per wave at E=896 falls 2,107 to 1,807, a 14% reduction. **This also fixes a bug.** Folding the key/value pair through `wave_reduce` leaves `max_idx` non-uniform across lanes on a tie, so the `scores[max_idx] = -INFINITY` clear that follows is not well defined: each tied lane blanks a different expert while only one of them is recorded. The ballot form resolves ties with `ctz` and broadcasts a single winner, so the clear is always keyed on the expert that was actually selected. The helper moves into `hip_reduce.h` as `multithread_argmax_lane_dpp` and `wave_argmax_dpp`, subsuming three near-identical copies: `warpReduceMax` here, plus `warpReduceMax_softplus` and `subwarpArgmaxLane` in `topk_gating_kernels.cuh`. The two `topk_gating` call sites are a like-for-like substitution of an already-identical implementation, so nothing there changes behaviour.

**4. Drop the `sig_scores` LDS cache, partially reverting #3466.** That PR bundled an `exp2f`/`rcpf` sigmoid with an LDS cache of the pre-bias sigmoid (`sig_scores`) that replaced the dependent `correction_bias[max_idx]` load in the selection loop. The sigmoid is kept as-is; the cache is removed and the selection loop goes back to `max_val -= correction_bias[max_idx]`. The cache is a shape-dependent trade rather than a win: it costs a second `num_experts` float array, 7,172 B against 3,588 B at E=896, which puts the kernel at 22 waves/CU against the 32-wave cap. Dropping it restores 32 waves/CU, worth more than the `topk` extra vector-memory instructions it reintroduces. Break-even is near E=640; below it the cache is marginally better (E=384 is 1.215x with it against 1.207x without), so it is dropped unconditionally rather than gated behind another template parameter for 0.7%. `correction_bias` is token-invariant, so the restored load should hit in cache. `grouped_topk_opt_sort_kernel`'s dead LDS bias slot goes with it, since the sizing no longer allocates for it. #3466's own configuration is not at risk: it reported 1.225x for its pair at E=384 / topk=8 / group=1, and this build is 1.21x against a baseline that already carries the sigmoid change, so the two are additive.

## Evaluated and not adopted: routing the ungrouped shapes to topk_gating

Since these routers are ungrouped (`num_expert_group == 1`), an obvious alternative is to dispatch them to the `topk_gating` kernels rather than improve `grouped_topk_kernel`. That was implemented and measured, and it is slower: 0.799x at E=384, 0.677x at E=512, 0.661x at E=640 and 0.856x at E=896 against the build in this PR. It is therefore not adopted, and the ungrouped shapes stay on `grouped_topk_kernel`.

## Test Plan

Test environment:

* GPU: **AMD Instinct MI355X** (gfx950)
* ROCm: 7.14.0 (HIP 7.14.60850), torch 2.13.0+rocm7.14.0

Benchmarked with `op_tests/test_moeTopkSoftmax.py -i 500 -w 50`, otherwise default arguments, so the token list is the test's own 1 to 163840. This PR touches no Python, so the test file is identical on both sides and only `csrc/kernels/topk_softmax_kernels_group.cu` differs, recompiled per side and relinked against the same prebuilt objects with flags taken from the JIT's own build. Both sides ran on one pinned, idle MI355X.

Three of the test's tables are affected:

| table | shape | changes reached |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `moeTopkSoftmax_biased_grouped_topk_kimi_k25` | E=384 g=1 topk=8 renorm scale=2.827 | all three |
| `moeTopkSoftmax_biased_grouped_topk_kimi_k3_strided` | E=896 g=1 topk=16, row-strided logits | all three |
| `moeTopkSoftmax_grouped_topk` | DeepSeek-R1 non-biased, E=256 g=8 topk=8 topk_group=4 | stride and DPP argmax only |

The DeepSeek-R1 biased shape is out of scope: it satisfies `use_opt_sort` and runs `grouped_topk_opt_sort_kernel`, which this PR only strips a dead LDS slot from.

## Test Result

| shape | geomean | decode (token <= 256) | prefill (token >= 1024) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Kimi-K2.5 biased, E=384 | **1.210x** | 1.181x | 1.252x |
| Kimi-K3 biased, E=896 strided | **1.229x** | 1.190x | 1.286x |
| DeepSeek-R1 non-biased, E=256 g=8, softmax | 1.201x | 1.160x | 1.261x |
| DeepSeek-R1 non-biased, E=256 g=8, sigmoid | 1.217x | 1.171x | 1.279x |

### Biased grouped topk, Kimi-K2.5 and Kimi-K3

| token | K2.5 base_us | K2.5 opt_us | K2.5 speedup | K3 base_us | K3 opt_us | K3 speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

title: [Triton] gfx942: fix head_size>=512 decode KV over-segmentation at low/mid batch
body:
## Purpose
Fixes #5673. On gfx942 (MI325), `select_3d_config` over-segments the `head_size>=512` decode KV split at low/mid batch: it applies the occupancy multiplier to `target_num_prgms` and clamps to `MAX_SEGMENTS=128`, so batch 1 saturates at 128 and batch 16 lands at 64 — ~2× the measured optimum, adding reduction overhead and shrinking per-segment work.

## Change (gfx942, head_size>=512 only)
- Skip the `occ` multiplier on `target_num_prgms`.
- Cap `MAX_SEGMENTS` at 64.

Result: `NUM_SEGMENTS_PER_SEQ` lands at **64 / 32 / 16** for batch **1 / 16 / 64** — the measured optima — instead of 128 / 64 / 16.

## Test Result (head_size 512, GQA 32/4, fp8 KV, MI325)
`bench_unified_attention.py -decode -fp8_kv --metric bandwidth -test`. **This PR alone, measured against unmodified `main` (no other changes applied):**

| ctx | batch | before | after | Δ |
|----:|------:|-------:|------:|---|
| 8192  | 1  | 394 GB/s  | 668  | **1.70×** |
| 8192  | 16 | 1479      | 1707 | 1.15× |
| 8192  | 64 | 1914      | 1911 | ~1× |
| 32768 | 1  | 1001      | 1251 | **1.25×** |

All shapes pass `-test` (`max_diff` ≤ 0.0005); output is unchanged (segmentation only reorders the reduction).

## Notes
Self-contained — one commit off a fixed base, **not** stacked on any other PR. Combines with the companion gfx942 decode `waves_per_eu=1` override (separate PR) for a larger low-batch gain, but the numbers above are this change in isolation. gfx942-scoped; other archs untouched. Based on the commit our workspace pins; **needs porting + re-validation onto current `main`** (which refactored `unified_attention.py`). AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; a human will review and re-validate.
